חזון The vision of. The נ is not radical.

The son of Amotz. There exists an opinion, though a solitary one, that when the father of a prophet is mentioned by name, he also was a prophet; another opinion is, that Yeshayahu was a member of the royal family, that his father Amotz and Amatzyahu were brothers, and that the evil-disposed of Yisrael were unable on that account to do harm to Yeshayahu, as they did to Yirmiyahu (vid. Yirmiyahu 38); but in fact Yeshayahu did not escape persecution, for he says, I gave my back to smiters, etc. (1. 6). Irrespectively of all traditional explanations, we may say that the father of a prophet, if mentioned by name, was a man of some distinction, whose character rendered him conspicuous among his fellow-men; sometimes he was himself a prophet, at others not, e.g., David, the son of Yishai (Shmuel II 23:1). David was the man of Elokim (Divrei Hayamim II 8:14), Yishai was not. It is with prophecy as with royalty; comp. Yehu, king of Yisrael, the son of Nimshi (Melachim I 19:16); Nimshi was not a king. We read, it is true, In the vision of Yeshayahu, the son of Amotz, the prophet (Divrei Hayamim II 32:32), where the qualifying term, the prophet, may as well be referred to Amotz as to Yeshayahu; but from the words, To Yeshayahu the prophet, the son of Amotz (Melachim II 19:2), we learn that Yeshayahu was the prophet. Thus the forefathers of Zephania are named (Tzefanyah 1:1), because the king Chizkiyahu was one of them.

Concerning Yehudah and Yerushalayim. The greater part of Yeshayahu’s prophecies refer to the cities of Yehudah, which were to be taken by the king of Ashur, and to Yerushalayim, which was to be delivered out of his hand; the whole of the second part of the Book of Yeshayahu has as its subject the exile of Yehudah, the other tribes not being mentioned here at all.

In the days of Uziyahu, Yotam, Achaz, and Chizkiyahu, kings of Yehudah. Yeshayahu very probably commenced his prophetical career in the last year of King Uziyahu, as shall be explained below (6:1). In strict regard to the words of the text, we think that he died in the days of Chizkiyahu; for had he lived in the days of Manasse, the son of Chizkiyahu, it would certainly have been stated in this verse. Some say that Yeshayahu was slain by Manasse, because he exclaimed, Mine eyes have seen the King, Hashem of hosts (6:5). If this statement is based on tradition, it may be accepted.

והאזיני And give ear. Sometimes verbs are derived from nouns, as האזיני, ‘give ear,’ from אׂזֶן ‘ ear.’ .There is in reality no difference between שמע ‘to hear’ and האזן ‘to give ear.’—Yeshayahu begins his prophecy, by addressing those witnesses, that have been pointed out to Yisrael by Moshe, when he said I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that you shall soon utterly perish (Devarim 4:26); the time, foretold by Moshe, had then come.
For Hashem speaketh. Listen to His word, since it is Hashem that speaketh ; or, because Hashem has commanded you to listen.

I have nourished and brought up children. Bnei Yisrael are compared to feeble children, who, nevertheless, through the care of their father are enabled to distinguish themselves amongst their companions.
פשעו בי They have rebelled against me. They withdrew from my command (comp. Melachim II 8:22; Shemot 22:8).
The ox knoweth, etc. Ox and ass are mentioned, as animals which are in constant use among people.

אבוס the crib. The place for the ass’s food. The form of the word is in the construct state the same as in the absolute. The participle passive Kal, 1) אבוסים Kings 5:3) and אבוס (Mishlei 15:17), ‘fatted,’ is derived from this word ; it means literally, ‘placed at the crib.’
Yisrael doth not know. They are, therefore, in their character inferior to the cattle.

My people doth not consider. Repetition of the preceding idea, as usual in most of the prophecies, in the song of Moshe (Devarim 32), in the parables of Bilam (Bamidbar 23., 24i> My people doth not consider. Repetition of the preceding idea, as usual in most of the prophecies, in the song of Moshe (Deut. xxxii.), in the parables of Bilam (Num. xxiii., xxiv.), etc. The meaning of the whole verse is, I have brought them up, but they do not know me.

הוי. Some consider the ה as a substitute for א, and explain אוי ═ הוי, ‘woe;’ comp. אדורם and הדורם, N. pr. (Divrei Hayamim II 10:18; Melachim I 12:18); איך and היך, how (Divrei Hayamim I 13:12 ; Shmuel II 6:9); but I think that it is a sign of the vocative case (derived from the verb היה ‘to be’), and that the passage must be rendered, O sinful people, etc. ; comp. הוי הוי ונסו, Ho, ho, flee (Zach. 2:10), הוי ציון המלטי O Tziyon, deliver thyself (Ibid. 11). The second person is, therefore, used in the next verse, Why should ye be stricken any more.
כֶבֶד Laden with. An adjective in the construct state; comp. עֶרֶל לב ועֶרֶל בשר, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh (Ez. 44:9).
Seed of evil doers. They and their forefathers have been wicked ; or, their father was an Emori, their mother a Chiti (Ez. 16:3), as I shall explain.
משחיתים Corrupters. That corrupt their soul or their way.
They have forsaken Hashem, that is, the service of Hashem.
נאצו They have provoked unto anger.

נזורו. They are gone away. Root נזר ‘to separate’ ; comp. וינזרו that they separate themselves (Vayikra 22:2). נָזוֹרוּ is formed like יָבׂלוּ ‘ they could ’ (Shemot 8:14). Many take it as Niphal of זור ‘ to separate ’; comp. נָכוֹנוּ ‘ they are prepared ’ (Mishlei 19:29); Niphal of כּוּן, ‘ to stand.

תֻּבּוּ. Should ye be stricken. The ת in תֻּבּוּ, they sat down. (Deuter. 33:3), is part of the root—תֻּבּוּ being Pual of תכה ; comp. וְשֻׁפּוּ and they stick out (Iyov 33:21)—but here it is the prefix representing the second person; תֻּבּוּ being Hophal of נכה.—You will revolt more and more. The more you are smitten, the more you revolt, while the proper way for you would be to repent; comp., And in the time of his—Achaz, king of Yehudah’s—distress did he trespass yet more against the Lord. (Divrei Hayamim II 28:22.)
סָרָה Rebellious. Adjective; root סרר, ‘to be rebellious,’ comp. סורר, ‘rebellious’ (Deuter. 21:18); supply מלה or דברה ‘ word;’ סרה may also be taken as a substantive, ‘ rebellion.’
The whole head is sick. Whereupon shall ye be stricken? for the whole head is afflicted already with all kinds of sickness, etc. The head and heart are mentioned as the principal parts of the body.
דַּוָּי Faint. Adjective; a form like נַּנָּב ‘ thievish,’ סַלָּח ‘ placable.

מְתוֹם A place containing soundness (תּוֹם ‘ soundness or integrity’). The form of the word is irregular, for it should be מָתוֹם like מָעוֹז (25:4). The same form is used Tehillim 38:4. R. Moshe Hakkohen says that מְתוֹם is the same as מְתִים ‘ people ;’ he quotes a parallel, Shoftim 20:48, and explains our verse, there is nothing in them that is good for man; but this explanation is rather far-fetched.

פצע Wounds. Supply the word רק ‘only,’ ‘but,’ before פצע. There is no soundness in him ; there are but wounds and bruises ; comp. שיאכל ושתה אין טוב באדם There is nothing good for man but that he should eat and drink. (Kohelet 2:24).
פצע A wound caused by the breaking of the bone.
חבורת A sore attended with suppuration. >
טריה Fresh, not yet dry (comp. Shoftim 15:15); in Arabic the word طرا has the same meaning. ..
זׂרוּ They have been squeezed. Root זׁרד ‘ to squeeze ’ (comp. Shoftim 6:38). The wound cannot be healed unless the matter is removed from it.
חבשו They have been bound up. Root חבש ‘ to compress,’ ‘to bind up ’ (comp. חובש ‘ruler,’ 3:7).
בַּשָּׁמֶן With the oil. With the oil, which the cure of the wound requires.

Your country, etc. What has been said hitherto in figurative expressions is now repeated in plain language. All their land has been smitten, a part of it is desolate, without inhabitants, a part destroyed by fire, another part robbed of its produce by strangers.
אכלים אתה Devour it. Devour its produce; comp. בעצבון תאכלנה In sorrow shalt thou eat of it. (Bereshit 3:17.)

ושממה And desolate. Supply ארצכם ‘ your country ’—and your country is desolate. זרים can be derived from זרם ‘ tempest ’ (32:2); the final מ would then be not a sign of the plural, but one of the radical letters; if so, if this derivation be correct, the two words זרים of this verse are two different grammatical forms.
And the daughter of Tziyon is left, etc. The fortified cities of Yehudah will be taken and only Tziyon will be left.
סוכה The hut. The place for the watchman ; that is, the temple built in honour of the Almighty.
מלונה A lodge, where the watchman stays through the night. במקשה In the garden of cucumbers.
נצורה Ruined (comp. 65:4)
Except the Lord of hosts, etc. These are the words of Bnei Yisrael, whom the prophet introduces now speaking.
כמעָט֑ Very small. Join with שׂריד ‘remnant,’ because of its disjunctive accent; for it is an important rule, that the most careful notice should be taken of the accents.

Hear the word of the Lord, etc. The prophet replies to their complaint, We are like Sedom, by saying, If you were so, it would be but just, for your princes are like the princes of Sedom,—this is meant by the address, Ye rulers of Sedom—and the people is like the people of Amorah.

To what purpose, etc. Why should I leave you longer in the land ? Is it for the sake of the multitude of your burnt offerings ? I am full, etc. An anthropomorphism ; in reality, He does not want anything; comp. If I were hungry, I would not tell thee, etc. (Tehillim 1. 12 ff).
אילים Large sheep.
מריאים A species of cattle, akin to the ox, but larger; its fat is prohibited. The Gaon compares מריאים fed beasts with מרא to feed (Mishnah Sabbath 24:3).
כבשים The young of the flock.
עתודים The old of the flock (comp. Bereshit 31:10)
לפני═פני Before me; it is not the object of לֵרָאוֹח ‘ to be seen.’
רמוס To tread. Infinitive.
לא תוסיפו Ye shall not continue. A prohibition (comp. Devarim 4:2); not a mere future.
להביא═הביא To bring. Vain oblations, etc. For your oblation is vain in mine eyes, and your incense an abomination.
ראש חדש═חדש Day of the new moon. In the Pentateuch it is clearly stated that the word bears this meaning, New-moon.

קרא מקרא That you proclaim them to be holy convocations. Yeshayahu mentions these festivals, together with the burnt offerings and oblations, because of the additional offering (מוסף) brought on such days.
לא אוכל I cannot bear. Supply the word נְשאׁ, ‘to bear.’ Comp. חמור לחם an ass laden with bread (Shmuel I 16:20).

עצרה Restraint. Comp. עׂצֶר ‘prison’ (53:8). Restraint from doing any work. עצרת (Vayikra 23:36) has the same meaning. Iniquity and restraint. God cannot bear iniquity coupled with the observance of holy days; for of what use is it to keep holy days and to do evil at the same time.
They are a trouble unto me. These words imply the threat, I shall therefore banish you, and they—the festivals—will then cease.
I am weary. A figurative expression.
ובפרשכם And when ye spread forth. The Hirik under ר is instead of Segol.
I will hide mine eyes from you. I will keep away mercy from you.
I will not hear. These words contain the same idea, I will not help you.
Your hands are full of blood. Because your hands, etc. Blood. Bloodshed.
Wash. Wash your hands of the blood they have shed.
הִתְזַכּוּ═הִזַּכּוּ Make you clean. It is Hithpael; the ת is absorbed in the ז; comp. לַמִּהְטַהֵר═לַמִּטַּהֵר unto him that purifies himself (Vayikra 14:4)
להיטב═היטב To do well. It is infinitive.
אשרו Straighten. Root א ; ישר replaces the radical י ; the reverse is the case in תתאמרו═תִּתְיַמָּרוּ you shall boast yourselves(61:6).

חמוץ Cruel. An adjective, like קרוב ‘ near ;’ comp. חומץ ‘ cruel ’ (Tehillim 71:4). Many explain אשרו חמוץ Give due consideration to the cause, do not judge off hand ; the meaning of אשרו would then be, Praise ye (comp. Bereshit 30:13).

ונוכחה. Some say that Hashem is now speaking ; Let us—Hashem and Yisrael—reason together (comp. Michah 6:2); but I think the words may well be assigned to the prophet; as if he said Hashem told me that we—you, Yisrael, and I—should submit to His rebuke ; for the prophet himself was not entirely without blame, as he reports, And He reproved me, that I should not walk, etc. (8:11), as I shall explain below (6:5).

שנים Scarlet (comp. Shemot 25:4). The idea contained in this verse is the reverse of that conveyed by the words of Yirmiyahu, Though thou wash thee with nitre, and take thee much soap, yet thine iniquity is marked before me (Jerem. 2:22); namely, the iniquity will depart, and you will again be free from all sin. The same is expressed by the words Wash you, etc. (ver. 16).
Though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool. A repetition of the same idea.
If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land. Otherwise, the strangers before-mentioned (ver. 7) will consume it.

You shall be devoured with the sword. That is to say, If you be obedient you shall eat the good, and if you rebel you shall be devoured with the sword. Supply before חֶרֶב ‘ the sword,’ either the verbal noun אֲכִילַת. ‘ a devouring of,’ or the preposition ב ‘ with ’ ; comp. בבית ═ בית ‘ in the house ’ (Melachim II 18:15).
For the mouth of Hashem hath spoken it. Be sure that this prediction will be fulfilled, for the mouth, etc.
The prophet has thus reproved the people but they do not listen.
How is the faithful city become an harlot. Yerushalayim is like a woman that has become faithless to her husband, after having been a faithful wife.
מלאתי Full of. The י is paragogic as in גנבתי the theft of (Bereshit 31:39.)
ילין Was lodging. The future is here used for the imperfect, which has no special form in Hebrew.
מרצחים Murderers. Literally, they that cause to murder. It is participle Piel, and has a causative meaning, referring to the judges.
Thy silver. Metaphor for judges and princes ; this verse is, therefore, followed by, Thy princes are rebellious. Thy silver is become dross. The best of the people are like dross.
מהול Mixed. The ה is one of the radical letters. Hapax legomenon.
שלמנים Rewards. (Comp. Shemot 22:5). They perverted judgment; the judge said, Give me such and such a sum, and it shall stand thee in good part in thy lawsuit with thy neighbour.
To the orphan—of whom they are not afraid. They judge not. That is, they do not render justice.
The cause of the widow—which she has to bring forward. Doth not come unto them: they do not like to hear her cause, therefore it does not come before them.
נאום The word of. A noun (comp. Yirmiyahu 23:31). To use נֻם instead of נאום is a blunder, for א cannot be omitted.
The Lord. This is added because the judges appear as the lords of the earth.

Hashem of hosts. He is truly Hashem, and the hosts of the universe are His witnesses. Why the name of Hashem is joined, in the construct state, to צבאות, though being a proper noun, is explained in the Book of Shmuel.

The mighty One of Yisrael, and Hashem of hosts compose a parallelism, in which Yisrael on earth beneath corresponds to the hosts of heaven above, for Bnei Yisrael are likewise called the hosts of Hashem (comp. Shemot 12:41).
אוי ═ חוי Woe. Woe unto them when I shall do the following thing.
I will ease me of mine adversaries. I will find comfort for their having provoked me. An anthropomorphism.
ידי My hand; that is, my smiting (comp. Shemot 9:3).
כבור As if it were with soap ; ═ בור בורית ‘ soap ’; or more correctly, purely (comp. Tehillim 18:25).
Thy dross. This expression reverts to the former metaphor, thy silver is become dross.
בדיליך Thy tin. R. Moshe Hakkohen remarks, that the names of the seven kinds of metal are not found in the Bible in the plural ; he forgets בדיליך, which is plural; the singular would be בדילֵך .

And I will restore thy judges, etc. When the kingdom of Yisrael, the ten tribes, with their judges, shall cease here, and the judges of Achaz shall likewise have gone, Chizkiyahu will appoint upright judges ; and this is in fact recorded of him.
As at first. As in the days of David and Shlomo. The ב in כבראשנה is not essential.
Tziyon shall be redeemed, etc. Tziyon will, in consequence of her justice, be redeemed out of the hand of Sancheriv.
And her returning people. The people that will repent. Supply יפדו will be redeemed.

פושעים Transgressors. They that rebel against authority. They are worse than חטאים sinners. And the destruction of the transgressors shall be together. All the fortified towns of Yehudah shall be captured.
And they that forsake Hashem, etc. The ordinary repetition of the same idea.

אילים Terebinths. The singular is אלה ; it has a masculine termination in the plural like נָשִׁים of אִשָּׁח woman, and סאים of סאה measure (Bereshit 18:6); comp. The gardens, which, in the corresponding phrase, balances terebinths.

יבשו They shall be ashamed. Some say that the י is here used instead of ת, the third instead of the second person, and explain many other instances in the same way; but I think that the third person of יכלו they shall be consumed of the preceding verse, is continued in יבשל, and in חמדתם ye have desired, passes over to the second person; there are many instances like it.
ותחפרו And ye shall be confounded
For he shall be as an oak tree, etc. After having said that they shall be ashamed of the oak trees they have coveted and stolen, the prophet compares them to an oak tree whose leaves have withered.

נובלת עליה Whose leaf fadeth. Literally, which is withering with regard to its leaves; comp. ותאבדו דרך, And you shall perish with regard to the way (Tehillim 2:12); similarly we say in the Confession, (קשינו ערף (ודוי We are stiff with regard to our neck. כאלה As an oak. This proves that מאי לים(ver. 29) is the plural of אלה oak, especially since this is likewise followed by and as a garden, etc.
החסון. The strong. Adjective; the substantive is חוסן strength.
נעורת Tow. That which is shaken off (נער to shake) from the flax.

לניצוץ As a spark (comp. Ez. 1:7). This verse refers to the idols, which are made strong, that they should not shake, but which those who formed them will burn in time of trouble, because they helped not; but the workmen themselves will likewise be burnt; ..
this is meant by and they will both burn. (Comp. Shemot 3:3.)
And none shall quench. And none shall help.
This chapter commences a new prophecy, but not without connection with the preceding. Tziyon will now be saved from the hands of Sancheriv, and she will besides be highly distinguished in the future.

This will take place, as the prophet says, In the last of the days. That is, in the days of Messiah, which are the last of the days of the world. Those days have not yet come; for since the days of Yeshayahu there has never been a period free from war. We learn from Josephus, and the literature of the Paras and Madai, that during the whole time of the second temple in Yerushalayim war had never ceased. Moreover, the prophet distinctly declares, Neither shall they learn war any more.

And shall be exalted. We know that the mount of the temple will not be physically raised; but what the phrase means is, that it will be established in such a way that people will hasten up to it from the four comers of the earth, as if it were higher than all hills.
ונהרו And they will flow. Root, נהר ‘to flow’; comp. נהר river, which is so called on account of its flowing motion.
And he shall judge. He, who is the judge, the Messiah, shall judge (comp. Numb. 26:59).

לְאִתִּים Into plowshares. Comp. אֵתוֹ his plowshare (Shmuel I 13:20); the Dagesh of the ת compensates for the omitted silent letter י; the same purpose is served by the long vowel Zere under א in the word .אֵתוֹ
למזמרות Pruning-hooks. Instruments for pruning the vineyards.

O house of Yaakov, etc. With these words the prophet rebukes Yisrael, as if he said, Since Tziyon will now, as you are well aware, be redeemed for her justice, and a time, besides, will come for her great salvation, we all owe obedience to the words of the prophecies, which are true as the light. The prophet includes himself in this rebuke, by using the first person plural, pro formd, as Moshe did when he prayed, forgive our iniquity; or because he grew up among the people and acquired something of their mode of speaking, as I shall explain (6:5)

Thou hast forsaken, etc. Some refer the second person to Hashem, and say that the prophet confesses here before Him that He has justly forsaken them, for they are full of Eastern customs, etc. R. Moshe Hakkohen refers it to Yisrael, and explains accordingly : Thou, O Yisrael, hast forgotten thy people and its religion.

מלאו According to some, they are enthusiastic; comp. מלא with enthusiasm (Yirmiyahu 12:6); I think that it means, they are full, namely, with the wisdom of the children of the East, the Aramæans ; comp. Aram in the east, and the Plishtim in the west (9:11); the next is, therefore, And are soothsayers like the Plishtim. בית יעקב in this verse must then be vocative, like the first (5:5).

ובילדי And with ideas of. And with what they bring forth by thought; for the resultant of any two forces is called נולד ‘ born, product.’ ישפיקו They satisfy themselves. Comp. יִשְׂפׂק ‘it shall suffice’ (Melachim I 20:10), although of a different conjugation; the latter being Kal, the former Hiphil. They are satisfied with secular knowledge, and do not seek for the prophecy, which is the best light.
Full of silver and gold. Silver is mentioned before gold, because it is in quantity more abundant.
קצה End. ה is paragogic, like ה in לילה night; the accent is therefore on the penultima.
In the preceding verse Yisrael is described as wise, in this as rich and mighty; in the same order Yirmiyahu enumerates these qualities (Yirmiyahu 9:23)
אלילים Idols. Root אַל "not"; the idols are called by this name, because there is no reality in them.

They worship the work of his hands, that which his fingers have made. They—all the people—worship the work of his—the smith’s—hands, that which his—the smith’s—fingers have made. ידיו "his hands", and ישתחוו "they worship" ; the Version evades the difficulty by translating ידיו "their hands".
וישה And boweth down. Niphal of שחח; comp. וימס ‘And it was melted’ (Jos. 7:5) Niphal of מסס. Their acts degraded them.

ואל תשא להם According to some—the ת being the sign for the second person, and referring to Hashem—and thou forgive them not. I am, however, of opinion that the passage has the following meaning: Not one of them dares to lift up his head or soul, because the context requires a phrase similar to And the man humbles himself ; or that the word ארץ ‘ the earth ’ is to be supplied: And the earth is not able to bear them (comp. Bereshit 13:6). The Grammarian, who asserts that אַל is only found with a command, is mistaken; comp. אל־מות, where there is no death (Mishlei 12:28)
בא Infinitive: ‘ to enter ’ (comp. Chavakuk 2:3); or imperative : enter ; the advice which they will give each other.
הטמן The same; infinitive or imperative. It is the Niphal of טמן

עיני The looks of. עין ‘eye,’ or ‘ look,’ though generally feminine, is sometimes masculine (as e.g. in this verse, since the masculine form שָׁפֵל is joined to עֵינֵי) ; and עֵינֵי ‘ the looks,’ is identical with כל אחד מעיני ‘ each of the looks’; comp. בנות ‘ each of the branches ’ (Bereshit 49:22).
Haughtiness. The contrary, lowliness, is meant; comp. He will enlighten my darkness (Tehillim 18:29)
ושפל He shall be brought low. The ו changes the past into a future; comp. וטהר he shall be clean (Vayikra 22:7)
The cedars, etc. All this may be taken either literally, or symbolically for the young, great, rich, mighty, and the kings.
ההרים The mountains. I derive הרים from הרה to conceive, as I shall explain in the Book of Tehillim (148:9).
The tower. The tower on the royal palace.
Ships of Tarshish. If taken figuratively, they signify the merchants; literally, they are ships which belong to Bnei Yisrael, and are going to Tarshish.
שכיות Pictures. Comp. אבן משנית A stone with a picture (Vayikra 26:1)
And the loftiness, etc. This idea is repeated here, because all the objects previously enumerated, excite pride in those that possess them, and cause dejection to those that lose them.
יחלוף He shall abolish. Comp. בני חלוף the afflicted (Mishlei 31:5), to whom death is imminent; this root has a similar meaning in חלף it is over (Shir Hashirim 2:11).
כליל. This word remains the same in the masculine and feminine, singular and plural; it means all (comp. Shemot 28:31; Vayikra 6:16).
He shall abolish. The third person refers to Hashem.
עשו They made. The subject is not named; it is the indefinite one or they; comp. ויאמר ליוסף and he (═ some one) said to Yosef (Bereshit 48:1). עשוהו one has done it (Kohelet 2:12).

חפר פרות. I think the singular is חפרפרת, and signifies a bird that flies out in the night like the bat, and keeps itself hidden during the day ; others say that חפרפרת means a bird which eats up the fruits during the night; in this case it consists of two separate words.
נקרת The clefts of. Literally a hollowed place of.
סעפי. Branchlike pieces projecting from the rocks, where people can hide themselves.

לערוץ To be mighty. Root ערץ ; comp. עריץ mighty. According to others, it is a transitive verb, meaning to terrify; אל תערץ (Jos. 1:9) has, perhaps, the same meaning, the word לבך thine heart, being supplied—do not terrify or discourage thine heart—and עריץ (29:20), is then a transitive adjective, terrible, like אימים (Bereshit 14:5), the terrifying ones.

Cease ye, etc. Since Hashem has issued His decrees against you, as indicated in the words ‘ Because of the fear of Hashem,’ etc. (ver. 10), no man has the power to undo them; cease, therefore, to rely on man, he will not help you, for he is vanity.

This Chapter is either the explanation of the latter part of Chapter II., beginning the cedars, the mountains, etc. (2:13, ff.) or the continuation of the subject, commencing Cease, ye from man, etc. (2:22); I adopt this latter view.
משען ומשענה. The stay and the staff. Poetically said for every kind of staff. The explanation of the figure follows immediately, The whole stay of bread and water.
The mighty man. He who has the strength required for a successful war.
The man of war. He who has the experience.
The judge, who is asked to show the right way according to the law. The prophet, who serves the same purpose; and also the astrologer, who foretells future events through the science of astrology.
The ancient, who has profited by the changes and trials of life.
חכם חרשים The cunning artificer.
נבון לחש The charmer. Even he that understands to charm the serpents, will be taken away. According to some, the eloquent orator; comp. מתלחשים whispering (Shmuel II 12:19).
תעלולים Babes. The ת is not a radical letter; root עול to be young. Comp. עולל child (Yirmiyahu 6:11). העלולים is here an adjective, they that are young,
וְנִנַּשׂ And shall be oppressed. Niphal; like נִצָּב (3:13), he is standing up. According to some, and shall oppress; the נ being radical, and נִנַּשׁ piel.
ירהבו They will have power or dominion ; comp. רהב power (51:9)
The house of his father. His family.
לכה To thee. It is the same as לך though having an additional שמלה לכה .ה thy clothing be to thee. We do not ask thee to give us clothing.
This ruin. Yerushalayim (comp. 5:8.).—This is just the style in which people speak while labouring under strong excitement.
יִשא He will swear (comp. לא תשא את שם יי thou shalt not swear by the name of Hashem, Shemot 20:7).
חובש Ruler. It is the same verb as in הובש מכה ‘ dressing a wound ;’ comp. עֶצֶר power (Shoftim 18:7).
There is no clothing. Even for myself.
כי לשונם ומעלליהם אל ה׳ For their tongue and their doings with regard to Hashem.
למרות To provoke. ל has Pathah, because of the omission of ה, the characteristic of the Hiphil; להמרות ═ למרות comp. להנחותם ═ לנחותם to lead them (Shemot 13:21).
The eyes of His glory. Publicly.

הכרת. According to some, the cutting off, derived from כרת to cut off, but more correctly, the knowing of; comp. הכירהו they knew him (Bereshit 42:8); the Dagesh in כ indicates the omission of the radical נ which appears in ינכר He is known (Mishlei 26:24). He who is able to judge of the constitution of the whole body from the face will find in it the declaration and confession of the truth; no further evidence is wanted.
And they tell their sin like Sedom. They do not even conceal their sins; for he who does conceal them feels at least ashamed of what he has done.
אמרו According to some, Praise ye (comp. Dent. 26:17); I prefer Say ye, from אמר to say—in the heart or with the mouth.

Shall they eat. They, that is, all the righteous (for these words have to be supplied); as if to say, Do not think that only one righteous man shall enjoy the fruit of his actions. This verse is closely connected with the preceding.
רע. Bad. According to some it is in apposition to אוי woe. Woe, evil, etc. I take it rather as an attribute to רשע woe to the hardened sinner.
נגשיו מעולל Every one of his rulers is playful. The מ in מעולל is not essential; מעולל is an adjective, and not a participle.
מישריך ═ מאשריך They that lead thee. א in מאשריך is instead of י, for the letters א ה ו י interchange; comp. 1:17.—They that ought to guide you mislead you.
בלעו They have destroyed. (Literally, they have swallowed up.) They have destroyed the way to such an extent that it is no more to be recognised.

Hashem standeth up. Therefore Hashem standeth up. לריב To plead. It is not the noun, ריב the strife, with the preposition ל, but infinitive Hiphil; the same is to be said concerning. לדין To judge.—This verse refers to the punishments to be decreed by Him.
עמים People. A great many; comp Devarim 32:19
Ye have eaten up, etc. How can you be the judges of my people, when you yourselves, etc. בערתם You have eaten up. Comp. Shemot 22:4. The vineyard. That is, Yisrael.
מלכם What mean you ? Dagesh in ל compensates for the omitted מה לכם ═ מלכם .ה is compounded, of two words, like (מה זה ═)מזה What is that (Shemot 4:3).
Ye grind. Metaphorically said, for you put to shame and contempt.
ומשקרות And wantonly looking about. In Rabbinical literature a woman of this class is called סקרנית (Bereshith Rabba, 100:19).

וטפוף According to some, Speaking; comp. והטף And prophesy (Ez. 21:2); but the grammatical principles of the Hebrew language will not admit of this explanation ; according to others, Mincing—comp. אטיף, the Chaldæan translation of הציף He made overflow (Devarim 11:8)—‘ moving slowly, like one that swims upon the surface of the water.’ Others, again, derive it from טף Little ones (Est. 3:16), and I incline to this opinion ; walking slowly like a child.
תעכסנה They put spurs. They wear spurs on their feet, like riding-men; according to some, they make a tinkling with their spurs.
ושפח And he will smite with a scab. It has the same root as מספחת scab (Vayikra 13:6), although written with שׂ; comp. בסורי ═ בשׂורי when I turn away (Hoshea 9:12).

פתהן Some supply א, so that פאתהן ═ פתהן the locks of their head ; but I compare it rather with הפותות the hinges (Melachim I 7:50), that is, the back of the doors, and find in this verse the description of the plagues of the whole body, from the head to the foot.
עכסים Ornaments for the foot.
שביסים Hapax legomenon; according to some, an ornament for the legs.
שהרנים A moonlike ornament of the girdle, derived from the Chaldæan סהרא moon; סהר (Shir Hashirim 7:2) is generally explained in the same way.
נטיפות Hap. leg. According to some, an ornament for the hair.
שרות An ornament for the ears; according to others, bracelets; comp. שרין the Kasdi translation of אצעדה bracelets (Bamidbar 31:50).
רעלות Hap. leg. An ornament for the cheeks.
פארים comp. תפארת ornament; for the hands.
צעדות An ornament for the arms; comp. אצעדה bracelet (which Shaul wore on his arm, Shmuel II 1:10). א of אצעדה is pleonastic, as the א in אזרוע (Yirmiyahu 32:21).
קשרים A well-known ornament for the neck.
בתי הנפש An ornament for the breast; the breast is called נפש soul, because it is the seat of the soul, it contains the heart.
לחשים Amulets. Inscriptions on gold and silver, for a charm.
טבעות Rings, for the fingers.
נזמי האף Nose jewels; I have already described them (Bereshit 24:22)
מחלצות Changeable suits of garments, worn over the dress; comp. חלצתו his armour (Shmuel II 2:21), which is worn over the garments.
מעטפות Mantles. A dress wherein the woman wraps herself. According to some, מחלצות shifts; מעטפות trowsers.
מטפחות Vails (comp. Rut 3:15).
הריטים According to some, a dress in the form of a Taleth (this word has a similar meaning in Arabic ), or figures (comp. 8:1), as I shall explain further on (ibid.)
נליונים Cloth (cp. 8:1).
סדינים Fine linen (cp. Pr. 31:24).
צניפות An ornament for the head;
רדידים. In Arabic, this word signifies a dress in form of a taleth. All these things here enumerated are, in general, articles of clothing, and vary with the fashion of the country.
בושם Sweet smell. It keeps the body fresh and healthy.
מק Rottenness is nearly the opposite of the preceding. Root מקק, to rot; verb, ע״ע; comp. תמקנה They shall consume away (Zac. 14:2).
נקפה A noun; נ is radical; we may fairly compare with it ונקף And he shall cut down (10:34); its mean-is a kind of cutting.
מעשה מקשה Well set hair; comp. עשה שפמו ולא Nor trimmed his beard (Shmuel I 19:25).
פתיגיל A fine embroidered garment, which is worn over all the dresses.

כי תחת יופי According to Saadiah: for the contrary (תחת) is more fit for them; others take כויה ═ כי burning (Shemot 21:24); comp. ברויה ═ ברי (root רוה) with plenty (Iyov. 37:11); but this is contrary to the rules of the grammar, since ו in כויה is radical. I think the passage must be taken in this sense: For instead of beauty, the above-mentioned consumption, destruction and baldness shall come.

The women shall become widows in consequence of the death of their husbands in war. וגבורתך And the men of thy strength. Supply מתי the men of; comp. והנבואה עודד הנביא And the prophecy, the prophecy of the prophet Oded (Divrei Hayamim II 15:8)
ואנו And they shall lament; comp. באני In my sorrow (Deuter. 26:14); root און to lament, it is a weak verb (ע״ו); the accent is on the ultima. as in וסרו And shall depart (Shemot 8:1).
פתחיה Her gates. Those of Tziyon, which is mentioned at the beginning of the chapter.
ונקתה And she shall be desolate. Comp. נקיון שנים cleanness of teeth (Am. 4:6).
She will sit. The pronoun refers to Tziyon.

Seven. That is, many; seven is used in this sense because it is the number of the days of the week. All this (that is mentioned in this verse) will happen in consequence of the death of the male persons in battle.
The branch of Hashem. Some refer this to Chizkiyahu; I think that it signifies the righteous portions of the inhabitants of Yerushalayim that will be saved.

צבי Beauty (comp. Ez. 20:6); according to some, desire; comp. the Chaldæan יצבא he desires (Daniel 4:14). R. Moshe Hakkohen takes it literally: Hashem will send his blessing upon the plants and fruits.
That is written, etc. I shall explain this in the minor prophets (Malachi 3:16).
אם For or when.—The remainder will be called holy, when Hashem will have washed away all these from Tziyon.
ידיח Shall have purged; comp. ידיחו they shall wash (Ez. 1. 38).
בער Removing; comp. ובערת And thou shalt put away (Devarim 21:21)
נא Now. נא is always identical in meaning with עתה now.
לידידי Concerning my well-beloved; comp. אמרי לי Say of me (Bereshit 20:13).
לכרמו Touching his vineyard.
ידידי My well-beloved. Root tri-literal דודי .(ידד) My beloved. Root bi-literal (דוד).

בקרן בן שמן In Keren Ben Shamen. A beautiful spot among the vineyards of Yerushalayim. According to some, בקרן On a hill. בן שמן Fruitful; comp. שָׁמֵן fat (30:23), לשׁד הַשָֽׁמֶן fat oil (Bamidbar 11:8); and this explanation is not incorrect.

ויעזקהו According to some: he sealed it; comp. the Chaldæan עזקתא Ring (3:21) for the Hebrew ;טבעת but this gives no sense; I think that this word is hapax legomenon. In Arabic there is, however, a word of the same root, meaning fence or hedge (to fence).
ויסקלהו, Piel; he removed the stones thereof; the Kal, (סקל) has the meaning, to heap up stones; comp. ושרשך And he shall root thee out (Tehillim 52:7).
ויטעהו מטע שרק ═ ויטעהו שרק And he planted it, the planting of a choicest vine. The verbal substantive is implied in every form of the verb, whether past or future.
Tower. A place for the watchman to dwell in.
And also made a wine-press therein. To press the vine within the vineyard.
באושים Thorns; comp. באשה thorn (31:40).

[The application of the parable is as follows:] And he fenced it. Palestine was filled with good houses and protected by strong walls. And he removed the stones thereof. Hashem expelled the Kenaani. And built a tower. The temple on Mount Moriyah was built. And also made a wine-press. The altar of burnt-offering was erected. And he looked that it should bring forth grapes, that is righteous men.
And men of Yehudah. And every man of Yehudah round about Yerushalayim.
What could have been done, etc. What good thing is left to be done for the vineyard that I have not yet done?
מדוע Wherefore. A compound of two words, like (מה זה ═) מזה What is this (Shemot 4:2). (מה לכם═) מלכם What is it unto you (Is. 3:15)
משובחו The hedge thereof. Comp. שכים thorns (Bamidbar 33:55).
לבער For pasture. Comp. ובער And he feedeth (Shemot 22:4).
Break down the fence thereof. By this the prophet indicates that the walls of the towns shall be destroyed.
בתה Waste. Comp. בתות The desolate places (7:19).
יזמר It shall be pruned. זמורה branch is of the same root; זמר means to dress the vineyard by cutting off the branches.
יעדר It shall be digged. עדר to dig, to prepare the vineyard by digging (comp. 7:25).
שמיר ושית Two kinds of thorns. The application of this figure is The wicked will increase.
The clouds. The prophets are hereby meant; comp. Her prophets also find no vision from the Lord (Eichah 2:9).
The prophet now explains who is meant by the vineyard.
משפח Disease. Comp. מספחת scab (Vayikra 13:6)
הוי Oh. The sign for the vocative; or (אוי ═) woe. That join house to house, etc. That move the boundaries of the houses and fields according to their own interest. אין ═ אפס Not.
Till there be no place. Till they have taken away every place.
הושבתם That you may be placed. Hophal of a verb ;פ״י comp. והורד and it was taken down (Bamidbar 10:17)

באזנָי באזנֵי יי ═ באזני יי To mine ears, the ears of Hashem, has come the report of the injustice which you have committed; comp. נביאכם יי Your prophet, the prophet of Hashem (Bamidbar 12:6); or, referring באזני to the prophet, supply אמר said, or קול came the voice of.
Ten. A round number, meaning many.
צמדי כרם Pairs of vineyards. They have removed the boundaries, and many vineyards were thus coupled together (נצמדים), combined into one.
בת Bath. A measure. חמר Homer; the same as ten pairs of vineyards. Bath and Epha are likewise equal.
משכימי That rise up early. Status constructus, although followed by the preposition ב; comp. השכוני באהלים that dwell in tents (Shoftim 8:11);
the same is the case with the following מאחרי בנשף, that continue until night. נשף The beginning of the night (comp. Mishlei 7:9, Iyov 3:9); sometimes נשף is the time before daybreak, the dawning.
ידליקם Causative. He will cause them to pursue; comp. דלקת Thou hast pursued (Bereshit 31:36); others compare it with דאדלק, the Chaldæan translation of המבעיר, he that kindled (Shemot 22:5).
כנור Harp. A well-known musical instrument.
נבל A musical instrument with ten holes. חליל Pipe. Likewise a hollow instrument; חליל is of the same root as חלול, hollow.

And they regard not the work of Hashem. Many explain, They regard, etc., because he who is given to drunkenness does not regard the ways of Hashem; comp. Whosoever is deceived thereby is not wise (Mishlei 20:1); but my opinion is, that by the work of Hashem those punishments are to be understood which Hashem was bringing over Yisrael, when the ten tribes went into exile.
ועם כבודו ═ וכבודו And the people of his glory, according to the rule of ellipsis; in the same way מח׳ צחה צמא ═ צחה צמא Men dried up with thirst.
צחה is nearly the same as צמא thirsty; comp. בצחצחות in drought (58:11); צח (18:4), the pure and dry air.
נפשה Her breath. נפש is the breath that comes out of the mouth; comp. נפשו his breath (Iyov 41:21).
ופערה And opened; comp. פערו they opened (Iyov 29:23).
לבלי חק Unusually.

ועלז בה And all that rejoice in it. or, and rejoicing will be—to others—at his fall. According to R. Yonah, the phrase ועלז בה And rejoicing, or laughing will be in it, describes that kind of laughter which may sometimes be noticed in people at the moment of death.
And the mean man, etc. And all men of the nations which surround Yehudah will be humbled.

But Hashem of hosts, etc. Then the excellence of Hashem will be known by the judgment (משפט) which He will have executed on Yisrael, and His holiness will be revealed by the kindness (צדקה) shown to them.
Then shall the lambs feed, etc. Yehudah will then be desolate, and lambs will feed therein, as if they were driven to be there.
כדברם As if they were driven. Comp. the Chaldee דבר to lead, to drive; and דברת floats (Melachim I 5:25).

מחים Strong lambs, that have marrow (מוח) in their bones; comp. ממוחים things full of marrow (25:6). וחרבות And the waste places of; comp. חרבן destruction. It is the construct state; supply הארץ the land; comp. ושכורת And drunken of sorrow. (51:21). משא ח׳ ל׳ ═ חמר לחם An ass’s load of bread (Shmuel I 16:20). גרים Strangers, that will then dwell there. מחים (Adjective, strong lambs) is the objective case; גרים strangers, the subject.
מושכי העון That fasten iniquity.

וכעבות העגלח חטאה supply הם משכים And draw sin as if it were with a cart rope. המאה is here a noun; it is the same as חטאת sin (comp. Shemot 34:7); it can also be an adjective, signifying a woman that committeth many sins.

ימהר Either transitive, let him bring hastily; comp. מהרו (Esther 5:5), fetch hastily; or intransitive, let him make speed; and only יחישה transitive, let him accelerate. As to two verbs in the future following each other without conjunction, comp. אל תרבו תדברו Talk no more (Shmuel I 2:3).—Let these prophecies be fulfilled, that we may see whether they are true.
Woe unto them that call, etc. They wish that these evils shall come, they are therefore like those that have no reason.
Woe unto them that are wise, etc. They do not know how to discern between good and evil, yet think themselves wise.
Woe unto them that are mighty to drink wine, etc. They lose their reason through drunkenness.
לנסוך ═ למסוך To pour out, though these words have different roots, נסך and מסך. Comp. מסכה she poured (Mishlei 9:2)
Which justify the wicked, etc. Wine deprives them of understanding, so does a bribe.
עקב For, the reward that comes generally at the end; comp. עקבו Its rear (Jos. 8:13).
וצדקת צדיקים יסירו ממנו And the righteousness of each of the righteous they take away from him; comp. בנות צעדה (Bereshit 49:20).
קש Stubble. Objective case. לשון אש The flame of fire. Subject.
חשש Chaff; comp. 33:11.
בלהבה ═ להבה through the flame; comp. בששת ═ ששת in six (Shemot 20:11); בבית ═ בית in the house (Melachim II 18:15); for ירפה, the predicate to חשש, is an intransitive verb.
Their root shall be as rottenness. Their root will rot, and they will not be able to stand.
כאבק As the dust of. It is the construct state; supply הארץ the earth, or a similar word. Their root. Their blossom. The parents and their children.
Therefore. For having forsaken His law.
And the hills did tremble, in consequence of the heavy blow.
כסוחה Cast away; the כ is radical; comp. כסוחה thrown down (Tehillim 80:17). These two words are various forms of the same root.
And He will lift up, etc. It will be as if He lifted up a banner to all nations to come and to fight against Yisrael; the same is meant by And will hiss, etc.
בזמן קל ═ קל Swiftly; or it is an adjective, attribute to the subject contained in the verb יבא he, a swift one, will come, and this latter explanation is the right one.
ינום He will slumber; נום signifies a sleep of a less profound kind than ישן. He will not slumber, much less will he sleep.
נתק It is broken. Niphal.
כצר Like flint; comp. צורים flint (Jos. 5:3); the form of the noun varies.
וגלגליו The wheels of his chariots; they are known. סופה ═ כסופה כמוץ. As the chaff of the storm. They will come as quickly as the chaff driven by the storm.

וינהום And he shall roar. Irregular form; because regularly the guttural letter widens the vowel, and causes the form of the future to be like ,יִפְעַל the second radical of the verb פעל being a guttural; in the conjugation tables, however, no notice is taken of this property, else we should not have in the paradigm the standard form of the future ויפליט
יִפְצוֹל And he lets escape. He lets escape the prey, as I think, in order to see whether there is any one to deliver it.
עליו Against him: against Yisrael.
Like the roaring of the sea, etc.; behold darkness. For the light shall then be withheld from the earth. Comp. darkness of water (Tehillim 18:12).

And if he look unto the land, etc. For they will be on the land, not on the sea. And behold darkness. Darkness is here a figure for the distress of the heart. ונבט According to some it is Niphal, And it is looked; but I think it is Piel, And he looks, and its subject is Yisrael, the same to whom reference is made in the word עליו, as I have already stated.

צר ואור According to some, Sun and moon; according to others, Moon and sun, because the moon is small (צַר) if compared with the sun; R. Adonim thinks that ה is omitted, צהר═צר light; for the letters א ה ו י are sometimes present in a word when they are superfluous, and at others omitted where they properly form part of the root; but he is mistaken, because ה does not belong to the vowel letters, and cannot be dropped except at the end of a word, where it replaces א. I take צר literally; it has here the same meaning as in Tehillim 119:143, namely, distress, or—being an adjective—distressed. Palestine will be darkened by distress as well as by the sun, which will cast a gloom over her at the time of her destruction; for a mist will rise and hide the sun.
בעריפיה In her destructions. Comp. יערף (Hoshea 10:2) He will destroy; similar to it is וערפתו And break its neck (Shemot 13:13)

In the year that King Uziyahu died. Our sages said that died is here used for became a leper; for when Uziyahu entered the temple to offer the incense, the earthquake took place. This may be true; but מות can also be taken literally; in that case the death of Uziyahu must be placed in the same year in which Yeshayahu became prophet; no objection can be raised from In the days of Uziyahu (1:1), since even months might have passed between Yeshayahu’s initiation as prophet and the death of Uziyahu. This chapter contains the first prophecy of Yeshayahu.
High and lifted up. Attributes to throne (כסא), not, as many thought, to the Lord. The throne is above the Hajoth as I shall explain on Yechezkel.
And his train. The train of the throne; kings usually have their thrones covered with drapery.
Seraphim. The prophet calls them Seraphim—i.e., burning ones—because they seared his mouth.
Stood by Him. Comp. Melachim I 22:19. Anthropomorphism drawn from the custom of great kings.
What the wings mean I shall explain on the visions of Yechezkel.
He covered his face. Comp. And Moshe hid his face (Shemot 3:6). He covered his feet, out of reverence.
He did fly, to carry the message of Hashem.
And one cried unto another. The number of the seraphim is not mentioned; some believe they were two, but I am of opinion that there were many.
Holy, holy, holy. Repeated thrice, to express the continuity of the declaration. Comp. Yirmiyahu 7:4, Yirmiyahu 22:29.

Holy. An adjective. Holiness is an essential attribute of Hashem; it is therefore the same in every place. Hashem showed Yeshayahu this vision, that he might purify himself from the uncleanness of the lips; for Hashem is holy, and so also should be His servants and messengers.
Hosts. Angels that are above.

The whole earth, etc. Although He is holy above, still His glory filleth the earth below. He who explains מלא כל הארץ that which filleth the whole earth, that is, its inhabitants, and compares it with וּמְלאׇׁהּ and the fulness thereof (Tehillim 24), is mistaken. Comp. ה׳ את כל הארץ וימלא כבוד And the whole earth will be full of the glory of Hashem. (Bamidbar 14:21)
And the posts of the threshold moved. It was as if the threshold would move away from its place.
אמות Posts. About the meaning of the word there is no question; in this sense, it is, according to some, hapax legomenon.
ההמון הקורא מקול ═ מקול הקורא At the voice of the multitude that cried.

The verse begins with the past וינועו, and continues with the future ימלא, because the Hebrew language has no special form for the imperfect tense; past and future are therefore used for it promiscuously.
נדמיתי I am undone. I am cut off from the company of the holy ones; comp. ודמיתי And I will destroy (Hoshea 4:5). Some compare it with דׂמִּי Be silent (Tehillim 62:6). This view also may be correct.

A man of unclean lips. The prophet was a man of unclean lips, I think, because he grew up with the Israelities, that were unclean in deeds and words, and he learnt their way of speaking; comp. And he warned me not to go the way of this people (8:11); therefore he says, And in the midst of a people of unclean lips I am dwelling.

For mine eyes have seen the king, who is holy, and whom I was afraid to anctify because of the uncleanness of my lips. Although he says, Mine eyes have seen, etc., it is but in a prophetical vision that he saw Him.
ויעׇף Then flew. As written here, with a short kamez under ע, it is derived from עוף to fly; but ויעַף (Jud. 4:21), where the ע has a pathah, is derived from עיף to be weary.
רצפה A live coal. Comp. רצפים coals (Melachim I 19:6).
With tongs. As men use to do.
From off the altar. Where the fire is holy, where there is no strange fire.
זה This, namely, הׇאֵשׁ the fire; אֵשׁ is used also as a masculine noun.
Thy sin. The sinning by words; for he spoke frivolously, like his fellow-men.
For us. He speaks now to the seraphim; therefore he says, for us (plural).
Here am I, send me. Since my lips are pure, I am fit to be the messenger, but I was not before. From these words I infer that this chapter contains Yeshayahu’s first prophecy.

Hear ye, indeed, etc. Some assert that Hashem does not accept the repentance of the sinner, when his earthly punishment is already decreed, to cancel the sentence. R. Moshe Hakkohen is of opinion that this passage describes the benefit the people will derive from listening to the good advice of the prophet; that they will be delivered from their afflictions. This is, however, contradicted by Lest they return and be healed. The first explanation is the right one.

השמן Make fat. According to some it is infinitive, like הקטר To burn incense (Shmuel I 3:16); and הׇשַׁע likewise, like הׇרַע To do evil (Vayikra 5:4); but this cannot be so, because of the conjunction פן lest. They are all rather imperative forms. We know that the prophet cannot make the heart fat; he shall only declare their heart to be so; there are many instances like it.

הׇשַׁע Shut. Comp. תשעינה Will be shut (32:3). In Chaldee, this word שעה has the same meaning. The imperative Hiphil ought to be הֶשֶׁע like הֶרֶף, but the guttural letter ע causes the alteration; the form הָשַׁע can also be derived from a verb (שעע) ע״ע
How long. The prophet wants to know how long this misfortune shall last, that the people shall not understand nor repent. The answer is, Till the land be desolate.
And have removed. He will take them far away, and bring them into a distant country.
העזובה The forsaken land. Adjective or participle passive Kal.

ועוד בה וגו׳ And yet in it shall be, etc. According to some: Ten more kings will rule over Yehudah before the exile, and then ושבה והיתה לבער it shall again be removed: comp. ובערת And thou shalt put away (Deuter. 21:21); others compare לבער with תבערו You shall kindle (Shemot 35:3)—and the number of kings from that time, Uziyahu included, was really ten. Some explain, the tenth part will be left in the land. Grammatically, עשיריה is an adjective, the tenth; but different from עשירית the tenth part; comp. שלישיה (19:24) the third. It is, therefore, clear that עשיריה refers to the number of kings.

אשר בשלכת Which were in Shalecheth. Two trees were in the gate Shalecheth, which were exceedingly strong. Those that take לשכת ═ שלכת are wrong, as well as those that derive it from השליך he cast; for whoever is able to say such things has no knowledge of grammar.
מצבת בם Substance is in them. They will still remain and stand firmly for ever; the comparison of the people with a tree is by no means uncommon; comp. for as the days of a tree, etc. (65:22).
Holy seed will be the substance thereof. Holy seed will they be that will remain after that. Those that would come back from the Babylonian exile are here hinted at.
And he could not. Pekach ben Remaliahu is meant; comp. Aram is confederate with Efraim, in the next verse.
Efraim. The kingdom of the ten tribes is called Efraim, because their first king Yerovam was of that tribe (Melachim I 2:26).
עם═על With; comp. האנשים על הנשים The men with the women (Shemot 35:22)
נא Now. Shear Yashub. The name of the prophet’s son, as I shall explain (ver. 14).
בנך Thy son. Those that derive בנך from בינה understanding understand nothing of grammar.

תעלת Ditch (comp. Melachim I 18:38), where the water is running; while בְרֵכָה pool signifies a gathering of rain water; many derive בְּרֵכָה from בְּרָכָה blessing, its water coming from a blessed place, from heaven.

חִשָּׁמֵ֨ר Accent on the last syllable. This word is to be compared with שמרים dregs, lees (25:6.), שמריו ושקם הוא על He has settled on his lees (Jerem. 48:11), and explained, Remain on thy lees (that is remain quiet), for הִשָּֽׁמֶר Take heed has the accent on the last syllable but one; and besides, the following Fear not proves the correctness of this explanation.
והשקט Transitive verb Make quiet; supply נפשך thyself or עמך thy people.

Tails of smoking firebrands. The prophet compares these kings to the tails of firebrands—אודים firebrands comp. Zach. 3:2—because they are like the remnant of a firebrand that smokes, but cannot burn; and adds. In the fierce anger because it is by their fierce anger that they are like tails of firebrands.
יען Because. י is perhaps the preformative of the future.

ונקיצנה Transitive verb, let us cause her to be distressed because of us; the suffix נה her, refers to Yerushalayim; the following, Let us make a breach therein, proves the correctness of this interpretation. The son of Tobel. According to some

טבאל is by a certain interchange of letters the same as רמלא, and בן טבאל therefore the same as בן רמליהו; this is nonsense, because Ben Remaliahu is mentioned before, and he says with Aram, Let us set a king in the midst of it, the son of Tobel. Others say that טָבְאַל means טׂב אֵלֵינוּ good for us, but אַל can only be taken as equal to לא, and בן טבאל would then be בן טבלא ═ good for nothing; but I conclude that it is the name of some famous prince in Yisrael or Aram.

תקום Shall stand. Supply זאת העצה this counsel; for יעץ he has taken counsel is mentioned above (ver. 5), and I stated already (5:2) that the verb contains implicitly a verbal noun, when it is not directly mentioned.
כי Although, Comp. כי עם קשה ערף הוא Although they be a stiffnecked people. (Shemot 34:9.) This plan will not be realised, although Retzin and Pekach besiege Yerushalayim.

And yet threescore, etc. Comp. the common phrase so and so many years are still left before such and such an event will take place. ב in בעוד is superfluous as in (טרם═)בטרם before. These sixty-five years begin with the year of the earthquake, that happened in the days of Uziyahu, when Amos prophesied And Yisrael will surely go into exile (Amos 7:11). Comp. And it was at the end of forty years (Shmuel II 15:7.)

יֵחַת Shall be broken; comp. החתות Thou hast broken (9:3); it is Niphal, like יִמַּס (13:7) Will be melted מֵעָם By a people. Evil shall befall them by means of a people that will come against them. יֵחַת can also be Kal of a verb נחת ,פ״נ to go down, (like יִגַּשׁ he will approach; comp. תֵּחַת It comes down) (Mishlei 17:9); הנחת Cause to come down (Yoel 3:11), where the נ is not omitted. The meaning of יֵחַת מֵעָם is accordingly: They will go down and be no more considered as a nation.
And the head of, etc. As I explained.

If you will not believe. Supply speak, or ask for a sign; wherefore immediately succeeds, And Hashem, etc., Ask thee a sign. But it appears that when the prophet said, If ye will not believe, etc., Achaz did not answer.
כי לא תאמנו Because there is no truth in you; comp. ויאמנו דבריכם So shall your words be verified (Bereshit 42:20)
Unto Achaz. Through Yeshayahu; comp. And Hashem spake unto Menashe and unto his people (Divrei Hayamim II 33:10).

העמק שאלה. Two consecutive imperatives without the conjunctive ו; comp. התאחדי הימיני Go thee one way, go on the right hand (Ez. 21:16). שְׁאָלָה Imperative, like שְׁמָעָה hear (Daniel 9:19). Ask, and touch the depth with the question, or ask on high above. Many take both העמק and הגבה as infinitives.

I will not ask, etc. From the answer of the prophet we conclude that the words of Achaz must be taken in a bad sense: I shall not ask nor shall I try Him, for I know that He cannot do what I should ask Him.

To weary men. To make them tired of a thing which they have tried to accomplish, so that they become unable to continue their efforts. Because you are kings, and people cannot resist you, you think the same about the ways of Hashem.

Therefore Hashem himself etc. Though you do not ask a sign, He will give it you. It is to me a matter of surprise that there are those who say the prophet here refers to Jesus, since the sign was given to Achaz, and Jesus was born many years afterwards; besides, the prophet says, For before the child shall know to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land shall be forsaken; but the countries of Efraim and Syria were wasted in the sixth year of Chizkiyahu, and it is distinctly said of whose two kings, etc. Many make the mistake of identifying Immanuel with Chizkiyahu; they cannot be the same, granting even this prophecy to have been uttered at the beginning of the reign of Achaz; he reigned only sixteen years, and Chizkiyahu was at the death of Achaz twenty-five years old. According to others, Immanuel is another son of Achaz, and others again take the names (Immanuel, Maher Shalal and Shear Yashub) as symbolical of the kingdom; but if so, what meaning would be in the child’s knowing good and evil and in Maher Shalal calling father and mother? (8:4). I think that Immanuel is the son of Yeshayahu, as well as Maher Shalal; the latter is proved by And I went unto the prophetess, etc. (8:3). Shear Yashub is similarly related to the prophet (ver. 3); each of the three sons received a name that contained some hint at future events; Immanuel implied that Elokim would help them and be with them during the troubles caused by the two kings; Maher Shalal, that the time for the exile of Shomron had arrived; and Shear Yashub, that the remnant of Yisrael would repent; this explanation is well borne out by the words, Behold, I and the children whom Hashem hath given me, are for signs and for wonders. Comp. The children which Hashem hath graciously given to thy servant (Bereshit 33:5). Those that in the former passage regard children as equivalent to pupils must produce us some analogy from Scripture. Yeshayahu himself was a sign and an example concerning Mitzrayim (20:3).—The Gaon says that the sign consisted in the child being a male child; but in my opinion the sign was that the child was to eat butter and honey; for it is not usual that children eat these things immediately after their birth.

We know that a male child is called נער, a female child נערה or עלמה—the feminine of עֶלֶם—whether she be a virgin or not; for עלמה signifies a person of a certain age, like the masculine עלם; and in דרך גבר בעלמה the way of a man with a young woman (Mishlei 30:19) עלמה is certainly not a virgin; because at the beginning of that passage it is said, which I know not (ibid. 18).
וקראת And shall call. Subject is, העלמה; comp. וחטאת And it sinneth (Shemot 5:16).
ברע The bad. The bad food; as הטוב the good means the good food.

For before the child shall know, etc. Some assume that such is the case at the age of twenty years, because of the words of Moshe, From twenty years old, etc. (Shemot 30:14); if so, this prophecy must have been delivered after the second year of the reign of Achaz. But it is possible that an earlier age than twenty is meant.
The Lord shall bring unto thee, etc. When Shomron and Damesek will be exiled, then Sancheriv shall come against Yehudah.
The fly. The host is compared to a fly.
The rivers of Mitzrayim. The king of Ashur conquered Mitzrayim; therefore the Mitzrim had to come to assist him.
וְנָחֽוּ And shall rest. Accent on the last syllable; comp. שָֽׂמוּ (Bereshit 40:15), וְשָׂמֽוּ (Bamidbar 6:27).
בתות Desolate places. Comp. בתה desolate (5:6).
ובנקיקי And in the holes of. Hapax legomenon; its meaning is found by the context.
נעצוצים Thorns Trees that bear no fruit. Comp. נעצוץ (55:13) thorn.
נהלולים Bushes. Hap. leg.—They will be so many that they will encamp even in uninhabited and desolate places.

Shall Hashem shave with a razor that is hired. This refers to the angel of Hashem coming forth and destroying the camp of Ashur (37:36). Some take השכירה in the meaning of great; comp. שכיריה (Yirmiyahu 46:21) her great ones. I think that שכירה is a noun like אכילה the eating (Melachim I 19:8), derived from שכר hire, which the owner of the razor receives; for this instrument, the hired razor, is very sharp; it is his profession. The head, the hair of the feet, the beard. Every mighty one, all princes and noblemen; it is said so distinctly (9:14)
ושתי צאן And two sheep. Elliptical expression for ושתי שיות צאן And two lambs of the flock.
A man. Every one that will be in Yerushalayim.
And it shall come, etc. Hashem will send a blessing, so that plenty will spring out of little; therefore the sign was given, He will eat butter and honey.
היה═יהיה Was; comp. ישיר (Shemot 15:1) sang, יעשו They made (Tehillim 106:19).
שמיר ושית Two kinds of thorns. This figure refers to the hosts of Ashur that destroyed the land year after year.
With arrows, etc. One will not be able to enter the vineyards of former days, unless armed with arrows, from fear, they might harbour robbers or wild beasts in the thickets.

And on all hills, etc. And all the hills, where vineyards have formerly been carefully dressed, will now again be prepared; for there will be no thorns, and Hashem will give such a blessing on the vineyards of the mountains, that people will send the cattle there; comp. He bindeth his foal to the vine (Bereshit 49:4). The prophet says that from one cow and two sheep there will be obtained a plentiful supply of milk; and the vineyards of the mountains, that will alone remain undamaged, will enjoy a boundless blessing from the Almighty.
גליון. According to some related to מגלה scroll; the י of גליון compensates for the omission of the Dagesh in ל; comp. דליו They are poor (Mishlei 26:7).

בחרט In the form of. Comp. Shemot 32:4. בחרט אנוש. In the form of a man. That is, in a form cast in the same way as the figure of a man is cast. Others take גליון as the singular to גליונים (3:23) a cloth to which the writing was affixed by embroidery. Maher Shalal Chash Baz. The prophet is told to indicate by these words the fall of Shomron.

.ואעידה According to some the א is here instead of ה. And take unto me faithful witnesses. According to others the future is used for the past: And I took unto me faithful witnesses. It may, however, be taken literally, that I should take as witnesses for me. The prophet did what Hashem commanded, although it is not related in the text.
Uriyah the priest; Uriyah was then high priest. Zachariah was likewise a great man; what our Sages say about the prophecies of Zachariah and Uriyah is well known.
ואקרב. And I went unto. Euphemism; comp. Shemot 19:15.
The prophetess. The wife of the prophet; she is called prophetess on account of her husband being a prophet, or perhaps because she was herself a prophetess.
For before the child, etc. This child was born two years before the conquest of Shomron.
ישא. The subject is the indeterminate pronoun one; one will carry away: comp. ויאמד ליוסף And one said to Yosef (Bereshit 48:1).
And the Lord spake again. The word again is used because the following prophecy refers likewise to the invasion of the king of Ashur.

The water of the Shiloah. According to some Yerushalayim is referred to by these words, but it is more correct to explain them as indicating the house of David, because the majority of the kings of this house were righteous, but the kings of Yisrael were all bad and wicked. מי השילח, literally: the canal, the water which is conducted by man, or which causes plants (שלחים) to sprout forth; comp. שלחיך Thy plants (Shir Hashirim 4:13).
Upon them. Upon the men of Yehudah, that conspired against Achaz.
אפיקיו Its rapid parts. — comp. Tehillim 42:2, Shir Hashirim 5:12 — or banks, according to the context.

גדותיו its banks; some supply ;ר comp. שרשות ═ שרשרות (Shemot 28:14, 22), but this is a mistaken inference, for in שרשרות it is the ר of reduplication which is dropped in שרשת; the root is שרש, but we have no instance where a radical ר is dropped, since it does not belong to the silent letters.
Immanuel. He is mentioned here because he is to serve as a sign that Yerushalayim will be delivered out of the hand of Pekach, Retzin and Sancheriv, even after the conquest of Damesek and Shomron.
רעו Break. Comp. תרועם thou shalt break them (Tehillim 2:9.) רׂעוּ as well as חׂתּוּ are imperatives; like סׂבּוּ surround (Tehillim 48:13).
Gird yourselves. These words are repeated twice, to indicate that they should be perpetually armed.

Take counsel, etc. Whatever you will counsel against Yerushalayim will not be realised. עצו. Take counsel. A biliteral verb (ע״ו). According to R. Moshe Hakkohen, י is dropped, and it should be יעוצו like זכורו (Nechemyah 4:8).
כי עמנואל. For God is with us. Here we have the reason for עמנואל Immanuel being the name of the prophet’s son.
For Hashem spake thus to me with a strong hand, that is: When the prophecy came with force upon me; comp. The hand of Hashem was upon me (Ez. 37:1).

ויסרני And instructed me. The ס has a dagesh to compensate for the absence of the י, which is the first radical; comp. אֶצָּרְךָ I formed thee (Yirmiyahu 1:5). He instructed me, etc. A proof of the correctness of my view concerning Unclean lips (6:5).

Say ye not. The prophet warns the right-minded not to conspire against Achaz in order to join the King of Ashur; and this is to be understood by And their fear, etc., which refers to the King of Ashur mentioned before (ver. 7)

אתו Him is added, although את is before the noun, as in many instances; or it means Him alone. You shall sanctify. That which is holy is usually revered by men; comp. for he is a man of God, he is holy (Melachim II 4:9).
מעריצכם is either an adjective, Your dreadful one, or participle, who in truth makes you fear.
והיה And he—namely, the King of Ashur—shall be.

למקדש For a sanctuary. For a place whither man is used to go to receive blessing and strength. It is to be connected with לאבן .נֶגֶף For a stone. For a rock, upon which man is used to go to find shelter.
For the two houses of Yisrael. The kingdom of Yisrael and that of Yehudah.
For a gin, to Efraim. And for a stumbling, to Yehudah.
By them. By the gin and snare.

צור According to some נ of the root is dropped; נצור ═ צור keep; but more correctly it is explained, Bind up; comp. וצרת And bind up (Deuter. 14:25). צור has, then, the same meaning as in the parallel phrase, חתום seal.—Do not reveal these prophecies, the testimony and the law.
למורי My disciples. An adjective (comp. 1. 4); it is the same as תלמידי my pupils.
And I will wait. These are the words of the prophet; he will delay revealing the divine message till the Almighty shall give him permission.
Behold, I and the children, etc. They may understand a part of the prophecy entrusted to me from my actions and from the names of my sons.
From Hashem of hosts, etc. These names were given by Hashem of hosts,
Who dwelleth on the mount of Tziyon, and loves His people exceedingly.
To you. He addresses his pupils.
המצפצפים That peep. צִפְצֵף has a meaning similar to רִּבֵּר; comp. אצפצף I shall peep (38:14).
והמהגים. Hiphil. And they that cause others to mutter.

Surely a people that seeketh unto their Elokim, etc. This is the reply. Surely such is a people that seeketh unto his Elokim! sarcastically and ironically said. How could one seek unto the lifeless idols for the benefit of the living.

לתורה ולתעודה Concerning the law and concerning the testimony. The preposition ל has the same meaning as in לי of me (Bereshit 20:13). לתורה ולתעודה Concerning the law and the testimony contained in the prophecy.—They will surely speak according to this word, etc. They will say : We shall not listen to it, for it is like a night that is not followed by a dawn; its secret will never come forth to light. According to some לתורה is an oath, by the law; but we find no analogy to this in Scripture.

And they shall pass through it, etc. Some explain this verse in the following way: Days will come when he that is travelling in Yehudah, and being himself of the tribe of Yehudah, will be hardly bestead and hungry through the host of Sancheriv; and when he sees that neither his king nor his idol will help him, then he will turn upwards to pray to Elokim in heaven. I think it refers to the host of Sancheriv when marching through the land of Yehudah; for when the army is large, it is frequently exposed to hunger.
Their king; that is, the King of Ashur.
And look upward. Wherever they will turn, upward or downward, only darkness shall meet them.
מעוף Dimness. Comp. עיפתה darkness (Iyov 10:22).

מנדח Scattered. Comp. והנדחים And they that are scattered (27:13); the construction of the sentence is perhaps אפלה מנדח ומעוף Dimness of darkness is scattered about; by this construction the masculine form of פנודח is explained.

מי לא מועף וגו׳ For such dimness and darkness will not come over Yerushalayim, though it is distressed by the enemy. According to others, The enemy will not be able to hurry to Yerushalayim, which he had distressed.

At the first, etc. The first time that the king of Ashur came, he afflicted the land of Yisrael only slightly, by taking the districts of Zevulun and Naftali; but the last time he afflicted it heavily, and took the whole of Galilæa. Of the nations. Perhaps Yisrael is meant; comp. בעממיך Amongst thy people (Shoftim 5:14)
The people that walk in darkness. The people of Yerushalayim, who in their affliction walk in her streets as if they were blind of both their eyes.

Thou hast multiplied the nation, that is, the tribe of Yehudah, that assembled again in Yerushalayim. לו הגדלת השמחה Unto him thou hast increased the rejoicing; this is according to the Keri; but according to the Ketib, To whom thou hast never before given so great rejoicing; comp. לא היה פחד There was no such dread before (Tehillim 53:6).
סבלו His burden. The form of the noun varies.
The staff of his shoulder. The staff that smote his shoulder.

החתות Thou hast broken. The ה has Pathah on account of the succeeding guttural (ח); comp. הַחלות Thou hast begun (Deuter. 3:24); it is a regular form. The second person refers to Hashem, as in הרבית Thou hast multiplied.
As in the days of Midyan. In the time of Gidon.

סאון. According to some, this word is related to סאה measure, and the meaning of the whole phrase is, Hashem gave to Ashur the full measure according to her deeds. Some say, that by metathesis סאון is said for אסון mishap; comp. כשב ═ כבש lamb; more correctly it may be said that this word is a hapax legomenon, and from the succeeding סואן, which is a verb (participle Kal), we see that נ is radical; the meaning of סאן is to cry loudly.

ושמלה מגוללה בדמים And garments rolled in blood. Every one lies slain in his blood. Or the garment which rolled in the blood of murdered people, etc. לשרפה והיתה It was burned. This refers to the destruction of the host of Sancheriv, which was burnt by the angel (37:36)

For unto us, etc. All this has come to pass through the merit of the child that is born unto us. We know that at the time of the invasion of Sancheriv, Chizkiyahu was thirty-nine years old; at the time of this prophecy he is, therefore, called child (ילד). פלא יועץ אל גבור אבי עד. According to some, these expressions are names of Hashem, and the following שר שלום, the name of the child. I think that all these words are names of the child; he is called פלא wonder, because Hashem did wonders in his days; יועץ counselling; this is distinctly said of Chizkiyahu (comp. Divrei Hayamim II 30:2); אל גבור Mighty chief; for Chizkiyahu was powerful; אבי עד The father of perpetuity, because the reign of the house of David was prolonged through his merits: עַד has here the same meaning as in 58:15. שר שלום Prince of peace because peace was established in his days; comp. Divrei Hayamim II 32:22

למרבה Some remark, after the manner of the Midrash, that the use of the final Mem in this word hints at the miracle of the sun’s shadow going backward (38:8). מרבה is either a noun, increase, like מְַעַשֶׂה work, or a regular participle Hiphil, causing to increase.
With justice. Comp. Divrei Hayamim II 32:22
A word. A prophecy or Divine decree.
And it hath lighted, etc. Repetition of the same idea as usual.
Efraim. The ten tribes.
The bricks are fallen down, etc. A figurative expression for Ashur has done evil to us, but we shall again be as happy as before, and even happier.
שקמים A kind of inferior fig-trees, sycamores.
The adversaries of Retzin. The Ashur.
His enemies. The enemies of Hashem : Aram, or Yisrael.
The Syrians, etc. The Syrians in the east of Yisrael will join Ashur to do evil to Yisrael.
And the Plishtim, etc. They are in the west of Palestine.
And the people. Namely, Yisrael.
Unto him that smiteth them. Unto Hashem, because in truth it is He that smote; the word המכהו has two determinations, like האהלי (Jos. 21:7), my tent.
The people did not return to the Lord, because there was none to show them the right way.
כפה Root. Comp. וכפתו And his root (Iyov 15:32).
ואגמון And rush. Comp. 58:5. It is a well-known tender plant.
The ancient, etc. Now the prophet explains that both head and root signify the old; the tail and the rush signify the false prophet.

מאשרי The leaders of. Here we have א instead of י. This process of substituting א for י is reversed in תתימרו You boast yourselves (61:6). In ומאשריו And they that are led, is the א again in the place of .י
Hashem will rejoice. Anthropomorphism; as human beings are accustomed to rejoice when their work is in a good condition.
חנף Hypocrite. A man who is virtuous in outward appearance, but vicious at heart.
For wickedness burneth, etc. The prophet compares the fate of the wicked with the fire which consumes the thing that has produced the fire.
Thorns and thistles. The wicked. ויתאבכו Hapax legomenon. And they mount up.

נעתם Is darkened. In Arabic the word signifies dark. This verse is closely connected with the preceding, where the smoke is described. R. Moshe Hakkohen compares נעתם with יועם is become dim (Eichah 4:1), and explains the ת to be the characteristic of the Hithpael; but this is a blunder.
And he shall snatch, etc. Figuratively said, referring to the civil wars which they shall wage against each other, though being brethren, and forming, as it were, one body.
Menashe, Efraim, etc. This verse explains the preceding; Menashe will fight against Efraim, and both against Yehudah.
הוי Oh. Sign of the vocative; the prophet invokes the judges and their scribes.
ומכתבים And they that cause to write. A verb that governs two accusatives; it is participle Piel. עמל כתבו They cause to write grievousness. עמל is to be joined with .כתבו
To turn aside, etc. They command the secretaries to write false documents for the orphans, widows and poor, who are powerless, and cannot open their mouths in defence of their rights.
And what, etc. All this you have done, but what do you think to do in future, when Hashem will visit your iniquities?
כבודכם Your Glory. Your army.

All this you have done. בלתי וגו׳ Except they bow down, etc. None will escape except those that will bow down amongst the captives, or throw themselves amongst the slain, as if they were slain with them.
הוי Oh. Sign of the vocative.
The rod of mine anger, wherewith I have chastised many.
And the staff, etc. And the staff that is in the hand of the Ashur, is the instrument of my indignation.
The people of my wrath. The people with whom I am wroth.
ידמה He meaneth. Comp. דמיתי I thought (Bamidbar 33:56); דמיון imagination (Tehillim 17:12). He does not think that I have sent him to chastise; he only considers how to overthrow every kingdom.
He will say in his heart. Behold my officers, etc. Those who formerly were officers, have now, through me, become rulers over nations.
כלנו Kalno כלנה ═ Kalneh (Bereshit 10:10); for the names mentioned there (Gen. x.) are names of places called after their founders, like מצרים Mitzrayim.
לממלכות עובדי אליל ═ לממלכות אליל To the kingdoms of worshippers of idols.
ופסיליהם מירושלים And their graven images of Yerushalayim. Of the country surrounding Yerushalayim, of the fortified towns of Yehudah, which were already in the hands of the Ashuri conqueror.
Shall I not, etc. This prophecy refers to Sancheriv, when he came to conquer Yerushalayim.
יבצע He will perform (comp. Zach. 4:9).
His work. To bring the host of Sancheriv unto Tziyon.
The fruit of the stout heart of the king. Comp. The fruit of their thoughts (Yirmiyahu 6:19)
עשיתי I have acted valiantly. Supply גבורה valour.
נבונותי I am prudent. Niphal of בין, verb ע"י.
ואסיר And I was removing. Future for the imperfect; comp. יעשו they made. Tehillim 106:19.
ועתודתיהם And their treasures. Comp. ועתדה And prepare it (Mishlei 24:26); the possessions which man provides for himself for the days that are to come.

כאביר Although it is written with Aleph, this letter is pleonastic, and the word means strong, mighty—I subdued those that dwell in strong fortresses. According to R. Moshe Hakkohen, who takes the א as radical—comp. אביר the chief (Shmuel I 21:8)—it means like a hero.
לחיל The riches. Comp. החיל the wealth (Devarim 8:17).
נודד Moving. A transitive verb, governing the accusative. כנף Wing. This figure is used because the nations have just been compared with eggs, and birds come from eggs.

הגרזן. An instrument to cut with. Comp. נגרזתי, I have been cut. (Tehillim 31:23.) Shall the axe, etc. That is to say, It is Hashem that has given the power to the Ashur. משוד. Only one parallel is found to this word; וישר, And he cut (Divrei Hayamim I 20:3); it is derived from a verb ע״ע (שרר, to cut), after the form of מֽעוֹז, strength.

Another figure is contained in the succeeding .וחנופת מרימיו כהנפת שבט ═ כהניף שבט ואת מרימיו It is like the shaking of the rod; and this is principally the action of them that lift it up. כהרים מטה. As the lifting up of the staff, which is done by the people, not by the wood.
