Among his fat ones, leanness. This refers to the death of the nobles of Ashur, related Divrei Hayamim II 32:21.
יֵקַד He will kindle. Comp. וַיֵרַד, And he came down (Tehillim 18:10.)
יקד. A burning. A noun like כְּפׂר, hoar frost (Tehillim 147:16.
The light of Yisrael. Hashem. Shall be a fire. This refers to the angel that destroyed the Ashuri camp.
His thorns and his briers. The wicked.
And the glory of his forest and of his fruitful field. A figure, signifying that his armies would be as numerous as the trees of the forest, and as the ears of a fruitful field.
Both soul and body. He destroyed them as if it were by burning.
מְסוֹס, Destruction. A noun like יְקׂד; it is not in the construct state.
נוסס. Wonderful; appearing as a miracle (נֵס)
And the rest of the trees, etc. There will escape but a few, whose number even a boy that has not yet had practice in counting, will be able to calculate and write down.
That smote them, the Ashur. This verse shows, that many of the men of Yehudah conspired against their king.

שאר יעקב. The remnant shall return. This is the name of the prophet’s son, which is to be explained now. Supply יעקב, after the first שאר. The remnant of Yaakov, that is Yehudah, will return; repeat likewise ישוב before אל: The remnant of Yaakov will return to the mighty God (comp. Mishlei 21:14). The verse, if written in full, would run thus: שאר יעקב ישוב אל אל גבור שאר יעקב ישוב,. The remnant of Yaakov will return, the remnant of Yaakov will return to the mighty God.
Mighty, who is able to help them.

For though, etc. Although Yisrael should in those days be as numerous as the sand of the sea, only those that will return to Hashem will remain; for destruction, which is decreed—חרוץ, decreed; comp. חרצת, thou hast decreed (Melachim I 20:40)—by Hashem, will come like a river, overflowing with righteousness.
נחרצה. A decree is made by Hashem. Comp. חרצת (Melachim I 20:40)
Inhabitants of Tziyon. All the other towns of Yehudah are already conquered.
He will smite thee, in his thought.
בדרך מצרים On the way to Mitzrayim. Sancheriv was then on his march to Mitzrayim.

מעט מזער. A very little. Supply בימים, of time. And the indignation, etc. And mine anger and wrath, on account of their great iniquities will all be spent. תבליתם. Their iniquities. According to some, their destruction; comp. בלותי, My old age (Bereshit 18:12). The form of the word is like that of תַּכְלִית (Tehillim 132:32)
וכמכת מטהו═ומטהו. As he smote with his staff at the sea, when the water flowed back over the Mitzrim.
So shall be lift up. This refers to the defeat of Sancheriv, after which he returned to his own country disappointed.
His burden. The burden imposed by the King of Ashur.
Thy neck. Yehudah’s neck. וחבל.
And shall be destroyed. Comp. וְחִבֵּל, And he will destroy (Kohelet 5:5). The yoke is broken, when the neck has become very fat; it is a figurative expression for, Yehudah will become mighty.
מעברה. The passage, or the name of a place.
לנו. They have taken up their lodgings. Comp. ללון, To stay over night. (Bereshit 24:23.
צהלי. Lift up the voice. Comp. מצהלת, the neighing of the horse (Yirmiyahu 8:16.)
בת גלים. Name of a country. בת has here perhaps the same meaning as in בת־ציון. (The state of, the people of.
הגבים. Name of a place; or pits; comp. גובא, pit, in Chaldee. העיזו.
They saved themselves or others of Yisrael; it is a transitive verb; comp. העז, Save (Shemot 9:19)
And yet, etc. There will yet come a day when he will stay in Nov.
מסעף Shall cut off the branches (סעיפים). Comp. לא תפאר Thou shalt not take off the crown (פאר, Devarim 24:20); ושרשך And he will take away thy root (Tehillim 52:7).
פארה Bough. Comp. פארות Branches (Ez. 17:6).
במערצה With strength. Comp. עריץ strong.
And the high ones of stature shall be hewn down, etc. The nobles shall be cut off.
ונקף And he shall cut down.
סבכי The trees that are thick with branches.
בברזל With the axe, that is, by means of the angel.
And Levanon, etc. The princes, that are compared with the trees of the Levanon, shall fall. בברזל אדיר ═ באדיר By a mighty axe; ברזל is to be supplied from the preceding בברזל with the axe.

The majority of commentators apply this chapter to the Messiah, as if the prophet said, The Ashuri army, which is now attacking Yerushalayim, will perish; but besides this partial deliverance, a time of complete redemption will come for Yerushalayim. R. Moshe Hakkohen refers the chapter to Chizkiyahu, on account of its being the continuation of the prophecy recorded in the preceding chapter.
חטר Rod. Comp. חוטרא, the Chaldæan translation of .מטה
גזע Seed.
נצר Branch. Comp. 14:19.
And there shall come forth, etc. Chizkiyahu was very young at the time of this prophecy.
ונחֽה And shall rest. Comp. ושבֽה (Vayikra 23:13), And she shall return. It is a verb .(נוח) ע״ו
The spirit of Hashem, that is, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, such as, e.g., was assigned to Yehoshua (Devarim 34:9).
And might. Chizkiyahu was mighty, as stated (Melachim II 20:20)

והריחו And his enquiry. The ear is sometimes deceived in hearing sounds, which are only imaginary; the eye, too, sees things in motion, which in reality are at rest; the sense of smell alone is not deceived. He will properly investigate the question before him by his piety; he will not judge according to what he seems to see or to hear, because the testimony of the witnesses might be false.
The rebuking and judging mentioned in this verse are privileges of royalty.
And he will judge the poor with justice. According to the rule, Neither shalt thou countenance the poor in his cause (Shemot 33:3).
ביושר ═ במישור With equity. לענוי ארץ The meek of the earth. The good.
With the rod of his mouth. With his mouth, which is, as it were, a rod for the wicked.
And righteousness shall be, etc. And uprightness will never depart from him in all his doings.
The wolf shall dwell, etc. The peace that will be in his days is now figuratively described.
ומריא I have already explained (1:11); it is a species of cattle, the fat of which is forbidden.
פרה The large cattle; the younger of the breed is called עגל (ver. 6). Some assert that the female of cattle is stronger than the male.
Shall eat straw. As if his nature had changed, and he would no more, in seeking prey, inflict suffering upon others.
ושעשע And shall play. In this sense the word has always the reduplication.
חור The aperture of the nose or mouth.
מאורת The eye, which receives the light.
הדה He stretches forth; ה perhaps for י. Comp. יְרוּ stretch forth (Yirmiyahu 1. 14); or it is hapax legomenon.

They shall not hurt, etc. The asp and cockatrice will do no harm, as if all Palestine were full of the knowledge of Hashem; for it is an acknowledged fact, that he who knows Hashem will never destroy, but always build and improve.
כמים אשר לים מכסים ═ כמים לים מכסים Knowledge will increase, like the water which covers the sea. The water is never stopped, so knowledge will continually make progress.

To him shall nations seek. To him, that is, to Messiah, shall nations seek, that is, shall all nations be subjected. But according to the above-mentioned view of R. Moshe Hakkohen, this verse may predict the circumstances which would accompany the miracle of the sun; comp. the princes of Bavel, who sent unto him to enquire of the wonder (Divrei Hayamim II 32:31).
בכבוד ═ כבוד With honour; comp. בבית ═ בית in the house (Melachim II 18:15)

The second time, with regard to the deliverance from Mitzrayim. This verse may be taken as a proof that the prophet in the whole passage refers to the Messianic period; for the restoration during the second temple was not. complete, since not all the tribes, and not even all the men of Yehudah, returned to Palestine. He who refers the chapter to Chizkiyahu finds in this verse the description of the return of the people to Palestine, when they found that Yerushalayim had escaped uninjured, and that Sancheriv had died after the loss of the greater part of his army.
And He shall set up an ensign. Hashem will, as it were, lift up a banner among all nations, in order that Bnei Yisrael should see it and return to their land.
Yisrael. The ten tribes, for Yehudah is mentioned separately.
The envy also of Efraim, etc. Efraim will not be jealous, that Messiah will be of the tribe of Yehudah; or, if Chizkiyahu be the person here indicated, that his kingdom will be strengthened.

And the adversaries of Yehudah. The enemies of Yisrael generally; if the prophecy refers to Chizkiyahu, Aram is to be understood. Shall not vex Efraim, by taking revenge for their hostilities in the days of Pekach.

ועפו According to some, And they will spread; comp. מגלה עׁפה A roll that was spread (Zach. 5:1). According to R. Moshe Hakkohen it is hapax legomenon, and means they will rest. פלשתים Supply מקום or ארץ The place, or the land of the Plishtim.
Toward the west. The Plishtim dwelt in the west of Palestine.
Them of the east. The Syrians.
They shall lay their hand upon Edom and Moav, in order to spoil them.
משמעתם. Supply יסורו אל or יסורו תחת Will come under their supremacy.
והחרים And shall utterly destroy. Comp. חרם doomed to destruction (Vayikra 27:29). Bnei Yisrael shall then cross upon dry land, and the sea shall not hinder them by rapidly returning to its bed.
בעים Hapax legomenon. ם is part of the root. The meaning of the word is, with strength. Those that compare it with תבעיון בעיו (21:12) have no knowledge in grammar.
הנהר The Yeor.
והדריך And make go over. It is a verb with two accusatives.
And there shall be an highway, etc. This verse explains the purpose of the utter destruction and smiting (ver. 15).
As it was to Yisrael, etc. This refers to the dividing of the Red Sea at the Exodus from Mitzrayim.
And thou shalt say. The second person refers to Bnei Yisrael, who returned home.
כי Though. Comp. כי חטאתי לך רפאה נפשי Heal my soul, although I have sinned against thee (Tehillim 41:5)
הנה אל ישועתי The God of my salvation is with me, and therefore אבטח I will dwell in safety.
The explanation of יה, the half of the name of Hashem, will be found in the Book of Tehillim, and of זמרת in the Pentateuch (Shemot 15:2)
And you will draw water. By this figure the prophet indicates that they will rejoice exceedingly, as the thirsty rejoices when he draws water.
And you shall say one to the other.
קראו Call aloud.
עלילותיו His deeds.
זמרו Sing. Comp. זמרת the best fruit (Bereshit 43:11). Lit. Give the best and choicest thing.
מודעת Known. Participle Hophal.
גאות Excellent thing. Feminine, as seen by the affix .ת
Cry out, etc. It is right, that thou, O Tziyon, shouldst lift up thy voice, for God is in thy midst.
The fall of Bavel is recorded after the ruin of Ashur, because it was Bavel that conquered Ashur.

נשפה High. According to some related to נֶשֶׁף (5:11) dimness; more correctly it may be compared with שְׁמׇיׅם heights (41:18), נ in that case being the characteristic of the Niphal; in both cases it means high; or the word must be considered as hap. leg.
For them. For those that come to attack Bavel.
That they may go into the gates of the nobles. They shall come and march at once into the country; they will undoubtedly conquer it.
I. Hashem is speaking.
למקדשי Those that are appointed by me for the purpose.
That rejoice in my highness. That are glad to show my might, or, whom I caused to rejoice in the power I gave them.

קול המון A resounding voice. It is the nature of mountains to echo the sound of words uttered by any person, and this echo is alluded to by the expression קול המון. The root of המון is המה resound; comp. הומה being in an uproar (Melachim I 1:41). The prophet explains also what this noise among the kingdoms of the heathen people signifies; Koresh, the king of Paras, and Daryavesh, the king of Madai, became allies in a war against Bavel; this is distinctly stated in Daniel.
מפקד He is appointing officers, or, he is causing to number; comp. פקודים number. The word מפקד governs two accusatives.
They come from a far country. They come from the country of Eilam. From the end of heaven. As if they came from the extremity of heaven; that is, they come from a great distance.
Hashem cometh. The decrees of Hashem are coming, they will soon be fulfilled. And the weapons of His indignation. Paras and Madai.

משדי From the Almighty. This destruction shall come from the Almighty, and who shall be able to prevent it? According to others: From a destroying hero (שודד ═ שדי), but the former explanation is the right one.
All hands, viz., of the Babylonians.
פני להבים A face of flames. A face burnt by the intensity of the pains. According to others: The face of the Lehavim; Lehavim being the name of a nation similar to the Ethiopians.
אכזרי Cruel. The י is paragogic, as in פנימי inner (Melachim I 6:27).
The land, viz., of the Chaldæans.

וכסיליהם According to some, כְּסִיל is the name of the star which is nearest to the south pole, at the sight of which the camels die. My opinion is that כסיל is the Heart of the Scorpion constellation; it is, however, possible that כסילים in this verse—comp. כְּסׇלִים flanks (Vayikra 3:4)—signifies the stars near the poles. R. Yonah remarks that there is only one star named כסיל, and that here, in the plural כסילים, other stars are included; comp. בתי השן the houses of ivory (Am. 3:15).

יׇהֵלּוּ They will let shine. Its form is like that of וַיׇחֵלּוּ and they began (Shoftim 20:31). Its root is הלל, and it is a transitive verb; comp. בהלו גרו when he lights his candle (Iyov 29:3). יַגִּיהַ Shall cause to shine. Likewise a transitive verb, as proved by יַגִּיהַ חׇשְׁכִּי He will enlighten my darkness (Tehillim 18:29)
The world. Koresh conquered many countries, as he says; All the kingdoms of the earth Hashem, the Hashem of heavens, hath given me (Ezr. 1:2)
אוקיר I will make precious. A transitive verb; it is Hiphil of יקר to be precious; comp. הוקר רגלך Withdraw (lit.: make rare) thy foot (Mishlei 25:17).
A man. The male population, which will perish in war.
Therefore I will shake it, etc. A figurative expression for the fugitive will nowhere find rest.
And it will be. And the army of the Chaldæans will be
מ֭דׇּח chased, by the pursuers. מֻדׇּח is participle Hophal, like מוקטר burnt (Malachi 1:11 ) מֻגׇּשׁ offered (ibid.) מֻצׇּב set up (Bereshit 28:12)
He will be pierced. He will find no mercy.
נספה That is joined. Participle Niphal.
תשגלנה They will be ravished. It is read תשכבנה by euphemism.
The Madai, who are the most cruel people.
They shall not regard silver, as being of any value; they shall only desire to slaughter.
תרטשנה They shall dash to pieces.
And Bavel, the glory of kingdoms. And Bavel that has been the glory of kingdoms; comp. הבית הזה יהיה עליון this house which will have been high (Melachim I 9:8).
לא תשב It shall not be inhabited.
יהל Shall pitch his tent. יאהל ═ יהל Comp. מאזין ═ מזין listening (Mishlei 17:4).
ערבי The Arabian. The word has here the same meaning as ערב Yirmiyahu 25:22 and Is. 21:3. Even the Arabian, who is accustomed to move from place to place, will not pitch his tent there.
ציים Beasts that dwell in the desert (צִיׇה)
אוחים hap. leg. Beasts at whose sight everyone is terrified.
בנות יענה Owls. A well known kind of birds.
שעירים Beasts like Shedim; wild goats.
אוחים might also be taken as a kind of birds.
איים Vultures. Plural of אַיׇה Vulture (Vayikra 11:14).
וענה And will sing or And will dwell; comp. מעון habitation (Tehillim 26:8).

באלמנותיו According to some the same as בארמנותיו in his palaces; comp. Ez. 19:7; but as the letters—with the exception of אׄ הׄ וֹ יׄ—do not interchange; it is better to explain the expression thus : And every one of the vultures will sing with his widows.
ותנים And dragons. Comp. Iyov 30:29
For the Lord will have mercy, etc. When Bavel was taken, Koresh allowed the exiled Yehudim to return home.
ונספחו And shall be joined. Comp. ספחני join me (Shmuel I 2:36)
And the people shall take them, etc. When people will see how Koresh honours Yisrael, they will like to be servants to Bnei Yisrael.
מעצבך From thy hardship. Yehudah is addressed. מעצבך from thy hardship refers to the sufferings of the body, מרגזך from thy trouble to those of the heart.
מדהבה Gold. Comp. דהב the Chaldæan translation of זהב gold; in Arabic it is likewise דהב (ذَهَبٌ). The gold of the tribute is meant here.
The staff. A figure signifying kingdom. The rod. The same. The king is like a shepherd, the people like his flock.
מכת Stroke. It is the construct state; supply יד of the hand, or with the hand; comp. השותים במזרקי יין They that drink wine out of basons [of silver or gold] (Am. 6:6).

מורדף Persecuted. Participle Hophal. The meaning of the whole sentence is: Who ruled over him that was persecuted without intermission. The word מורדף might, however, be taken in the active sense persecuting.
Is at rest, since the death of the King of Bavel.
פצחו They break forth. The root פצח in Arabic means to speak poetically.
Yea, the fir trees, etc. For he had caused the fir trees and the cedars to be hewn down, to build with them fortresses and ramparts.
שאול The grave. It is common; therefore רׇגְזׇה (femin.) and עורר (mas.).
רפאים The dead. The א is, perhaps, instead of ה (the root being רפה to be weak).
עתודי The chiefs (lit., the he-goats) Comp. An he goat also and a king (Mishlei 30:31).
It hath raised up from their thrones. They were rising from their thrones as if they were alive; it is possible that the Babylonians had the custom of having thrones in the graves of their kings.
All they, etc. They would, if they could, speak thus.
חלית Art thou become weak. Root חלה to be ill; comp. מחלה illness. (Shemot 15:26)

יצע Was spread. It is the past, like יֻלַּד was born (Bereshit 35:26); or the future instead of the past.—As to the masculine form יצע (the subject רמה being feminine) compare לקח מהם קללה And of them a curse shall be taken up. (Yirmiyahu 29:22); this is a poetical license; the same freedom in the use of the gender is to be noticed in the Arabian language. Concerning the following ומכסך, which is participle masculine, the same remark is to be made.

הילל Very probably Lucifer, as בן שחר morning star proves. It is seen on certain days a little before dawn, and of all the host of heaven there is no star that shines with such brilliancy as this; its name is therefore הילל (lit., splendour); comp. יחלו They shall cause to shine (13:11).
חולש Who didst weaken. Comp. ויחלוש And he defeated (Shemot 17:13). According to others: Who didst cast lots; comp. קלקל בחצים He divined by arrows (Ez. 21:26).
I will ascend to heaven. An expression indicating the pride of the heart.

Upon the appointed mount. Upon mount Tziyon, which is the place appointed by Hashem for His sanctuary; comp. מועדי אל the synagogues of Hashem (Tehillim 74:8). This explanation is confirmed by the words which follow: in the sides of the north; for Tziyon was in the north of Yerushalayim.
Join this verse to the following : Thou hast said, I will ascend, etc. but thou shalt be brought down, etc.
אדמה I will be like. It is Hithpael, the characteristic ת being absorbed by ד; the Dagesh in מ proves that it is Hithpael.
ישגיחו. They shall look.
אליך יתבוננו. They shall become reasonable through thee.

תבל The inhabited world. This noun is feminine in every instance but the present. Some refer the suffix to מדבר wilderness, others to the Babylonian king, explaining ועריו הרס he hath pulled down his own cities. לא פתח.
He did not open. Supply, their prison.
In his house. Which he had prepared for himself, that is the grave; comp. man goeth to his long home (Kohelet 12:5)

There is an old tradition that when Nevuchadnetzar had died, and was buried, he was dragged out of his grave again, because the people of his kingdom were in doubt whether he really was dead, and feared he might again return to them as he had done before. This is perhaps really the fact; there is at least no doubt, that this verse refers to Nevuchadnetzar, who was the first of the Babylonian kings that reigned over Yisrael. This we may infer also from the words Prepare slaughter for his sons (ver. 21).
כנצר As a bough.
מטועני Pierced. Comp. طَعَنَ (טען) to pierce in Arabic. According to some,—who in a rather circuitous way derive it from טען to load, comp. טענו load (Bereshit 45:17)—full.
מובס Trodden, A verb ע״ו; (root בוס.
תחר Thou shall be joined. The radical א is dropped; comp. אהב I love (Mishlei 8:17); according to the grammarian R. Jehudah, י is omitted, and the word is derived from יחד to be together.
For thou hast destroyed thy land, even thy land, how much more other countries; this explains the words : And he pulled down his cities (ver. 17).
To his sons. To Belshatzar and his whole family.
Their fathers. His father Evil Merodach and his grandfather Nevuchadnetzar.

ערים Enemies. Comp. ערך thine enemy (Shmuel I 28:16). ומלאו וגו׳ Nor fill, etc. For they would stir up hatred everywhere; ולא מלאו═ומלאו. According to others : the face of the world will then be filled with cities, because the Babylonian kings will no longer be the masters of the earth.
שם Name. The person himself. שאר That is near to him. Comp. Vayikra 20:6. The father is meant. נין Son. נכד Grandson.
קפוד Hedgehog. A well known animal. According to some קפוד is derived from קפד to roll—comp. קפדתי I rolled (xxxviii 12)—on account of its power of rolling itself together.
מטאטא Besom. All agree that this word is hap. leg.; it signifies an instrument wherewith refuse is removed.
He hath sworn. The decree of Hashem is His oath.
I thought. Whatever I had planned, as far as concerned the past, has come to pass, and the same will be the case concerning the events that are planned for the future.
As I have thought to break Ashur in my land, that is, in Yerushalayim, where His residence is.
From them. From my land and from my mountains.
This is the purpose, etc. So will this plan be carried out, which I formed against Bavel.
For all the nations. For Ashur, for Bavel, each in its turn.
For Hashem of hosts, etc. Since Hashem has decreed, who can annul it.
המשא. The prophecy or a parable in the prophetic style, as is apparent from the words For out of the serpent’s root, etc.
צפע Cockatrice. It is the same as צפעני (11:8); it is more dangerous than the serpent.—Chizkiyahu shall be mightier than his father, and more dangerous to the Plishtim (comp. Melachim II 18:8).
And his fruit. The fruit that he will bring forth, will be שרף מעופף a fiery flying serpent; the flying one is the most dangerous of the fiery serpents.
בכורי דלים The firstborn of the poor. Yisrael, who had become impoverished sooner than any other nation,—Yisrael shall enjoy abundance and safety; the opposite fate shall befall the Plishtim.
Thy root. The fathers.
ואחריתך And thy remnant Thy children; comp. לאחריתו to his posterity (Daniel 11:4)
הילילי Howl. Lift up thy voice publicly.
For there shall come from the north a smoke. The king of Ashur, and probably Sancheriv is meant, as may be inferred from the words that Hashem hath founded Tziyon (ver. xxxii).
בודד Alone. Related to בָּדָד alone.
במועדיו In his castles. The smoke shall enter, and no one shall be able to remain there, even alone.

ומה יענה מלאכי גוי And what shall each of the messengers of the nation answer? That Hashem hath founded Tziyon, and therefore Ashur cannot conquer it; when the nations shall enquire, what has become of Yerushalayim, the messengers will give this answer to those that have sent them.
בליל In the night of. ליל is in the construct state. It is an elliptical expression for in the night of such and such a day of the week.
מואב In Moav. במואב═מואב; the preposition ב is omitted.
נדמה Was destroyed. Comp. ודמיתי and I shall destroy (Hoshea 4:5).
Kir. Name of a province of Moav; comp. Am. 9:7
הבית The inhabitant of Bayith. יושב הבית═הבית;
Bayith is a place in Moav.
To the high places. In order to worship the idols.
Their heads. The heads of the Moavim.
גרועה A cutting. It is a noun, (not a participle); comp. חבלתו חוב his pledge for the debt (Ez. 18:7).
The preposition ב on before כל ראשיו governs also .כל זקן Comp. Bereshit 49:25.
In their streets. In the streets of the Moavim.
גגותיה Her roofs. The roofs of the country.
ייליל Shall howl. Comp. ייטיב he will do good (Iyov 24:31); in both cases the sounding of the radical is an anomaly.
נפשו ירעה לו His soul shall cry out unto him. The soul of Moav shall cry out unto him, or the soul of every one of the armed soldiers will shout and say.
למואב For Moav.

בריחיה ונו׳ Her bars, etc. The bars of the country cry, etc.; comp. Howl, O gate (14:31); or Her bars have been brought to Mitzrayim, whence the king of Ashur was coming, or to Tzoar near Sedom; in either case ענלת שלישיה a heifer of three years oldis in apposition to Tzoar; or בריחיה being equivalent to בורחיה —not to ברוחיה for how could a participle passive be formed of a neuter verb!—her fugitive men came to Tzoar.
יעערו They shall raise up. The second ע is not radical, but the reduplication of the radical ע. The form is irregular.
Nimrim. Name of a place.
משמות Desolation. It is a noun; for were it participle Hiphil of a verb (שמם) ע״ע, the ש would have Hirek (מְשִׁמּוֹת)
יתרה Abundance. A noun.
עשה He hath gotten. Comp. Devarim 8:17.

ופקדתם And that which they have laid up. Comp. פקדון that which hath been delivered him to keep (Vayikra 5:23).—They will carry their treasures to the willows of the brook, to hide them there, or better they will carry away their treasures by boats on a certain river in their land, which flows between willows; that is, they will carry their property to another place, where it may be kept for them.
עד Unto. To be repeated before באר אלים unto Be'er Eilim.
דם Blood. The blood of the slain of Moav.
נוספות Additional evils. Supply רעות evils; comp. מלות עזות═עזות impertinent words (Mishlei 18:23).
כי אשית For I will bring. To be repeated before לפלטת: for I will bring against the remnant of Moav a lion, namely the king of Ashur.

כר The dromedary. A species of camel, that runs swiftly; comp. הכרי the swift messenger (Melachim II 11:19). According to some, הכר the dromedary, is called מושל ארץ the ruler of the earth, because its strides over the ground are the greatest; but it is more correct to say that כר is in the construct state: the animal is found only in the possession of monarchs.
והיה And he shall be. The Moavi shall be.
The daughters of Moav. The villages. Comp. Bamidbar 21:32
Take counsel, etc. The prophet says to Moav, Before this misfortune befalls thee, take counsel for thyself.
פלילה Judgment. The form of the word is like that of אכילה eating (Melachim I 21:32); comp. פלילים judges (Devarim 32:21).
Thy shadow. To hide Bnei Yisrael, when they take refuge with thee. נדחים Outcasts. People that are banished from their home.
נודד Him that wandereth, without being banished. Bewray not, when he cometh unto thee.
Mine outcasts. The outcasts, who are the brethren of the prophet, or who are the people of Hashem. It is certainly flattering attribute assigned to Bnei Yisrael.
The spoiler, who had conquered Shomron, viz., the king of Ashur.
For the extortioner, etc. For there shall yet be a time, when this tyrant will perish and oppression cease.
המץ The extortioner. A transitive adjective; root מצץ to suck, or to press; comp. תמצו You press out (66:11).
They are gone. The armies of the oppressor, the king of Ashur, are gone.
בחסד For the piety (of Chizkiyahu).
The throne of royalty.
In the tabernacle of David. In Yerushalayim.
A judge. Chizkiyahu.
מהיר Quick. Root מהר to be quick; comp. מהרה quickly.
We have heard. The prophet represents now Bnei Yisrael or the other nations as speaking.
נא Proud. The omission of the ה is irregular.
לא כן בדיו His branches will not be so. Comp. בדים branches (Ez. 17:6). Others render בדיו his thoughtsand כן right; comp. Bamidbar 27:7. As to בדיו his thoughtscomp. בדיך thy words (Iyov 11:3)

לאשישי קיר חרשת תהגו אך נכאים Some explain, For the foundations of Kir Haresheth shall you mourn, Surely they are stricken; that is, they will think of the present ruins of Kir Haresheth, when people will speak of their former grandeur. As to אשישי foundations, comp. the Chaldæan אֻשַׁיָא the foundations (Ezra 4:12). I, however, prefer to connect לאשישי with אשישי flagons (Hoshea 3:1), since the vine of Sibma is mentioned immediately afterwards, and to explain the passage thus—When you will remember the joyful days of the past, which are a contrast to the distress now prevailing, you will lament that you are stricken.
שדמות Vine trees. Comp. Devarim 32:32.
אמלל Languisheth. Each of them languisheth.
בעלי גוים The chief of nations. Comp. אדני יוסף the master of Yosef (Bereshit 39:20). לבעליו to his owner (Shemot 21:34). The king of Ashur is meant by בעלי הגוים the chief of nations.
הלמו Have broken down. Root הלם to smite; comp. והלמה And she smote (Shoftim 5:26).
They are come even unto Yazer. They are so long.
They wandered into the wilderness. They extended beyond the boundaries of the inhabited land.
שלוחתיה Her trees. Comp. שלחיך פרדס דמונים thy plants an orchard of pomegranates (Shir Hashirim 4:13).
נטשו They spread. Comp. נטושים spread (Shmuel II 30:16)
I will bewail. These are the words which every Moavi will speak.
Sibma. Name of a place; supply על for.
אריוך I will water thee. An irregular form; י is instead of ו, and ו instead of ה; the pronominal suffix of the second person refers to Cheshbon, the largest province of Moav.
קיצך Thy summer fruit. Thy fruit of the summer (קַיִץ).
הידד Hedad. A word used by those that stamp and trample about, causing damage to the fruits and the com while they are still fresh.
The gladness is gathered, to be taken away from them and given to others; it will leave them.
The Karmel. A part of which belonged to Moav.
ירועע He will shout. Comp. תרועה blowing the trumpet (Vayikra 23:24); ירועע is Polel of a verb הידד.

ע״ו Hedad. The hedad is pleasant, when it is heard at the wine press, at the time when the wine is produced; but its effect is of an opposite character, when it is heard in the midst of the fresh fruits and corn.
Wherefore my heart, etc. These are not the words of the prophet, but of the Moavim, whom the prophet represents as speaking.

Moav is weary, etc. He is tired of going up to the high place for the worship of idols; or it is to be taken in the same sense as ולא יוכל And he shall not prevail. The second explanation is preferable.

Hath spoken. His word is His decree. The expression hath spoken, is a figure taken from the custom of a king, who gives the orders to his servants. The figure is used in order to bring the idea of the divine decree nearer to our understanding.
But now Hashem hath spoken, etc. Hashem hath now revealed this prediction, namely, that three years are left till the fulfilment of the above prophecy.

As the years of a hireling, who daily counts when the end will come; so the prophet is satisfied, when he sees that the time of the calamity of Moav approaches. And the glory of Moav. His great armies. ונקלה וגו׳ Shall be diminished, and but very few will remain.
לא כביר Not great, quantitative; comp. כבירים many (Iyov 34:24), or Not great, qualitative; the meaning of the phrase is there will not be left of them any great man; comp. כביר great (Iyov 36:5)
מוסר Taken away. Comp. הסיר He took away (18:5).

דמשק מוסר מעיר Damesek is taken away from being a city. Join מוסר with the feminine noun דמשק, although it has a masculine form. More correctly, however, דמשק may be taken as equal to עם דמשק the people of Damesek, especially since in the phrase which follows, the feminine והיתה and she will be, is used.
מעי Heap. Comp. לעיים to heaps (Tehillim 79:1); the מ is not radical.
The cities, etc. This was caused by the king of Ashur.
The fortress also shall cease, etc. When Sancheriv came, Damesek had been already conquered and also Shomron with its fortresses.

And the remnant of Syria, Damesek was the capital of Syria. They shall be as the glory of the children of Yisrael, of which it is said, The glory of Yaakov shall be made thin (ver. 4). Others explain, And the remnant of Syria will be reduced to so disgraceful a condition, that the condition of Bnei Yisrael will be considered glorious, in comparison with the fate of Damesek.
The glory of Yisrael shall be made thin. The numbers of Yisrael shall be greatly reduced by slaughter and captivity.
And it shall be, the first time.
כאסף קציר As when the harvestman gathereth the corn. הקוצר the harvestman, must be supplied before קציר.
And it shall be, the second time. The king of Ashur came twice against the land of Yisrael.
In the valley of Refaim. A place where the harvest was bad, thin and meagre.
כנוקף As the shaking of. Comp. ונקף and he will cut down (10:34); ינקופו let them kill (29:1).
אמיר The top of the olive-tree. Comp. האמירך He hath exalted thee (Devarim 26:18); the word אמיר has the same meaning in Arabic.
Four or five. Supply berries.
בסעיפיה פוריה In the branches of the fruitful olive-tree.
ישעה האדם על עשהו Shall a man look to his maker. Man will renounce his own powers, because of Hashem, and this is the true confidence in Hashem (comp. Shmuel II 22:42).
And his eyes shall see, etc. They shall no more see the worship of idols, for they will only visit places sanctified to the worship of the Lord.

והחמנים Nor the images of the sun. The נ is not radical; comp. רחמניות merciful (Eichah 4:10). חמנים are images made like chariots in honour of the sun (חַמָּה) as stated in the history of King Menashe (Melachim II 21:3)
His strong cities. The strong cities of Yisrael.
החרש The tree. Comp. Yechezkel 31:3.
והאמיר And the uppermost branch. They abandoned everything, the root and the branches, in their flight, when Bnei Yisrael entered the land of Kenaan.
They left. By the pronoun they the Kenaani are meant.
And she shall be desolate. The prophet speaks here of Shomron, for she was the capital of the kingdom of Yisrael.
Because thou hast forgotten, etc. The prophet turns now to the people of Shomron, and rebukes them.
נעמנים The same as in Arabic; a plant that grows quickly. זר means likewise growing quickly. וזמורת שורק זר ═ וזמורת זר And a branch of a thriving vine-tree.

תשגשגי Thou shalt make to grow. Root שנא to be large; comp. שניא great. Thou shalt make it to grow quickly. And in the morning shalt thou make thy seed to flourish. The same. As a general rule for the understanding of the prophetical books, I say, that from the one part of the verse we can infer what the words of the other part signify.
נד There will depart. קציר The branch. Comp. בקצירי in my branch (Iyov 29:19)

נחלה Sore. Supply מכה plague, to which the word is an attribute (מכה נחלה ═ נחלה), a sore plague; comp. בריאה ומאכלו and their meat plenteous (Chavakuk 1:16) ═ בריאה ומאכלו אכילה. This explanation is supported by the words which follow: וכאב אנוש and of desperate sorrow; with אנוש con-connect ויאנש and it was very sick (Shmuel II 12:15). Thou hast a great many children, but when the day of affliction shall come they will all perish.
Woe to the multitude of many people, that is, to the king of Ashur and his army, coming against Tziyon.
ישאון That make a rushing. It is of the same root (שאה) as שאון noise. The נ in שאון is not radical; the form of the noun is like that of זדון pride (Mishlei 11:2)
But He shall rebuke him. Hashem will rebuke the king of Ashur.
From far off. That is, far from his own land.
And shall be chased. The part of the army that will be left will be pursued.
At eveningtide, that is, when the inhabitants of Yerushalayim are afraid of him.
בלהה Trouble. Comp. בלהות terror (Ez. 26:21); בהלה ═ בלהה like כבש ═ כשב lamb.
And he is not. When the angel will have come forth and destroyed the greater part of the camp.
This is the portion of them that spoil us. These are the words of the prophet in his rejoicing.
הדי Oh ! It is the sign of the vocative case. Comp. Zac. 2:10.
צלצל Shadowing. Reduplication of צל shadow. A shady land is identical with a wide land.
Which is beyond the rivers of Kush. That is, beyond the rivers of the kingdom of Ashur.
That sendeth, etc. That is accustomed to send messengers over the sea.
Go, ye swift messengers, and bring good tidings to Bnei Yisrael, that are fled or are driven into exile, and are now beyond the rivers of Kush.
And in vessels of bulrushes. This phrase is added because of the rivers mentioned before,
גוי ממשך ומורט A nation dragged and peeled. Bnei Yisrael are meant, that have been dragged from their homes like sheep, until they were flayed from the dragging.
To a terrible people. To the Ethiopians.
מן הוא From thence. From that people, or from those rivers.
גוי קו קו A nation of line by line. A nation whose intellect is like that of a child, who is taught gradually, line by line. ומבוסה And therefore it is trodden down.
בזאו They have spoiled. א is to replace the second ז of the root which is omitted; comp. דליו they are thin (Mishlei 26:7). This is the explanation of R. Moshe Hakkohen.
Rivers. This is a figure for kings; comp. The water of the river (8:7)
All ye inhabitants of the world. As if a banner were raised over the whole earth.
You shall hear, so as to know the work of Hashem, which He has done in the camp of Sancheriv.
I will take my rest. This refers to the divine glory which remained.
ואביטה And I shall see.
מכוני My dwelling-place, Yerushalayim.
אויר צח ═ צח Pure air.

עלי אור After rain. Comp. ענן אורו the cloud of his rain (Iyov 37:11). The sun is also called אור, the moon too,—comp. אורים גדולים great luminaries (Tehillim 136:7)—because they are the cause of the rain, but of course only at the will of the Almighty.
גומל Ripening, Comp. ויגמל And it ripened (Bamidbar 17:23). יהיה נצה Will still be in the flower.
And He will cut off. The pronoun refers to Hashem.
הזלזלים The sprigs. The branches which are joined to the root; the word is hap. leg.
הנטישות The large branches, that spread (נטש) widely.

כרת ═ התז He cut. This verb is often met with in Rabbinical Hebrew. The two verbs in the past follow each other without a conjunction, like חמק עבר Hath gone, passed by (Shir Hashirim 5:6). The meaning of the verse is: The Ashur will perish before the fruit of their devices will be ripe.
They will be left, etc. The host of Ashur, having been destroyed through the angel, will be left, etc.
לעיט To the fowl (comp. Bereshit 15:11); its forms are like those of שֵׁשׁ (Est. 1:6), and שַׁיִשׁ (Divrei Hayamim I 29:2), marble.
וקץ And shall summer. Comp. קיץ summer (Bereshit 8:22).
תחרף Shall winter. Comp. הֹרֶף winter (Bereshit 8:22).—The beasts will remain there to eat the corpses of the killed.
שי Present. Comp. Tehillim 76:12.

A people dragged and peeled. Yisrael, who has been dragged and flayed during the period of his captivity, will now be brought, to the honour of Hashem, to His abode on Mount Tziyon. According to R. Moshe Hakkohen, this chapter describes the redemption announced by the words—Hashem shall set His hand again the second time to recover the remnant of the people, etc. (11:11.
The Lord rideth upon a swift cloud. This figure signifies the imminent fulfilment of the divine decrees.
וסכסכתי And I will set. Comp. יסכסך He will set up (9:10)
ונבקה And shall fail. Root בקק to empty. Comp. בוקק maketh empty (24:1). נבקה is Niphal of בקק, and is formed like נסבה and it will be wound about (Ez. 41:7).
אטים Charmers. Comp. אט softly (Melachim I 21:27); אטים signifies things that are done secretly.

וסכרתי And I will give over. The כ is here, according to some, substituted for נ, but, in fact, only the silent letters interchange; it is rather to be compared with ויסכרו and were stopped (Bereshit 8:2).
אדנים קשה A cruel lord. The grammatical irregularity is already explained (Shemot 21:4).
And a fierce king. The king of Ashur.
ונשתו And shall be dried up. Comp. לשונם בצמא נשתה their tongue is dry for thirst (41:17)
והאזניחו And shall leave.. א is epenthetic. והאזניחו נהרות And the people will leave the rivers.
דללו They shall be poor. Comp. דל poor (Vayikra 14:21).
יאורי מצור The ponds of siege. The ponds which are prepared in order that the enemy should not be able to destroy the inhabitants through want of water, when he besieges the town.
קנה וסוף The reeds and flags. The plants on the banks of the river.
קמלו Shall be cut off. Another instance of the same root occurs in this book (33:9)

ערות Some compare it with מתערה spreading himself (Tehillim 37:35), and say that it means green; all green herbs that grow on the banks of the river and at its mouth, and all that is sown near the river, all will dry up. Others, The banks of the river and its mouths have been stripped of every thing that had been there, for the plants may be considered as a covering to them.
ואנו And they shall mourn.
הדיגים The fishers. A noun analogous to גַּנָּבִים thieves (1:23).
חכה Angle. Comp. בחכה with an angle (Chavakuk 1:15), an instrument by which the fish are caught. Many derive the word from חֵךְ palate, but they are far from being right.
מכמרת Net.
שריקות Red. Some compare it with משרק comb, but more correctly it is derived from שורק vine branch (5:2), and it signifies, having the colour of the vine branch, red; comp. שרקים red (Zac. 1:8).
חורי It is either an adjective, meaning white, or a noun, signifying fine things, חוֹרָי being a plural form used instead of חורים; comp. חוֹרֵי the nobles of (Yirmiyahu 27:20).
שתותיה Her foundations. Comp. Tehillim 11:3. The buildings which they erect to take the fish in.
שכר Sluices. Comp. ויסכרו and they were stopped (Bereshit 8:2), although שכר is spelt with שֹ; comp. בסורי ═ בשורי when I depart (Hoshea 9:12).
אנמי נפש The ponds for fish. Ponds containing the lives (נפש) of the fish.
חכמי פרעה, יעצי פרעה ═ חכמי יועצי פרעה The wise men of Paroh, the counsellors of Paroh. This is an elliptical expression; comp. נחרי נחלי דבש Rivers, brooks of honey (Iyov 20:17).
נבערה Foolish. Comp. בער fool (Tehillim 73:22).
I am a son of wise men. Comp. A son of free men (Koh. 10:17). Each of them will praise himself: my father was wise, my forefathers in days of old were also kings.
Where are thy wise men, etc. If they in reality be the sons of wise men, of royal family, why do they not know what Hashem has decided for Mitzrayim.
נואלו Are become fools. Comp. נואלנו we acted foolishly (Bamidbar 12:11).
נשאו They are deceived. Comp. השיאני hath beguiled me (Bereshit 3:13); it is Niphal.
פנת The stay. The nobles. Comp. פנות the chiefs (Shoftim 20:2).
שבטיה The tribes thereof, that is, her families.
נסך ═ מסך Hath mingled. The two roots have the same meaning, namely, to mingle.
עועים Perverseness. An irregular form of עוה to overturn. Comp. עַוָּה Overturned (Ez. 21:32)

Head or tail. Even a plant in its integrity, with head and tail, will not be left to them. Others take the phrase and explain it figuratively, They are wandering about and do not know what to begin; they can do neither the work of the head, of the old and noble (9:14), nor that of the tail, of the common people. In the same way the phrase, palm-tree and reed, is to be explained.
And it shall be afraid, etc. When the Mitzrim shall have heard these decrees of Hashem, and also witnessed their fulfilment, they will fear Hashem.
לחגא For a terror. Comp. יחגו they reel to and fro (Tehillim 107:27). ובמחוגה and with the compass (44:13).
The land of Jehudah. The glory of God, which is manifested in that land, is meant.
The language of Kenaan. We may learn from this that the Kenaani spoke the holy language.
עיר ההרס The name of a town. It is surprising how people can confound ה with ח .(ההרס with החרס)

Shall there be an altar, etc. The explanation of the Midrash is known, that the altar refers to the slaughter of the Mitzrim; but the verse can be explained literally. Comp. And they will worship with sacrifice and meat-offering (ver. 21)
They shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors, etc. Whosoever will be in trouble will come thither to bring his offering.
ורב And a great one. Comp. רב chief (Est. 1:8)
ועבדו בזבח ═ ועבדו זבח And they shall worship with sacrifice.
ורפאם רפא ═ ורפא And he will surely heal them.
ונעתר And he will be entreated. He will accept their prayer.
אשורה To Ashur.—Mitzrayim and Ashur will be in peace together, after a part of the Mitzrim have been taken captive and made subjects of the king of Ashur.

שלשיה The third. Most of the commentators compare it with ושלשים and chiefs (Shemot 14:7); but they must presume the existence of the second degree before they speak of the third. More naturally it is derived from שלשה three, and explained by the third; for there will be in Ashur people that will know Hashem, and many more so in Mitzrayim; and Yisrael will be a blessing in the midst of the land, for through him Mitzrayim and part of Ashur will know Hashem.
Whom Hashem of hosts hath blessed. For Hashem has blessed Yisrael, therefore he will be a blessing, etc; or He has blessed each of the three.
My people. Because they will erect an altar to the Lord publicly, He calls them my people.
And the work of my hands (and not my people), for there will be only a few of them that will know the work of Hashem.

And mine inheritance. Yisrael remains His inheritance for ever, for Ashur and Mitzrayim are this only temporarily in comparison with Yisrael. The Chaldæan translation renders this passage thus: Blessed be my people that is in Mitzrayim.
Sargon. Either Sancheriv or another Ashuri king.
Ashdod. A place belonging to the Plishtim.

And loose the sackcloth, etc. This shows that the prophet wore sackcloth. It would be a strange thing that the prophet should have gone naked, as a sign for Mitzrayim. I shall explain this circumstance, with the help of Hashem, at the beginning of the minor prophets (Hoshea 1:1).
ומופת And an example. Comp. And Yechezkel shall be unto you an example (Ez. 24:24).
שלש שנים וגו׳ Either in three years from that day, or three years, shall Mitzrayim be in misfortune.
Kush, that came to help them.
וַחְַשׁוּפַי And my naked people. The first person refers either to the prophet, the people whose nakedness he indicated by going naked, or to Hashem; the people whom Hashem hath made bare.
שת The back. Comp. Shmuel II 10:14.
ערות מצרים Either, To the shame of Mitzrayim; or join וחשופי, mentioned before, also to ערות, so that ערות מצרים is in apposition to .שת
And they shall be afraid. Bnei Yisrael, that flee to Mitzrayim, will fear.
Their expectation. The country to which their eyes are directed for help.
Their glory. Of whom—that is, of whose alliance—they were proud.
The inhabitant of this isle. Bnei Yisrael, who live in these islands near Mitzrayim, will say,
This has happened to those to whom we fled, etc.
מדבר ים The desert of the west, that is, Bavel, which is west of Paras and Madai; or the desert of the sea, ים being taken in its original sense, the sea.
לחלוף To pass through.
He cometh from the desert. He, the enemy, comes from the desert, and not from the sea.
From a terrible land. From Paras and Madai.
חזות A vision.
Grievous for Bavel.
Unto me. The first person refers to the prophet.
The treacherous dealer, etc. He who wishes to be treacherous and rebellious will be able to be so, and he who wishes to rob will be able to rob.
Eilam. A Parsi province.
צוּרִֽי Besiege. Root צור to besiege; comp. וצרת and thou wilt besiege (Devarim 20:12). It has the accent on the last syllable, like שׁוּבִֽי return (Tehillim 116:7).

All the sighing thereof have I made to cease. Some explain, None will be left that should sigh for Bavel; others, All the sighing she has caused, has ceased. I think that the whole passage, from the beginning of this verse till the end of the chapter, is the speech which the prophet put into the mouth of King Belshatzar; for it is well known that the prophet rejoiced in the fall of Bavel; how, then, could he have said, Therefore are my loins filled with pain (ver. 3)? The connection is as follows: the king says, When I heard the cry, ‘ Go up, O Eilam ‘—the soldiers used to call out in battle the name of their country—I made all her sighing cease with musical instruments; the vessels of the house of Hashem were brought, and they drank out of them, while Bavel was in siege and distress.
Therefore. Because I heard the cry, Go up, O Eilam, I neither heard nor saw anything on account of my great fear.

פלצות Boasting. Comp. מפלצתה her pride (Melachim I 15:13); the meaning of the whole phrase is: The boasting of the Paras terrified me; it may also be rendered trembling; comp. יתפלצון they tremble (Iyov 9:6).
The night of my pleasure. The night in which he drank out of the holy vessels. Hath he turned, into fear unto me. Belshatzar was frightened when Daniel read to him the miraculous writing (Daniel 5:3)
צפה הצפית I think that these words are hap. leg., and that the phrase means sing the song.

Arise ye princes, and anoint the shield. For Belshatzar was killed that same night, and Daryavesh, the old, was anointed king. The king is called shield, מָגֵז, because he protects the people; comp. Behold, O Lord, our shield (Tehillim 84:10)
For thus hath the Lord said unto me. These are the words of the prophet.
Set the watchman. This is not to be done really, but only to be seen in a vision.
וראה וגו׳ When he sees a chariot with a couple of horsemen, a chariot of asses, or a chariot of camels, he will hearken diligently to learn what news they have to tell.

אריה A lion. According to the Midrash, Habakkukis meant, because חבקוק ═ אריה taking the arithmetical value of the letters. I think ב must be supplied; comp. אש אוכלה as a consuming fire (Devarim 4:24). The watchman called with a loud voice like a lion.
I stand continually upon the watch-tower, to seek prophecy.
צמד With a couple. Supply עם. with, before ויען .צמד
And every one of them answered,
Bavel is fallen, is fallen. The repetition indicates that no remnant has been left to her.
He hath broken. There is no noun in the text to which the pronoun he could refer; comp. אשר ילדה אותה ללוי whom she had born unto Levi (Bamidbar 26:59).

My threshing. Bavel is the object of threshing; the pronoun my refers to Hashem, to the prophet, or to the chariot of men. The meaning of the phrase is: I also threshed it, and it has become like ‘ the corn of my floor.’ It is also possible that בן גרן signifies the pure corn that is kept in the threshing-floor, and refers figuratively to Yisrael.
Dumah. Comp. Bereshit 25:18.

He calleth to me. The prophet here represents Dumah as speaking, and we have to imagine a spy coming from Seir to search Dumah; he asks the watchman, Watchman, tell me, what is the time of the night, what is the time of the night? just as one of the people of Dumah would ask who had to rise early for a journey, or for work in the field, as is usual in a great many places. The repetition indicates that he asks several men. I, however, think that this question is put to see whether the watchmen sleep.

מליל Of the night. It should be followed by a genitive; it is without the genitive, like בייז חלבון in the good wine of (Ez. 27:18); מיין הטוב like the good wine of (Shir Hashirim 7:10), where the name of the place, whence the wine comes, is omitted. According to the Gaon (Saadiah), the meaning of the phrase is, O watchman, how much has passed of the night? O watchman, how much is left? I explain it thus, O watchman, what of such and such a night of the week; comp. 15:1
Morning hath come, and also the night. Many mornings and nights have passed, and you, O Seirites—for you are one of them—did not come against us to war.

תבעיון Ye wish. The root בעה to wish, to enquire, is of Chaldaic origin; the third letter of the root is here fully written, י being substituted for ה. The same is the case in בְּעָיוּ wish ye, which is like שְׁלָחוּ send (Melachim II 2:17). The meaning of the whole phrase is: If you wish to come, do so.
Return to those that sent you, and come all together.
אתיו Come. The word is irregular, the regular form is אְַתוּ; the א has a Zere, probably because of its guttural character.
By the watchman, the chief of the country is perhaps meant; for there are many chiefs that cannot endure hardship, and prefer to surrender their country.
בערב In Erev. Comp. Yirmiyahu 25:29. The Arvim belong to the family of Kedar; the second בערב has the same meaning.
Dodanim. Comp. Bereshit 10:6. The land of the Dodanim is hot and dry, wanting water.
Bring water. The prophet tells them to be kind to the caravans, and to give them water, for Moav was rebuked for not having done so (Devarim 23:5).
התיו Bring. ה is instead of .א
Teima. Comp. Bereshit 25:15.
With his bread. With the bread of him that is now thirsty.—Be kind to him, for he used to feed every one that came wandering to him.
They prevented. They, that is, he and his men or friends.
For they fled from the swords. They, that are wandering about, are fleeing because of the king of Ashur.
נטושה. According to some, sharp, the נ being put instead of ל, (לטושה ═ נטושה); this is wrong; נטושה means spread; comp. Shmuel I 30:16
For thus hath Hashem said unto me, etc., because of this sin, that they did not show kindness; comp. because they did not prevent you, etc. (Devarim 23:5.)
Within a year, according to the years of an hireling. That is, within a year, that will seem to be as long as the year of an hireling.
And the residue, etc. This expression indicates that the greater part will perish.
The valley of vision. Yerushalayim, the centre of all prophecies.

Thou art wholly gone up to the house-tops. Some think, they went up in order to offer incense to the host of heaven, but my opinion is, that they went up in order to see the force that besieged Yerushalayim, as is generally done under such circumstances.
תשואות Stirs. Root שאה to stir; comp. שאון noise (13:4).
עליזה Joyous.—Yerushalayim had been full of men, but they were smitten with captivity and famine, and could not fight.
מקשת אסרו Because of the bow they were bound. When they saw the bow of the enemy, they surrendered out of fear, and became prisoners.
מרחוק ברחו ׳ Which have fled from far. The relative אשר which is to be supplied; comp. עם אשר לבבם שלם ═ עם לבבם שלם in behalf of those whose heart is perfect (Divrei Hayamim II 16:9)
Therefore said I. The first person refers to the prophet.
שעו ממני Look away from me. Root שעה to let loose, to turn away; comp. תשעה Thou wilt depart (Iyov 7:19).
אמרר בבכי I will embitter by weeping. I will embitter those that listen.
ומבוכה And of perplexity. Comp. נבוכים entangled (Shemot 14:3).
מקרקר overthrowing, or pulling down, derived from קיר wall, with a negative sense; comp. ושרשך, and he will take away thy root (Tehillim 52:7), derived from שרש root.

ושוע אל ההר And of crying to the mountains. Some say that this phrase means the same as ישעו ואין מושיע they look, but there is none to save (Shmuel II 22:42); others, their cry will reach the mountains.
And Eilam, etc. In the following the prophet predicts the siege of Yerushalayim by Nevuchadnetzar. Eilam. Even Eilam, that was defeated by Nevuchadnetzar, was to take up arms against Yerushalayim.
And Kir, though being far from Yerushalayim;—comp. And Aram from Kir (Am. 9:7)—will uncover the shield round Yerushalayim against Yisrael.
Thy valleys. The second person refers to Yerushalayim. שת שתו.
They prepare, the forts, the trenches, and all the instruments of war.

And he discovered, etc. The veil was already taken away from the eyes of Yehudah, when the enemy was approaching; they saw immediately that they had no strength to resist. The third person ויגל, And he discovered might also be referred to Hashem.
And thou didst look. Yehudah is addressed.

Ye have seen also, etc. They looked to the fortifications, and found that the breaches of the town of David were many; they were therefore obliged to collect the waters of the pool, that they might serve as a fence round the town.
And ye have numbered, etc. They had to count the houses, in order to know the number of the soldiers.
And the houses have ye broken down. The houses that were near the wall from without.
ומקוה And a ditch. מקוה מים ═ מקוה A gathering of water (Vayikra 2:36).
Unto the maker thereof. Unto Hashem, who has decreed to bring Nevuchadnetzar against Yerushalayim.
Unto him that fashioned it. That fashioned the decree.
מרחוק Long ago. Join מרחוק either with ויוצרה, he that fashioned it long ago, or with לא ראיתם, you have not seen for a long time.
And in that day did the Lord, God of Hosts, call, etc. That is, God decreed. More correctly, however, this phrase may be referred to the words of the prophet.

הרג Slaying, causing the separation of the soul from the body; הרג is used with reference to cattle instead of שחט, and on the other side וישחטם, And he slaughtered them (Bamidbar 14:16) is used with reference to men instead of .ויהרגם
For to-morrow we shall die. The prophet foretells what people will say in the days of the siege.

ונגלה And it was revealed. This thing was revealed. באזני In mine ears. Supply אָזְנֵי the ears of. Comp. נביאכם יי Your prophet, the prophet of Hashem (Bamidbar 12:6). According to some the suffix in באזני refers to the prophet; but the first explanation is better.
Till ye die by the hand of the enemy who will besiege you.
Hashem of hosts. This attribute is added, because the treasurer is mentioned, who was appointed over the royal house, and whom some believed to be the master of the money stored up there.
הסוכן The treasurer. Comp. מסכנות stores (Shemot 1:11).
עַל Concerning. He shall prophesy concerning him, and say to him.
What hast thou here? Why didst thou stop here? And whom hast thou here of thy family that could assist thee?

חצבת Thou hast hewed. Comp. חצובים hewed (Devarim 6:11). Thou thinkest that thou wilt always remain treasurer, and that thou wilt die in Yerushalayim, and therefore thou hast already prepared a grave for thee.—Those commentators that take gravein the sense of palace are mistaken, as shown by the words there shalt thou die (ver. 18).
מטלטלך Will carry thee away. Reduplication of טול to carry. Comp. ויטילו And they cast (Yonah 1:5).

גבר O man. Thou, who thinkest that thou art mighty. Comp. והיית לאיש and show thyself a man (Melachim I 2:2). גבר is here the vocative case. It can also mean as the carrying away of a man. I prefer the first explanation.
צנוף יצנפך צנפה He will surely bind thee together. Comp. מצנפת mitre (Shemot 28:4). He will take him, together with all his money and wealth.
כדור Like a ball. The כ is the prefix of comparison; the word is familiar from its use in the Rabbinical literature; its meaning may also be gathered from the context.
A large country. Bavel.<

There shalt thou die, etc. There he shall die, with all his horsemen. The shame of thy lord’s house. For thou art a disgrace to the house of thy master; or thou wilt then be, etc. This prediction was probably verified in the exile of King Yehoyakim or Jehoiachim; comp. And I will call my servant Elyakim, the son of Chilkiyahu (ver. 20)
To my servant. He was the servant of Hashem; not so Shevna.
Thy robe and thy girdle. Every officer has a certain robe and girdle, as e.g., the wise men of Athens wore a certain distinctive girdle.
A father. A good teacher and a friend, like a father.
And the king of the house of David, etc. From this verse we learn that the house (ver. 15) means the royal palace.
יתד As a nail. כיתד ═ יתד. Comp. וכעיר ═ ועיר And like a wild ass (Iyov 11:12)
And they shall hang, etc. Having compared Elyakim with a nail, the prophet continues, they shall hang upon it, etc.
הצאצאים The offspring. The children that will come out of him.

והצפיעות And the issue. The female children are perhaps meant; comp. יצא צפע shall come forth a cockatrice (14:29). Since he is said to be the father, the men of Yehudah are as it were his sons, and the women his daughters. All vessels of small quantity. The children are compared to small vessels.
האגנות The cups. (Comp. 24:6). The gold was perhaps kept in those vessels.
כלי הנבלים. The vessels of psalteries. Musical instruments. Nothing will remain in the royal palace, that should not be placed under his authority.
The nail, etc. Shevna, who thought himself a nail fixed in a strong place.
The burden that is upon it. The supporters of his government.
Tzor. A town near the sea; it was conquered by Nevuchadnetzar.
כי שרר מבית מבוא For it is laid waste, that there is no house, no entering in. For every house in Tzor is destroyed, that no merchants come there any more.

From the land of Chittim. Even from the land of Chittim, which is very far, this destruction was announced to the ships of Tarshish. Chittim is mentioned, because of the ships which passed the coast thereof. Comp. (Bamidbar 24:25)

Inhabitants of the isle. Inhabitants of Tzor. Whom the merchants of Zidon, etc. Although Tzor was full of merchants from Zidon, etc. Zidon. A town likewise on the sea; comp. Zevulun shall dwell at the haven of the sea, etc., and his border shall be unto Zidon (Bereshit 49:13)
And by great waters, etc. The merchants brought to Tzor the seed of the Sihor, and her increase was the harvest of the Yeor.

סחר A mart. סחר is a noun and means merchandise; but we have here to supply בעלת; And she was the mistress of the merchandise (that is, the mart) of the nations. Comp. ובעל חסרון ═ וחסרון That which is wanting (Kohelet 1:15)
The sea. She that had the greatest power on the sea, that is Tzor. I travailed not, etc. It is as if there were no people in the isle of Tzor.
And at the report, etc. As at the report of the defeat of Mitzrayim every one was startled, so they will be startled at the report of the fall of Tzor.
אל תרשיש ═ תרשישה To Tarshish.
כל אי ═ אי Every island.
Is this your joyous city, etc. Is this Tzor, that was a rejoicing to you—Comp. a rejoicing to the whole land (Tehillim 48:3)—that old Tzor, that must now see her people go far away into captivity.
המעטירה The crowning city. That was a glory to the islands.
כנעניה Her merchants. Comp. כנען a merchant (Hoshea 12:8)
Hashem of hosts, etc. Hashem, who is the King of hosts has decided this.

עברי ארצך כיאור Pass over to thy land as a river (עברי אל ארצך═עברי ארצך); that is, hasten to thy country, as quickly as the river flows, or, pass through thy land as the river which overflows the country.
מזח Strength. Literally, girdle. (Comp. Tehillim 109:19). It is used as a figure for strength, because a girdle supports the loins.
He stretched out His hand. Hashem stretched out His hand, that is, He brought the punishment.

מעזניה The strongholds thereof. The fortresses of Tzor.—The נ in מעזניה is instead of the Dagesh in the .ז כנען Merchant city. According to some, ארחת כנען ═ כנען, the caravan of Kenaan, because of the feminine pronoun in מעזניהֹ her strongholds.
And He said. And Hashem said.
המעשקה O robbed city. The wealth of her merchants in Tzor will be taken away.
Pass over to Chittim. To trade there.
The land. The inhabitants of the land.
This people. The people of the Chaldæans.

לא היה There was none like them. Comp. לא היה פחד There was no fear like it (Tehillim 53:6). According to others: Would that it were not; for it founded the kingdom of Ashur for wild beasts, that is, the Chaldsæans laid Ashur waste, and it became the habitation of wild beasts. לציים For the little wild beasts that live in the land. They set up the towers thereof etc. Although they, viz., the Ashur, have set up the towers for defence, etc.

בחוניו The towers thereof. Comp. בוחן tower (32:14). More correctly, the suffix in בחוניו refers to the people of the Chaldæans: when they, viz., the Chaldæans, set up their towers of siege. עוררו They raised up. It is a transitive verb. The palaces thereof. It was as if the towers stirred up the palaces, but before they awoke, he brought her to ruin, that is, the Chaldæan brought Ashur to ruin.
Ships of Tarshish. Ships that go from Tarshish to Tzor with goods.
ונשכחת And shall be forgotten. ונשכחה ═ ונשכחת; comp. ושבה ═ ושבת And it will return (Ez. 46:17).
The days of one king. The reign of Nevuchadnetzar, his son, and grandson are considered as one.
Shall Tzor sing as an harlot. Tzor will again be active in words and deeds.

Take up an harp, etc. The forgotten harlot walks about the city playing, that she may be remembered again; thus Tzor will send letters to all her neighbours, that the merchants may again come to her as before.
And it shall come to pass after the end of seventy years, when that aforementioned time will come.
לאתננה To her hire. Comp. אתנן זונה, hire of an harlot (Devarim 23:19), the money for her whoredom.
And shall commit fornication with all the kingdoms. They will come to her for merchandise.
And her merchandise, etc. Of her profits she will sanctify a part to the Lord.
לא יאצר It shall not be treasured up. It shall not be put in the storehouse ולא יחסן .(אוצר) Nor laid up. It will not be put away in a strong place (חוסן).
To them that dwell before Hashem. To the exiles of Yerushalayim, when they will return in the days of Koresh.
To eat sufficiently. The exiles will be satisfied.
וּלְמִבְסֶה ═ וְלִמְבַסֶּה And for a clothing.
עתיק Durable. Strong; comp. עתק strength (Shmuel I 2:3).

Some ask, How can the prophet promise that the hire of the harlot Tzor will be sanctified to the Lord, since the Law prohibits the hire of an harlot to be brought to the house of the Lord? (Devarim 23:19). The reply to this question is, that the Law prohibits the real hire of an harlot, but the prophet uses the words, her hire, in a figurative sense; in reality, he does not speak of an harlot at all.
בוקק. He maketh empty. Comp. Hos. x. i.
ובולקה And maketh it waste. This word is met with a second time in the book of the vision of Nachum (Nachum 3:10).
ועוה And turneth it upside down.

And it shall be, etc. All men shall be alike in this catastrophe. כעם ככהן וגו׳. As with the people, so with the priest. etc. When two nouns with the prefix כ follow each other, the phrase is elliptical; the complete sentence would be: as with the people so with the priest, and as with the priest so with the people, as with the servant so with the master, and as with the master so with the servant, etc.
כמלוה As with the lender, as with him who gives away money without security.
נושה The capitalist.
אשר נושה בו He who borrows money on security.

הבוק תבוק. Shall be utterly emptied. Comp. בוקק (ver. 1); הבוק is infinitive Niphal of a verb בקק) ע״ע to empty). חבוק is formed like יסוב is driven back (Tehillim 114:3.) הבוז תבוז Shall be utterly spoiled. The same.—Since Hashem decreed this, there will not remain to man any cause to exalt himself above his fellow.
The earth mourneth, because the King of Ashur has destroyed many countries.

נבלה Fadeth away. Niphal of בלל, to confound; comp. ונבקה, and it will be emptied (19:3); ונסבה and it will be surrounded (Ez. 41:7); the second נבלה might, however, be the Kal of נבל, to fade; comp. נבול תבול, thou wilt surely wear away (Shemot 18:18).
יושבי מרום═מרום they that sit on high, the chiefs of the land.
תורות The laws. The laws which are dictated by common sense, in which all agree.
חלפו They have abolished. Comp. יחלוף, he shall abolish (2:18).
חק Ordinance. The laws of Hashem, contained in the natural order of things; and this is likewise the meaning of ברית עולם, the covenant of the universe.

באלה ═ אלה By a curse; comp. בששת ═ ששת, in sin (Shemot 20:11); according to others, the preposition תחת, for, is to be supplied; comp. פ׳ שפ׳ ונ׳ תחת ═ ונשלמה פרים שפתינו. And let us bring our lips (that is, the words of our lips, our prayer) instead of bulls (Hoshea 14:2).
חרו They are burned. Comp. וחרה, and may be burnt (Ez. xxiv. II).
The new wine mourneth, etc. Because there is none to dress the vine and to dig the ground.
The merry-hearted. For wine maketh glad the heart (Tehillim 104:15)
The mirth of tabrets ceaseth, from the feasts.
The noise of them that rejoice, when they are drunk.
They shall not drink wine with a song, for the strong drink shall be bitter. יֵמַר is according to my opinion a verb ע״ע—comp. וָאֵקַל And I was despised (Bereshit 16:5)—Niphal of מרר
The city of vanity. The city whose inhabitants go after vain things.
Every house is shut up, that no man can come in. For every one will go out into the streets because of the great trouble.
צוחה A crying.
על מקום היין ═ על היין In the place of wine.
In the streets. Publicly.
ערבה Is darkened. Comp. עֶרֶב evening.
ושאיה And with destruction. שאיה is a noun derived from שאה to be waste;comp. שואה desolation (10:3).
In the city is left desolation. This phrase is used by the prophet improperly; comp. Better is he than both they, who hath not yet been (Kohelet 4:3).
בנקף As the shaking. נקף is similar in meaning to ונקף and he shall cut down (10:34).
As the gleaning grapes, that is, only a few; for when the vintage is over, the gleaning grapes are left.

They shall lift up, etc. All commentators agree that from the words, Behold, Hashem maketh, etc. (ver. 1), the prophet refers to the remote future, to the war of Gog and Magog; only R. Moshe Hakkohen refers this prophecy to the king of Ashur, and finds in a feast of fat things (25:6) the indication of the destruction of the hosts of Sancheriv, which remains the subject of the prophecy until the words, Woe to the crown of pride, etc. (28:1).—
They shall lift up, etc., they that escaped, etc.

ירנו They shall shout. Comp. הרנה the proclamation (Melachim I 22:36). They shall cry aloud from the sea. They that go on the sea, shall cry, etc. צהלו They shall cry aloud. Comp. צהלת הסום the neighing of the horse.
באורים Some explain it, In the countries; comp. כשרים אור the land of the Chaldæans (Bereshit 11:31); others: In valleys. The former explanation is the right one.
שם The name. Supply כבדו glorify; for the verb כבדו in the first half of the sentence refers also to the second. They (ver. 14) can also be explained to refer to the righteous.
מכנף From the uttermost part. The word כנף corner, is used here to signify a great distance, because the earth is round.
צבי Glory. The word is derived from a Chaldaic root. And I said. Each nation will say so. Have we heard, etc. The same.
רז׳ Leanness. Comp. רזון leanness (Tehillim 106:15). The repetition indicates that these words are said every moment.
בגדים בגדו וגו׳ Treacherous dealers have dealt treacherously, etc. For all people deal treacherously again and again.
Fear and the pit, etc. And therefore the evil is come to all people; for when any person is in fear, and a kind of pit is near him, and his foot is besides caught in a snare, he must instantly fall.
Windows from on high, etc. A figure for decrees of the Lord.
רעה Is broken. Comp. תרועם thou wilt break them (Tehillim 2:9); a word found frequently in the Targum.
פור התפוררה Is broken asunder. Comp. ויפרפרני and he hath broken me asunder (Iyov 16:12); פוררת thou hast divided (Tehillim 74:13)
The earth shall reel, etc. The inhabitants of the land will flee from one place to the other, and be moved like the cottage of the watchman; for the watchman changes the place of his abode.
And shall be heavy, etc. When they will be about to move and to flee, their transgression will be too heavy for them, and they will fall.
קום To rise. It is infinitive; comp. אלקום no rising up (Mishlei 30:31 ).

Many refer this prediction to an eclipse of the sun and moon; but more correctly it is referred to the angels, that are ready to assist or to attack a nation. Comp. Daniel 10:13, 20. These words are therefore followed by: the kings of the earth on the earth; for the reign of the kings is in connexion with the reign of the angels.

באסיר ═ אסיר As a prisoner. As prisoners are gathered, etc. As people who are brought to the prison to be shut in are often left there for a long time before they are visited to be supplied with their food. The idea contained in this simile is, that this evil will last a long time. יפקדו they shall be visited, may also be compared with ומימים רבים תפקד and after many years thou wilt be visited (Ez. 38:8), and explained in an evil sense.

Then the moon, etc. Sun and moon, the rulers of heaven, are used here in a figurative sense for the kings of the earth, who will be ashamed; but it is also possible that an eclipse of sun and moon is meant by the prophet. The kingdom of Hashem will then appear on the mount of Tziyon, and honour will be given to those that remain faithful to Hashem. According to others this passage refers to the worshippers of the heavenly bodies; but this explanation is at variance with the context.
My God. The first person singular refers to the prophet, or these are the words which every one of the ancients is represented speaking (24:23).
עצות מרחוק Counsels of old. Objective case governed by עשית thou hast done.—The counsels of oldare the plans of God predicted by the prophets.
אמונה אמן With faithfulness and truth. As to the repetition אמונה אמן comp. עזי ומעזי my strength and my fortress (Yirmiyahu 16:19).
For thou hast made a city an heap, etc. Many cities will be destroyed, when Gog and Magog will come. According to R. Moshe Hakkohen it refers to the period of Sancheriv.
לגל An heap. Comp. Bereshit 31:51.
זרים Strangers. Non-Israelites.
מעיר Of every city.
יכבדוך עם עז Shall a strong people glorify thee. Those who have escaped or are far off shall glorify thee, when they will hear the report.

For thou hast been, etc. It is wonderful how all well fortified towns were taken, and the city of the poor, that is, Yerushalayim, escaped. A refuge from the showers, from the enemy who is compared to showers of water.
For the blast of the terrible ones is as showers against the wall. This phrase is to explain the expression from the showers.
בציון In a dry place. Comp. בארץ ציה in a dry land (Yirmiyahu 2:6).
חורב בצל עב ונו׳ The heat in the shadow of a cloud, etc. Repetition of the same idea.
בצל עב In the shadow of a cloud, that is, in the shadow which hides the clouds and makes them invisible.
זמיר עריצים The song of the terrible ones. It is the same as שאון זרים; comp. זמירות songs (24:16).
יענה Shall be low. It is an intransitive verb of the same root as עני poor (Devarim 24:12); לענות to be humbled (Shemot 10:3)
In this mountain. In Tziyon.
A feast of fat things, etc. God will feed them with fat things,
ממחים with things full of marrow—comp. ומוח and the marrow (Iyov. 21:24); ממחים is participle Pual—
and then he will give them to drink lees well refined, so that they will become drunk; comp. As you have drunk on my holy mountain, etc. (Ovadyah 16)
ובלע And he shall discover. Comp. כבלע when are discovered (Bamidbar 4:20).
הלוט The covering. Comp. וילט and he wrapped (Melachim I 19:13); it is the same as the corresponding מכסה ═ מסכה covering; comp. והמסכה and the covering (28:20)
בלע המות Death will destroy them.
And the Lord will wipe away tears from off all faces. For they have caused great evils to all.
ואמר And they will say. The people mentioned before, will say.
ויושענו And he saved us. And he saved us continually. It is the imperfect tense.
The hand of Hashem. His punishment.
Moav, that will come to help the besiegers of Tziyon.
ונדוש And shall be trodden down. Niphal of a verb (דוש) ע״ו or בְּהִדּוּשׁ .(דשש) ע״ע As is trodden down. Infinitive Niphal; וּ is here instead of וֹ; these two vowels are capable of interchange.
מדמנה Dunghill.
And he shall spread forth. Hashem shall spread forth. In the midst of them. In the midst of Moav.
השוחה He that swimmeth. Comp. שחו to swim (Ez. 47:5).
His pride. The pride of Moav.
ארבות Hap. leg.; the meaning must be found from the context. Some compare it with ארבות windows (Bereshit 7:11), but their explanation is far-fetched.
Thy walls. The pronoun refers to Moav.

השח השפיל He brought down, he laid low. Asyndeton; comp. כרע שכב נפל He bowed, he fell, he lay down (Shoftim 5:27). The past is used here because the action was already completed in the time of Sancheriv.
עיר עז לנו ישועה ישית To a city which is strength to us, he will appoint salvation. To Yerushalayim, which is strength unto us, God will appoint salvation.
חומות וחל For walls and bulwarks. חֵל הַחוֹמוֹת ═ חֵל the fence of the walls.
Open ye gates, etc. The gates of that city should only be opened for righteous people like Bnei Yisrael, to enter and to dwell in it.
יצר סמוך תצר שלום Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on thee. Others are of opinion that שלום may be used as masculine and feminine.
Trust ye, etc. Therefore fathers will say to their children, Trust in the Lord, etc.
ביה In the Lord. ב is a preposition, and has its usual meaning.

צור עולמים Everlasting strength. ביה In some books all the letters of the Alphabet are combined with this word (יה), which consists of one-half the number of letters composing the full name of Hashem, in order to form new names for the Divine Being. In the book of Tehillim (68:5) I shall explain this.
השח He bringeth down. A verb ע״ע like הֵקַל he afflicted slightly (8:23). Them that dwell on high, etc. This refers to the heathens.
ישפילנה ישפילה He layeth it low, he layeth it low. He will continually lay it low; comp. עזי ומעזי My strength and my fortress (Yirmiyahu 16:19).
The foot shall tread it down, etc. He will bring it so low, that it will be trodden not by the foot of the noble but by that of the poor.
רגלי ═ פעמי feet. Comp. פעמים (Shemot 23:14) ═ רגלים (ibid. 17) times.
The way of the just, etc. And why is all this? because there is no path for the righteous but that of rectitude,
and Thou, O Hashem, art most upright and dost weigh the path of the just.
תפלס Thou weighest.

We waited for thee, O Hashem, even for the way of Thy judgment, etc. These are the words of the righteous that hope in Hashem, that He will show His judgment in the universe; for the soul is longing for Thy name. Before ארח path supply the preposition ל for.
נפשי My soul, that is, the thought of my soul, was בלילה אויתיך I have desired Thee in the night;
Yea the thought of my spirit within me, was אשחרך I will seek Thee early. Man has נפש soul and רוח spirit, as I explained in Kohelet.
When Thy judgments are, etc. When Thy judgments appear on the earth the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
תבל World. The inhabited part of the earth.

יחן Let favour be shewn. A verb ע״ע; it is a form like יוסב is turned (28:27).—Hashem is merciful to the wicked, but they will not learn righteousness; He has patience with them for a long time, they might perhaps improve.
In the land of uprightness. In the place where the people are upright, they (the wicked) will do wrong.
נבחות Straightforwardness. It is related to נכח before (Shemot 26:35); comp. נכחים right (Shmuel II 15:3). And will not behold, etc. He does not wish to consider the greatness of Hashem.

רמה ידך בל יחזיון When Thy hand is lifted up they will not see. יחזו ויבשו קנאת עם But they shall see and be ashamed for their envy at the people; let them show their envy of Thy people, and be ashamed, אף אש צריך תאכלם And let the fire devour Thine enemies. Some explain the former phrase thus: Let them see Thy punishment inflicted upon all of them. According to this explanation, the phrase has the same meaning as the words אף אש צריך תאכלם yea, even the fire, which shall devour thine enemies.
תשפות Thou wilt ordain. Comp. שפות set on (Ez. 24:3).
For thou also hast wrought, etc. For Thou hast always done for us what we do not know how to do.

Other lords, besides Thee, have had dominion, etc. For we worshipped Thee even when others became our masters. בעלונו Had dominion over us, were our masters (בעלים); comp. לבעליו unto the owner of them (Shemot 21:34). But by Thee only we make mention of Thy name. Nevertheless we praised Thy name. לבד בך But by Thee. Thou hast helped us, therefore we were able to praise Thee.
