They are dead. Those our masters, that have owned us, are now dead.
יספת Thou hast continued. Thou hast removed it far unto all the ends of the earth. The more Thou hast chastised Thy people, the more they acknowledged Thy glory, even when exiled from their country.
In trouble. In their trouble.

צקון They poured out. The נ is paragogic, as in ידעון they knew (Devarim 8:3); the word is besides irregular; the regular form is יצקו; the first radical is dropped in צקון; comp. ירד═רד he went down (Shoftim 19:11). As to the phrase they poured out a prayer, comp. he will pour out his prayer (Tehillim 102:1).
מוסרך למו Thy chastening upon them. They mention in their prayer the punishment which thou hast inflicted upon them.
Like as a woman, etc. This verse describes the chastening mentioned in the preceding verse.
תקריב That draweth near Lit. that bringeth near, namely, herself.

We have conceived, we have been in pain with, as we have brought forth, wind. We have conceived, and we have been in pain with wind, and so we have also brought forth wind. We had no strength to deliver ourselves; this is the meaning of the following ישועות בל נעשה we have not wrought any deliverance. We were not able to bring any deliverance.
ארץ In the earth. Supply ב; comp. בששת═ששת (Shemot 20:11).

ובל יפלו Some say, that א is omitted, as in ויפלו (Nechemyah 6:16); but the latter has its usual meaning (and they fell), as will be explained by me. I explain בל יפלו we could not help their falling.

Thy dead men shall live. Only Thy dead men shall live; Hashem is addressed. Generally, it is believed, that this phrase contains some reference to the resurrection of the dead. Some explain it as a contrast to They are dead, they will not live, (ver. 14), they, that is, our masters, are dead, but we, who were considered as dead, are living.

My dead body. The first person refers to the prophet, who is one of Bnei Yisrael, that are considered as dead. Let Thy dead men live, and let the dead of my people rise, as if they heard the cry: Awake, etc.

טל אורות A dew of light. A dew acccompanied by light. Thy dew. Hashem is addressed in these words. According to others, אורות means herbs; comp. Melachim II 4:39; it signifies a kind of herb, which turns toward the sun and moon.

וְהָאָרֶץ ═ וָאָרֶץ. And the earth Shall cast out the dead, out of itself. תפיל Shall cast out, shall bear; comp. כנפל אשח As the untimely birth of a woman (Tehillim 58:9). Others explain, Thou alone hast given life to Thy dead; for it is the nature of the earth to throw the dead into its midst.
Come, my people, etc. R. Moshe Hakkohen explains this verse to mean that the people shall shut themselves in Yerushalayim, because of Sancheriv.

חבי Some explain this word as a regular form of a verb (חבה) ל״ה; the feminine form חבי is used, because עם is sometimes feminine; comp. וחטאת עמך And thy people sinneth (Shemot 5:16). R. Jehudah, the Grammarian, says, that חבי is a noun like שבי captivity. The first explanation is the right one.
Hashem cometh out. The decrees of Hashem come out.
Her blood. The slain, that are buried in the earth.
ביום ההוא In those days.
The Lord shall visit. As mentioned in the preceding verse.
Livyatan. The Theli ; (תלי) it has the epithet בריח stretching, because it stretches from one end to the other. [I think it is a sea monster].
Even Livyatan, that crooked serpent. This is likewise an animal that lives in the sea; it is like a serpent, for there are also serpent-like animals in the sea. עקלתון Crooked. It is an adjective.
And the dragon that is in the sea. That is, The great dragon in the sea. (Ez. 29:3).

Some are of opinion that the Livyatan, the stretching serpent, and the Livyatan, the crooked serpent, are both land animals, and are used figuratively for the kings of the land; while the dragon that is in the sea, is used for the king of Mitzrayim (Comp. Ez. 29:3), or as others believe, for the king of Tzor. R. Moshe Hakkohen thinks, that this verse refers to the élite of soldiers, princes, and nobles.
חמר Wine Comp. חָמֶר wine (Devarim 32:14). A vineyard of wine. A vineyard that yields a large quantity of wine.
ענו Sing. Comp. ענות Singing (Shemot 32:18).
Unto her. Unto Tziyon. The imperative sing is addressed to the singers. The prophet has said already, that Yehudah is the pleasant plant of Hashem (5:7)
I, the Lord, do keep it, that is to say, the Divine glory remains in Tziyon.

I will water it every moment. The prophecy will not cease. פן יפקד. R. Yonah, the Grammarian, says, that לא ═ פן, and פן יפקד עליה ;אפקד ═ יפקד means accordingly, I will not punish her (though I shall punish all other nations). Comp. פן תפלס Do not ponder. R. Isaak ben Shaul compares יפקד with נפקד there lacketh (Bamidbar 31:49), and joins this with the preceding phrase in this way, I will water it every moment, lest its leaves drop.
עליה Its leaves. Each of its leaves. Comp. 1:30. R. Moshe Hakkohen explains it thus, I shall guard it day and night, lest the enemy hurt it. I think that this explanation is the right one.
Fury is not in me, etc. Some say that this verse is the continuation of the words of Hashem. Fury is not in me, that is, great fury is not in me.

Who would set, etc. Anthropomorphism. Supply ב before שמיר brier, comp. בששח═ששח in six, (Shemot 20:11). The meaning of the sentence is, Who would set me against the brier and thorn of the vineyard, that is, against the wicked people; and in the day of my war against the vineyard, אפשעה בה I would go through it;—comp. כפשע but a step (Shmuel I 20:3)—
אציתנה I would burn it;—comp. הציתו they have burnt (Shmuel II 14:35)
Or let him take hold, etc. Or let Bnei Yisrael take hold of my strength, then I shall not have war with them—comp. Hashem hath been like an enemy (Eichah 2:5)—
nor with other nations, for the sake of Yisrael; this double peace is indicated by the repetition of the words he will make peace unto me.

R. Moshe Hakkohen explains these two verses in the following way: Fury is not in me, what I am going to say, I shall not say with fury. מי יתנני וגו׳ Who would give me—comp. נתתני thou hast given me (Shoftim 1:15)—the briers and thorns of the vineyard! I would go through them, etc.; that is, if they do not remove the wicked men of Yisrael, I will slay them all; or let him take hold of my strength, etc., then Yaakov shall take root.—

I think that Hashem is not represented as speaking in these two verses, as is the case in many passages of this book—we need only refer to the preceding chapter, verses 18 and 19—but the men of Yehudah, after having heard Hashem’s promise, I Hashem will keep it, lest he visit it, are introduced, saying, We do not declare with fury, that if the enemy should come to turn the vineyard into a place of briers and thorns, we should kill ourselves. Comp. And Yechezkel shall be, instead of And I shall be (Ez. 25:24), And Shmuel, instead of And myself (Shmuel I 12:11); As he hath done, instead of As I have done (Vayikra 8:34); במלחמה in war, is to be joined with מי יתנני who would turn me in this way: If one should come to turn me by war into a place of briers and thorns, etc. או יחזק Or if He would strengthen my stronghold, etc., to give me the strengthening promise that He will be in peace with me, and so should the enemy be, then Yaakov would take root, etc. I am compelled to explain in this way by the phrase, He will make peace unto me, because it is Hashem alone that maketh peace.
.בהבאים ═ הבאים In future. According to some: the children.
ישרש He shall cause to take root. Comp. ישרשיח ותשרש and didst cause it to take deep root (Tehillim 80:10).
תנובה. Fruit.
Hath he smitten him, etc. This prophecy refers to the fall of Shomron, to which alone the expression אשרים groves can be applied.
Those that smote him. The Ashur.
Of them that are slain by him. Of the Kenaani that were slain when Bnei Yisrael conquered their country. Hashem did not smite Bnei Yisrael in the same way as he smote the Kenaani.
בסאסאה. In measure. According to most commentators בסאסאה is a reduplication of סאה measure, like ירקרק green (Vayikra 13:49); מטלטלך Will carry thee away (22:17).
Thou wilt debate with it, with Shomron; comp. the defenced city (ver. 10).

בשלחה According to some: with its sword. The meaning of the sentence accordingly is: Shomron destroyed itself with its own instruments of war. Comp. השלח the sword (Yoel 2:8). More correctly, however, it may be compared with שלחיך thy plants (Shir Hashirim 4:13), especially because of the words: on the day of the east wind. Shomron was punished with her own measure, she had quarrelled even with the people of her own villages,—which may be considered as her plants (שלחה)—therefore. הגה Hashem removed her; comp. הוגה he was removed (Shmuel II 20:13); ה replaces the radical י; as in ידה═הדה he stretched forth (11:8).
קדים East wind.

By this, therefore, shall the iniquity of Yaakov be purged, etc. That is, no evil shall befall him—for the iniquity of Yaakov (עון יעקב) is the source of all his evils—and the decree shall be rescinded, if they abolish idolatry.
הסר To take away. Infinitive.
The altar of Ba'al.
גיר Chalk.
מנפצות Beaten in sunder. Comp. תנפצם Thou shalt break them (Tehillim 2:9).
לא יקמו Shall not stand. Shall not remain.
The defenced city. Shomron. בדד Shall be desolate.
סעפיה The branches thereof. Comp. על שתי הסעפים upon the two branches (Melachim I 18:21). The open towns are meant.
קצירה The bough thereof. Comp. בקצירי In my branch (Iyov. 29:19).
They shall be broken off. The pronoun they refers to פארות the smaller branches, while קציר signifies the large branch.

מאירות Some explain: Collect; comp. אריתי I have gathered (Shir Hashirim 5:1). Even the women that have no strength will break and gather them. Others: Set on fire. The branches will be used as fuel. This is the right explanation. Comp. תאירו ye kindle fire (Malachi 1:10)
ביום ההוא In those days.
יחבט Shall beat off. Comp. תחבט thou wilt beat (Devarim 24:10); חובט beating (Shoftim 6:11); therefore the expression תלקטו you will be gathered together is also used.
One by one. Only a few will be left out of many.
And it shall come to pass in that day, etc. Then all the children of Efraim that are in exile will hasten to return to Yerushalayim, seeing that their own kingdom has ceased to exist.
The drunkards of Efraim. The princes indulged in wine.
צבי Beauty. Comp. 4:2.
Crown. The royal crown, the king.

ראש The best. Comp. ראשי בשמים the chief spices (Shir Hashirim 4:14). ניא שמנים Valley of oil. There was so much of it, that it was like a valley full of oil. Comp. בגיא in the valley (Devarim 3:29). Others compare נֵּיא with נֵּא proud (16:6), and say that the radical ה is omitted.
הלומי Overcome. Comp. הלמוני they have smitten me (Mishlei 23:35)
חזק Mighty. Attribute to יום day, or חיל host, which is to be supplied.
שער קטב. The כ in כזרם refers also to שער: As a destroying wind.
קטב Destruction. Comp. קטבך thy destruction (Hoshea 13:14).
הניח לארץ He cast down to the earth. Hashem sent those storms and caused them to visit the earth. ביד With the hand. With His mighty hand.
עטרת Crown. Singular form but plural sense; there are many instances of this usage.
ציצת נובל The blooming of the blossom which will fade away,—comp. בת בבל השדודה O daughter of Bavel, who art to be destroyed (Tehillim 137:8)—or the blossom of the fading plant, and this is better.
כבכורה As the hasty fruit. As the fig that ripens before any of the summer fruit comes.
In that day, etc. This will be just the reverse of the fate of the crown of Efraim; for the kingdom of Hashem will appear in Tziyon.
To him that sitteth in judgment. To the judges. God will strengthen them. אל השער ═ שערה.

To the gate. שערה משיבי מלחמה. Some explain: who turn the battle away from the gates. R. Moshe Hakkohen renders the passage thus: (Hashem will give strength to those) who have escaped, and this is the right explanation.
They also, etc. There are also some of the men of Yehudah that have erred through wine, etc.
The priest, whose duty it is to teach; the prophets, whose duty it is to exhort the people.
בראה In the words of the prophet, who rebukes the people; בדברי הראה ═ בראה.

פקו פליליה, they pervert judgment; by the subject they the judges are meant, and the verb פקו has a transitive meaning; or the words of the judgment are unstable, דברי the words of being supplied. I prefer this latter explanation; for פקו is intr.; comp. ופיק ברכים, and the tottering of the knees. (Nachum 2:11.
For all tables are full of vomit, etc. This is usually the case with drunken people.
בלי מקום So that there is no place, which is not full, etc.; comp. עד אפס מקום until there be no place, (5:8). קיא צואה Asyndeta. They are covered with filthiness from the top to the bottom.
Whom shall he teach knowledge, etc. When the prophet is about to reprove them, no one understands him; for because of the wine they have not their reason; they are like little children.
שמועה Doctrine. A noun.
גמולי Those that are weaned. This form can be both the absolute state of the noun as well as the construct; comp. השכוני באהלים they that dwell in tents (Judg. viii., 11).
עתיקי Drawn. An adjective of the same root as ויעתק and he removed (Gen. xii., 8)
For precept must be upon precept, etc. One must speak to them in the same way as the father speaks to his little child, that does not yet know much.
צו לצו Precept after precept, or precept joined to precept.
קו לקו Line after line. This is just the way how writing is taught.
Here a little and there a little. Little by little, gradually.
בלעני שפה With laughing lips. Comp. לענ derision (Ps. lxxix., 4). The teacher speaks to the child in a laughing and mocking way.

And with another tongue. The teacher usually tries to substitute letters which are easy to pronounce for the more difficult ones; in the same manner the prophet must speak, when he rebukes this people.
He said. The prophet said.
This is the rest, etc. Yerushalayim is the place of your rest; there procure rest for the weary; he shall not take refuge in Ashur or Mitzrayim.
המרנעה The refreshing. Comp. מרגוע rest (Iyov 6:16); both words are substantives. According to the grammarian of Yerushalayim מרגעה is a participle.
אבו ═ אבוא They would. Comp. ההלכו ═ ההלכוא who went (Jos. 10:24)

But the word of Hashem was unto them, etc. They indeed thought that the word of Hashem itself was of no importance; it was only a school-exercise to them. That they might go to Mitzrayim. Comp. Woe to those that go down to Mitzrayim, etc. (31:1), a portion of this same prophecy.
Ye scornful men, that say mockingly, that the words of Hashem are like precept upon precept, etc.
מושלי According to some, they that rule; comp. ממשלה dominion; but better, the poets; comp. המשלים they that speak in proverbs (Bamidbar 21:27)
We have made a covenant with death. We shall not die now.

חזה An agreement. R. Moshe Hakkohen says that חזות (ver. 18) signifies a kind of prophecy; but how can he apply this explanation to the phrase ?עשינו חזה I think that חזה means prophet, and explain עשינו חזה to be the same as עשינו ברית חזה We have made a prophet’s covenant, a covenant like that made by divine inspiration.
שוט שוטף An overflowing scourge, that is, famine; or better, the scourge of an overflowing stream; שוט נחל שוטף ═שוט שוטף.
כי Although. Comp. Tehillim 41:5
הנני יִסַּד I will lay the foundation. יסד is an adjective, derived from a Piel like אִבַּד he hath destroyed (Eichah 2:9). Comp. ושבח אני and I praise (Koh. 4:2); which is likewise transitive.
בחן Tower. Comp. ובוחן and towers (32:14). Tziyon will be protected against the King of Ashur.

מוסד מוסד A sure foundation. The first מוסד is a noun, meaning foundation; it is a genitive, governed by the preceding noun יקרת the value of; the second is a participle Hophal, like מוסב; the ס has therefore a Dagesh, as a substitute for the omitted silent letter (ו).
Shall not make haste. For this prophecy refers to a very remote future.

To the line, to the plummet. The figure, taken from the line and plummet of the builders, is used because of the words I will lay the foundation. Some are of opinion that Chizkiyahu is meant by the tried stone.
ויעה ברד And the hail shall sweep away. Comp. היעים the shovels. ברד the hail is the subject to יעה, which is a transitive verb; by hail the King of Ashur is here meant.
וסתר מים ישטפו. Repeat כזב falsehood after וסתר; And the waters shall overflow the hiding-place of falsehood; or supply אלה these: And the waters will overflow the unstable hiding-place.
וכפר And shall be disannulled. Comp. יכפרנה he will pacify it, that is, will annul or remove it. וברית חזותכם═וחזותכם And your prophetical agreement.
והייתם Then you shall be.
The ו has the same force as فَ in Arabic; comp. וישא ביום השלישי on the third day, then Avraham lifted up (Bereshit 22:4)
That it goeth forth. That the overflowing river goeth forth.

זועה Vexation. It is not the same as זעוה (Devarim 28:25), with transposition of letters, as many think; but it is derived from זוע to tremble, to move; comp. ולא זע and he moved not (Est. 5:9); the ו in the middle is analogous to the ו of מָוֶת death. The meaning of the whole phrase is: Whoever hears of you, of what has befallen you, will be afraid.
המצע The mattress, which is underneath in the bed.
מהשתרע than that a man can stretch himself on it. Comp. שרוע superfluous too long (Vayikra 22:23).
המכסה═המסכה The covering.
בהתכנס It is Infinitive of כנס to assemble; comp. כנוס gather together (Est. 4:16); and means When many gather together under it. The figure refers to the people and its rulers.
As in mount Perazim, known by the wars of David (Shmuel II 5:20); the place was called בעל פרצים place of breaches, because the Plishtim were suddenly defeated there in a miraculous way.

As in the valley of Givon (Jos. 10:12), where sun and moon stood still. That He may do His work, His strange work. In the same way Hashem will make a strange war against Yisrael, such as was never heard of before.
And bring to pass His act, His strange act. A mere repetition of the preceding idea, not an exceptional instance.
מוסרותיכם ═ מוסריכם Bands.
ונחרצה Even determined. Comp. חרצת thou hast decided (Melachim I 20:40)
Hear my voice, hear my speech. Parallelism.
Doth the plowman, etc. The plowman tills the ground once and twice, and sows, then the earth by its natural power brings forth the increase.
יפתח He opens, וישדד and he breaks the clods, that is, he prepares the field; comp. Hoshea 10:11. יפתח and וישדד are a repetition of the same idea in different words.
שוה He hath made plain. Derived from שוה equal; comp. נשתוה alike (Mishlei 27:15).
קצח A kind of cummin, but smaller and black.
שורה According to some, good; according to others, with measure; comp. במשורה with the measure (Vayikra 19:35), and this is right.
ושערה And barley. It is well known.
נסמן Marked. Comp. סימן sign.
נבלתו In its place. Comp. מגבלות measured (Shemot 28:14)
ויסרו For Hashem instructed him. Hashem has already instructed him, who sows and scatters the seed, and taught him how to do it.
למשפט According to the custom, to do as it is usually done; comp. כמשפט after the manner (Bamidbar 29:32). His Elokim doth teach him. The same.
בחרוץ With a threshing instrument. Comp. 41:15.
יסב Neither is turned about. Repeat לא, the negation of the first part of the verse, before יוסב
Bread corn is bruised. It is customary for bread corn to be bruised.
אדוש To thresh. The א is prosthetic, as in אזרועך thine arm (Yirmiyahu 32:21).

והמם And he turneth, etc. And when he turns the wheel of his cart to till the field, his horsemen will then not break it (the corn), for Hashem has appointed every thing for its proper season; therefore the prophet continues This also cometh from Hashem, namely, that he shall not bruise it always.
הפליא עצה Who is wonderful in counsel.

תושיה הגדיל Who is great in wisdom. R. Moshe Hakkohen derives הושיה from יש substance.—The nature of the earth and the seeds is better than the character of man, who hears the words of the prophet without any profit The reverse is expressed by a similar figure: Let my doctrine drop like rain, as I explained (Devarim 32:2)

Ariel. Yerushalayim. According to some, Ariel is the name of Yerushalayim, on account of the altar therein, which is called הראל and also אריאל Harel and Ariel (Ez. 43:15, 16); for the letters אׄ הׄ וׄ יׄ interchange; according to others, on account of her planet being the lion; but this is absurd.
קרית The city; it is in the construct state; supply אמת of truth, or some similar word: the city of truth,

where David hath dwelt; or the city, where David dwelt, since the whole sentence, with the past tense of a verb, can in this case be considered as a noun in the genitive governed by a preceding substantive; comp. בראשית ברא in the beginning, when Hashem created, etc. (Bereshit 1:1); תחלת דבר וגו׳ the beginning of Hashem’s speaking to Hoshea (Hoshea 1:1).
ספו Add. Comp. לספת to add (Bamidbar 32:14).
חגים Sacrifices.

ינקפו Will cease. It is a neuter verb. It can also be rendered: they shall kill, ינקפו being explained to be a transitive verb with the omission of the subject (הנקפים the men that kill); comp. ויאמר ליוסף and one said to Yosef (Bereshit 48:1)
To Ariel. To Yerushalayim.

תאניה ואניה Heaviness and sorrow. Comp. ואנו and they shall mourn (19:8). According to others, A waste place, the two words being derived from אנה where; the meaning of the phrase is, that only her place will be left.
והיתה לי כאריאל And it shall be unto me as Ariel, as the altar which is desolate of sacrifices, or like an altar, because the inhabitants will be slaughtered.
כדור Suddenly. Comp. 22:18.
מגדל מצב ═ מצב A tower set up.
And thou shalt be brought down. This applies to the words of Chizkiyahu’s messengers to Ravshake.
Thou shalt speak out of the ground. Thou shalt speak so, as if the voice came from the depth of the earth.
כאב As a potter. Comp. כאבת as bottles.—The potter, because of his vocation, speaks from below.
כאבק דק Like small dust. Some word must be supplied, because of אבק being in the construct state.
The multitude of thy strangers. The army of the Ashur. Yet it shall be at an instant, suddenly. All this, mentioned before, shall take place suddenly.
By Hashem, etc. From Hashem will this visitation come against the besiegers.
With thunder from above.
With earthquake below.
With great noise, with storm and tempest, and flame of fire. All this refers to the angel that was sent to destroy the Ashuri army.
Shall be as a dream, etc. It will be like a dream; it causes man to see things by night, which, when he awakes, are no more. This was to be the case with the Ashuri camp.
צובאיה ═ צוביה Her hosts. ואנשי מצודתה ═ ומצודתה And the men engaged in her siege, or And all the towers of the besiegers.
והנה And behold. The word חלום dream, is usually followed by והנה and behold, or as if; the subject to the following אׄכֵל is רָעֵב the hungry.
שוקקה Desirous to drink.

Stay yourselves. The prophet addresses the men of Tziyon who will be curious to know how this will happen, and what the meaning of this prophecy is.—The prophet speaks in the same manner as people use to speak one to another; and why do they still not understand him? because they are drunken, but not with wine.
נסך He has covered. Comp. והמסכה and the covering (28:20). Upon you. Upon the inhabitants of Tziyon.
ויעצם And he closed. Derived from עצם bone; he put, as it were, a bone on your eyes.
כסה He covered. This proves that נסך has also the meaning, he covered.
The vision of all. Every prophecy.
For it is sealed. They cannot understand it; the same meaning is contained in the words, seal the law (8:16), as I explained.
And the book is delivered, etc. Neither the wise men nor those that have no intellect will understand this prophecy.
נגש He vexeth himself. Comp. והנגשים the taskmasters (Shemot 5:13). It is Niph.—They will afflict themselves in vain with fasting.
בפיו With his mouth. With the mouth of each of them.
מלמדה Accustomed. Comp. לא למד unaccustomed, (Yirmiyahu 31:18)

הנני יוסיף Behold I will proceed, comp. ונשאר אני and I am left (Ez. 9:8); אמלל אני I am withering (Tehillim 6:3); אמלל is the third person past, because of the Pathah under ל. Some explain יוסיף to be a participle like תומיך supporting (Tehillim 16:5).

להפליא את העם הזח הפלא ופלא To be very embarrassing to this people, that they shall not understand, that the wisdom of the wise shall be lost, etc. Others explain this phrase thus: To do a marvellous work among this people; comp. עשה פלא who performs wonders (Shemot 15:11). I explain it in the following way: To do to this people a wonderful thing like this.
המעמיקים That seek deep in the depth of their hearts.
להסתיר═לסתיר To hide. Comp. להשמיד═לשמיד to destroy (23:11)
הפככם You are going from the truth.
אם כחמר היוצר יחשב Shall man be esteemed as the potter’s clay.
ויצר And the thing framed. It is derived from יצר to form. ליצרו Of him that framed it. Comp. לי of me (Bereshit 20:13)
מעט A little. A little while, a few days.
And Levanon shall be turned, etc. And the Levanon, that yields more fruit than Karmel, will become like Karmel, and the latter like a forest; that is to say, they will have scanty food.
And in that day shall the deaf hear, etc. Then they will understand the words of the prophecy, and those blind men will not see, until they have already been in darkness.
The meek also shall increase, etc. The righteous will escape, when the fortified towns of Yehudah will be taken, and the judges of Achaz will be no more, as I explained above (1:26).
אפס Is brought to naught. Comp. Bereshit 47:15.
שקדי That watch. Comp. לשקד to watch (Mishlei 8:34)
מחטיאי אדם בדבר That make a man an offender for a word, that watch the words of man, and accuse him, in order to see him punished; or that cause others to sin by their words.

יקושון They lay a snare. Comp. מוקש snare (Devarim 7:16). R. Moshe Hakkohen explains יקושון they rebuke, comparing it with התקששו וקשו be rebuked and rebuke (Tzefanyah 2:1), and says that the ש ought to have a Dagesh.
Who redeemed Avraham, by taking him away from amongst the wicked.
יחורו Shall wax pale. The root חור to be white is frequent in Chaldee.
For when he seeth his children, etc. For when he sees his children, and the good which I shall do to the pious, they—he and his children—shall sanctify my name.

יעריצו They will cause others to fear the God of Yisrael, or they shall be afraid, intransitive. Having mentioned Yaakov, the prophet says metaphorically, they will sanctify, etc. that is to say, if Yaakov were alive and saw his pious children, and the wonders which God performed for their sake, he would join his children in sanctifying His name; for He was the holy one of Yaakov.
ורגנים And they that murmured, comp. יתרגנו and you were murmuring (Devarim 1:27). They are the opposite of those that learn doctrine.
הוי Woe to.
ממני ═ מני Of me. (Comp. 22:4).
ולנסוך מסכה And that cover with a covering. Comp. והמסכה and the covering (28:20). It is figuratively used for counsel.
ולא מרוחי ═ ולא רוחי But not of my spirit, that is, of my prophecy.
That walk to go down, etc. This verse explains the preceding.
במעוז In the strength of. מ retains its vowel, although the word is in the construct state, because of the second and third letter of the root being the same.
והחסות And the trust. A noun; it is the contracted form of חסיות; comp. עבדות slavery (Ezr. 9:8)
שריו His princes. The princes of the people; they sent even their princes to Mitzrayim, that the Mitzrim might deliver Yerushalayim from the Ashur.
כל הוביש═כל הבאיש. The א is superfluous; הבאיש is transitive, Every one blamed those that had gone to Mitzrayim; for they went to a people that would not profit them.

The burden of the beasts of the south. This refers to those that went down to Mitzrayim. South. Mitzrayim, which is in the south of Palestine. The prophet says that, on their way, those messengers would meet wild beasts, as bears, tigers, etc.; this is expressed in the words a lion, a leopard, amongst them an asp, etc.

בארץ צרה In a narrow land, whence they will not be able to escape. They will carry, etc. Those messengers will carry their property on the back of the mules, in order to bring it to Mitzrayim into safety. חיליהם Their property. Comp. החיל the property (Devarim 8:17).
דבשת Bunches. Hap. leg.—The beasts of the south will do them much damage.
לזאת To this. To Yerushalayim. רהב הם שבת Their strength is to sit still. He who remains in Yerushalayim, and will not go down to Mitzrayim, will be strong and safe.
Now go. Now go with them; the prophet has hesitated to be together with them.
חקה Note it. חקה is without Dagesh in ה; some copies have the Dagesh; it is the imperative instead of חוקקה or חוקקהּ or חוקקנה.
כחשים Lying. Adjective of the same form as אִבָּרִים husbandmen; the כ has Segol, on account of the guttural letter which follows.
שמוע Infinitive. To hear.
See not. You shall not prophesy.
לראים To the seers. To those that see a divine vision.
נכחות Upright things. Comp. טובים ונכוחים דבריך thy words are good and upright (Shmuel II 15:3). It is an adjective.
דברי חלקות ═ חלקות words of flattery; חלקות is a substantive; so also דברי מהתלות ═ מהתלות, words of mockery.
Get you out of the way, etc. These words are addressed by the people to the prophets.
Cause the Holy One, etc. Cause the mention or the name of the Holy One of Yisrael to cease, etc.
Ye despise this word, the prophecy.
בעושק In oppression. In the money wrongly taken from the nation.
ונלוז And a perverse thing. נלוז is an adjective; supply דבר thing. Comp. תועבת ח׳ נלוז the perverse (man or thing) is an abomination to Hashem. נלוז is the opposite of ישר upright.
Therefore, because you trust in the money, which you send to the King of Ashur, that he shall not come. This iniquity shall be to you, etc., that is, it will destroy you.
כפרץ מגדל נופל ═ נופל כפרץ As a breach of a falling tower. דבר נבעה ═ נבעה A swelling thing. Of the same root is אבעבועות blains (Shemot 9:9). נבעה can also be joined with פרץ: a swelling breach.
לפתע פתאם Suddenly at an instant. The two words have nearly the same meaning; comp. אדמת עפר the dust of the earth (Daniel 12:12).
נבל Vessel.
He shall not spare, to break it.
לחתות אש To take fire. Comp. יחתה אש he takes fire (Mishlei 6:27). גחלים אתה חותה thou shalt heap coals of fire (ib. 25:22). במכתתו In the bursting of it. Derived from כתת, a verb ע׳ע.
ולחשוף מים And to take water. Lit., to reveal the water, which is hidden. Comp. מחשוף to make appear (Bereshit 30:37); חשף he made bare, (52:10).
גבא Pit. Comp. וגבאיו and its pits. (Ez. 42:11), and גבא, the Chaldæan translation of בור (14:15). This prophecy refers to those that went down to Mitzrayim for assistance.
בשובה In rest. Comp. שובה give rest (Bamidbar 10:36). You will find salvation at home, and you need not go down to Mitzrayim.

ננוס. According to the grammarian R. Yonah: we shall lift ourselves up; he compares it with נֵס banner (that is lifted up), and gives thus to ננוס a meaning similar to that of נרכב we will ride, as required by the parallelism. Others taking ננוס in its usual sense, we shall flee, explain the passage thus: You fled without cause, you will therefore be compelled to flee by your pursuers.
קל The swift. An epithet of the horse, as is כר swift of the camel.

אלף Thousand. It is in the constr. st. אלף אחד The thousand men of one of you; אחד signifies the officer. The meaning of the whole phrase is: An officer over a thousand men will flee at the threatening of one man.
Shall ye flee, shall all of you flee.

Till ye be left as a beacon upon the top of a mountain, etc., till a few out of many will be left. I think that the words as an ensign on a hill refer to those who remained in Yerushalayim and did not go down to Mitzrayim.
Will Hashem wait. An anthropomorphism.

לחננכם That He may be gracious unto you. A verb ע״ע like לחמם to warm (47:14); it is the Kal like לשכב to lie (Bereshit 34:7); all these forms, however, are irregular. And therefore will He be exalted, that He may have mercy upon you, for the Lord is a God of judgment,
He will do judgment on Ashur for your sake.
Thou shalt weep no more, says the prophet to his people, for he will be, etc. Hashem will be gracious unto thee.
לקול זעקך. The ל indicates the cause: At the voice of thy cry, that is, because thou hast cried unto Him.
עָנָ He hath answered thee. It is an irregular form; comp. פֵּאֲרָ He hath glorified thee (55:5).

לחם צר Scanty bread. They were afflicted with famine, as I said before (29:17). מים לחץ The water of affliction. מים is not in the construct state, but מֵי the waters of is to be supplied. מים מי לחץ ═ מים לחץ; comp. שרה האהלה אהל ═ האהלה שרה to the tent, namely to the tent of Sarah. (Bereshit 24:67)

And thine ears, etc. Thou wilt see thy teachers before thee, and hear the words of thy prophets and instructers, that call after thee from behind. Some explain the words thine eyes shall see and thine ears shall hear to express figuratively the seeing and understanding of the heart. תאמינו ═ חימינו; א is substituted for י as is frequently done.
When you turn to the right hand, etc.: When you are about to depart from the right way, either to the right or to the left, you will hear distinctly the words of them that show the right way.
צפוי The covering. A noun.
אפודת The ornament of. The ornamental covering over the image.—
Thou shalt cast them away, for they can be of no use.
דוה A menstruous woman, that is unclean, and whom no clean person may touch.
Then shall he give, etc., that thou shalt sow, after the death of the King of Ashur.
ככר ═ כר (Bereshit 13:10), Plain; comp. בבת עין═בת עין the apple of the eye (Eichah 12:18). In that day shall thy cattle feed, etc. Such will be the abundance of corn and fruit.
The oxen and young asses that ear the ground, that are employed in ploughing the fields. אלפים Oxen. Comp. אלפיך thine oxen (Devarim 7:13).
בליל Provender. Comp. Iyov 6:5.
חמיץ═חמץ Leaven.
אשד זרה Which he winnows. Supply אתי it.
ברחת With the shovel. Derived from רוח wind. It is an instrument used for the same purpose as מזרה the fan.
יבלי Rivers. Comp. יובל river (Yirmiyahu 17:8). And there shall be upon every high mountain, etc. The rain will come in such quantity, that the water will remain upon the mountains.

In the day of great slaughter, etc. When people will die through the fall of towers. It is a kind of consolation to learn, that when ten die, myriads are kept alive: for although the wall might fall upon the widow through the rain, Hashem will not keep it back from coming down and giving life to many; the rain has no knowledge that it should come down upon one place and not at the same time upon the neighbouring ones.

Moreover the light of the moon, etc. All commentators refer this verse to the Messianic period, to the time of the war of Gog and Magog; only R. Moshe Hakkohen is of opinion, that all this part of the book refers to one and the same event. We read e. g. in the next chapter (ver 1.): Woe unto them that go down to Mitzrayim; the same we read above (ver. 2).
The meaning of this verse is, that Hashem will increase the light of the moon and sun after the rain in a wonderful way.
Sevenfold, the prophet himself explains it, as the light of seven days taken together.
In the day that Hashem bindeth up, etc. When Hashem heals the wounds of Yisrael; it refers either to the time of the war of Gog or to the time of the Ashuri dominion.
The name of Hashem, the report of what He has done to the army of Ashur.
From far. From heaven; the angel that smote the Ashur came down from heaven.
משאה Smoke. Comp. המשאת the smoke (Shoftim 20:40); there are many words for smoke.
And His breath. The breath that comes out of His mouth; a figurative expression for the work of the angel.

להנפה. Most of the commentaries say that להנפה is the same as להניף, to wave; but R. Moshe Hakkohen is of opinion, that it means to bridle, and that by the breath of God, the false spirit, described by Michayhu (Melachim I 22:19—23) is to be understood; and this is the right explanation. And there shall be a bridle in the jaws of the people, causing them to err. The bridle is put in the mouth of the horse, to make it go the right way, but the spirit mentioned here, will be רסן מתעה a misleading bridle. The same idea is expressed by ,בנפת שוא and this proves that להנפה has the meaning to bridle.
To you, to Yehudah.
As in the night when a holy solemnity is kept, In the night of the passover. Our sages said therefore, that the Ashuri army was destroyed on the Passover night.
לבוא To come. To be joined with כהולך as when one goeth.
And the Lord shall cause His glorious voice to be heard. The people will be frightened, as they are when they hear the thunder.
ונחת And the lighting down. Comp. ותנחת and it cometh down (Tehillim 38:3).
And shall show to all people.
בזעף With the indignation. The preposition ב governs also the nouns נפץ ,להב, etc.
נפץ With scattering. Comp. תנפצם thou wilt scatter them (Tehillim 2:9).
And hailstones. A figurative expression.
בשבט יכה As if he were smitten with a rod or for Hashem will smite him with a rod.

מוסדה Grounded. Participle Hophal; מטה is sometimes used as a feminine noun; comp. Michah 6:9.—The following is the meaning of the whole verse: And in every place where this rod shall pass, and upon which Hashem shall lay his staff, it will be done. בתפים ובכנרות with tabrets and harps; Hashem will not be weary, but there will be a continual smiting by the angel, who shall rejoice as if he were playing with tabrets and harps.
תנופה Playing. Lit., moving, sc. the hand to play with musical instruments.
מאהמוֹל═מאתמוּל Of old.

תפתה Tophet. The name of a squalid place near Yerushalayim, where all refuse was cast, and whence a continual smoke was rising. The meaning of the sentence is: Tophet is prepared by Hashem for the King of Ashur.
גם הוא למלך הוכן. Yea, for the king it is prepared. For all his officers and princes have already perished. According to others the pronoun הוא refers to the King of Ashur.
מדרתה The pile thereof. Comp. מדורה fireplace (Ez. 24:9).
The breath of Hashem, the breath that cometh out quickly; it expresses figuratively the immediate fulfilment of the divine decrees.
אוי ═ הוי Woe!—Woe unto those that go down to Mitzrayim, that do not see the deliverance that is coming, and go thither in order to be saved, but will in fact perish there.
ולא שעו And they look not. Lit. They do not resign themselves to the mercy of Hashem. Comp. שעו מני turn away from me (22:4); to consider שענו ═ שעו is incorrect.
Yet he also is wise, etc. Hashem also knew their plans, and has brought evil upon them.
לא הסיר He hath not called back.
And not a spirit, that is, not an angel. Comp. ורוחו and His spirit═and His angel (48:16).
His hand. The striking with His hand.
And they all together, Mitzrayim and those that fled thither. The King of Ashur attacked Mitzrayim at the same time that Yerushalayim was threatened by him.
יכליון They shall fail. It is the full form, without dropping the third radical, like יחסיון they trust (Tehillim 36:8)
יהגה He roareth. It is the same in meaning as ישאג.
יקרא עליו מלא רעים אשר When all shepherds are called, one by the other, to join in the fight against the lion.
מלא The full number, all of them, that not one shepherd shall fail to come.
לא יענה He will not abase himself. Root ענה to be poor. Comp. עני poor (Devarim 24:12); לענות to be humble (Shemot 10:3); יענה shall be brought low (25:5).
So shall the Lord of hosts come down, etc. The angel coming down to smite the Ashuri army is meant.

כצפרים As birds. This noun is feminine, although it has the plural termination ־ִים (comp. פילגשים concubines, signifying exclusively a female being, and still with the masculine termination); it is therefore followed by the feminine form עפות flying.
עפות is a participle. Comp. רצות ושבוּת running and returning (Ez. 1:14).
יגן He will cover. Comp. מגן shield (Bereshit 15:1). As the birds cover with their wings their young ones, in order to protect them, so will the Lord, etc.
וְהִצִּיל And to deliver. Although there is a Hirek under the ה, it is nevertheless infinitive.
פסוח To pass over. Comp. ופסח and he will pass over (Shemot 12:23)

Turn ye unto him, etc. The prophet, addressing Yisrael, says: Return, ye Bnei Yisrael, to God, from whom you have deeply revolted. סרה is derived from סרר to revolt. Comp. סורר rebellious (Devarim 21:18)
Your hands. Your workmen.
חטא For a sin; for a sin κατ ἐξοχήν, a sin that surpasses all others.
With a sword, not of a mighty man, but with the drawn sword of an angel. The sword is a figurative expression.
And his young men that will have escaped shall be discomfited, shall be overtaken on the ways in which they try to flee.

And he shall pass by his stronghold, etc. He will go beyond his stronghold at the border of his kingdom, for his great fear; he will flee, and not rely on his strongholds. And his princes, etc. His princes that will have escaped, or will remain in the land, will be afraid of every ensign which they will see.
Fire, furnace. By these names the altar in Yerushalayim is meant; or they are used figuratively, like And the flame of consuming fire (29:6).
Behold a king shall reign, etc. This refers to Chizkiyahu and his princes, the firm establishment of whose government is promised.
ולשרים And princes. The ל has no meaning as far as I know. Comp. לאבשלום (Divrei Hayamim I 3:2), למן (Shemot 9:18).
והיה איש And a man shall be. Either every one of the officers of Chizkiyahu, or Chizkiyahu himself is meant.
מחבא Hiding place. Participle Hiphil.
בציון In a dry place. Comp. ציה dry (41:18).
עיפה Thirsty. Comp. Ps. cxliii.—
The verse may also be explained thus: And Yehudah shall be like one who sitteth in a hiding-place from the wind, etc.
תשעינה Shall be dim. Root שעע. Comp. השע Shut (6:10)
נמהרים The rash. Hasty in a foolish way. It is derived from מהר to be hasty.
עלגים The stammerers. Hap. leg.; in Arabic it means slaves. It is contrasted with to speak plainly (דבר צחות).
צחות Pure words. Supply מלות words; for צחות is an adj., in form and meaning like זכות.
נבל The vile person. Comp. נובלת fading (1:30).

כילי The opposite of שוע. שוע Bountiful. A noble person, whose hands are loose, ready to give, and not closed. Comp. ושוע and turning. Adopting a sort of homiletic explanation, כילי may be said to be composed of two words, כי לי for it belongs to me; for he says, שלי שלי what is mine shall remain mine (Aboth 5:13)
For the vile person, etc. This refers to the officers of Achaz.
תועה Error. It is a noun; the forms of nouns are manifold.
The instruments also, etc. The instruments of justice; for the officers were judges, whose principle was to arrest judgment.
But the liberal. Chizkiyahu and his officers, of whom it was said, And princes shall rule in judgment.
Ye daughters. According to some the towns, which are like the daughters of the metropolis Shomron.
שנה על שנה ═ ימים על שנה. Year after year.

רגזה=רגזנה Be troubled. The opinion of the Nagid is, that רגזה is imperative, referring to the feminine בטחות, although it has a masculine termination; according to R. Moshe Hakkohen it is infinitive.
The gathering of the increase shall not come. Repetition of the same idea.
חרדו Tremble. Imperative masculine. Comp. תעירו ye stir (Shir Hashirim 2:7); תמצאו ye find (Ib. 5:8). It may be considered as an elliptical expression.

רגזה I have explained this word already. פשוטה וערה Strip you and make you bare. These words are to be explained in the same way. וערה And make you bare. Comp. עריה naked (Ez. 16:7). עריה תעור Thy bow will be made quite naked (Chavakuk 3:9). I think that women, daughters (ver. 9), are to be taken literally.
סופדים They shall lament. כל all is to be supplied. Comp. וכל הנשים יתנו and all women shall give. (Est. 1:20)
My people. The people of Shomron.
קוץ שמיר Thorns, briers. Asyndeton. Comp. אדם שת אנוש (Divrei Hayamim I 1:1).
Yea, upon all the houses of joy in the joyous city. Supply thorns shall come up.
The palace of the king. נטש, shall be forsaken; עזב, shall be left. Pual.
עופל An elevated place. Comp. ויעפילו and they ascended.
ובחן And tower. Comp. בחוניו his towers. (23:13). היו מערות═ היה בעד מערות shall become dens.
יערה Be poured. Niphal. עד יערה עלינו רוח Until the decreed evil, the approach of the King of Ashur to the land of Yehudah, be poured upon us. רוח signifies here the divine decree.
And the plain, that is cultivated, will be like Karmel, and Karmel, etc. Comp. 29:17
Then judgment shall dwell, etc. Hashem will punish those that forsake him.
And the work of righteousness shall be peace, as in the time of Chizkiyahu. Comp. And peace without end (9:6) Some explain ver. 15 sqq. as a blessing.
My people. Yehudah.

וברד When it shall hail. The Pathah under ר proves that the word is a verb; comp. עשן it smoked (Shemot 19:18). When it shall hail, coming down on the forest. When the hailstones will come down, they will come down on the forest, not on the fields.
The city shall be low, shall be like a wide plain without walls
Beside all waters, that shall come.
That send forth the feet of the ox and the ass. Comp. 30:24; all these chapters from xxiv.—xxxvi. form one continuous prophecy.
הוי Ho! Interjection of calling. The prophet addresses Ashur.
כהתמך שודד when thou shalt have finished spoiling.
כהנלותך ═ כנלותך When thou shalt have finished. Of the same root is מנלם the perfection thereof (Iyov. 15:29)
O Hashem, etc. This was to be the prayer of the righteous at the time of the invasion of the Ashuri king; the prayer is given here as a prophecy.
Their arm. The arm of the soldiers.
The tumult of Ashur.
מרממתך By Thy honour. The honour which Thou hast given him.
Your spoil. Those of you that have become a spoil of the nations; the possessive pronoun your refers to Bnei Yisrael, of whom the king of Ashur carried a part away into captivity.
גבים Locusts. Comp. גובא in Chaldee, meaning the same as ארבה locusts in Hebrew.

שוקק Gathering. Some think that משק the steward (Bereshit 15:2) is of the same root. I compare it rather with ישתקשקון they gather themselves (Nachum 2:5), which expression is likewise used of locusts.
Hashem, etc. The divine glory, that revealeth itself in Tziyon.
Thy times. The pronoun refers to Yehudah.
חכמת The wisdom of. Some noun must be supplied.
His treasure. The treasure of strength of salvation.

אראלם According to some their altar; comp. אריאל (29:1); if this were correct, we should have to supply על for, but this explanation is not in accord with the whole context of the chapter. Others say, that אראה להם ═ אראלם I shall see them; this is not probable. I think that it means their messenger, as we may infer from the ambassadors of peace in the second half of the verse. Comp. Shmuel II 23:20.—All the messengers of the nations, that are desirous of peace, will weep when Ashur has dominion.
The highways lie waste. For the king of Ashur will not be faithful to his treaties with other nations.
He regardeth no man. He does not esteem any person to be worth anything in comparison with himself.

אבל אמללה ארץ The earth mourneth and languisheth. ארץ is sometimes used as a masculine noun; comp. 9:18. This phrase overthrows the rule laid down by R. Moshe Hakkohen (Iyov 20:26), that words which can be used both as masculine and feminine nouns, cannot be joined with a feminine attribute, after having been joined with a masculine one in the same phrase.
החפיר לבנון He—the king of Ashur—put the Levanon to shame. החפיר is transitive. קמל Till it was hewn down.
השרון Sharon. Comp. Shir Hashirim 2:1.
ונער בשן וכרמל And Bashan and Karmel shake off. Comp. נעור shaken (Nechemyah 5:13)
Now, that he has already destroyed too much, will I rise.
אתרומם═ ארומם will I be exalted. It is Hithpael; the ר should have a Dagesh to compensate for the omission of the ת, as the נ of אֶנָּשֵׂא has.
Ye shall conceive. Ashur is addressed.
חשש Chaff. The word has the same meaning in Arabic.

רוחכם אש תאכלכם According to some: Your breath, as fire, shall devour you. It is more correctly considered as the continuation of the preceding figure of the chaff and stubble: Your wind, will not lift you up, but, like fire, utterly destroy you.

As the burnings of lime. As if they were burnt by lime.—This refers to the sudden destruction of the Ashuri army through the angel, as is the case with the next simile as thorns cut off, which are burnt in the fire.
Ye, that are near. Bnei Yisrael are addressed, as may be inferred from the next verse, The sinners in Tziyon etc.

The sinners in Tziyon are afraid. They will be afraid of Hashem, when they see His power displayed in the destruction of the Ashuri army; then will they say: Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire, with Hashem, who is like the devouring fire, that is, in Tziyon, where the divine glory manifests itself. The prophet replies.
He that walketh, etc. בצדקות ═ צדקות In righteousness.
אוטם That stoppeth. Comp. יאטם that stoppeth (Tehillim 58:5); although the two words are of two different conjugations.
ועוצם And shutteth. Comp. ויעצם and he shut, though not of the same conjugation.
He, who does all this,
shall dwell on high, etc., shall dwell in Tziyon in safety, as if he dwelt, etc.
לחמו נתן His bread, bread, sufficient for his sustenance, shall be given him.
נאמנים Sure. Lit. faithful. The water will not deceive his hope, will not fail. He will dwell in peace and be satisfied.
Thine eyes shall see the king, etc. The prophet brings these words back to the memory of Yehudah;
Thine heart shall meditate, etc. These are the prophet’s own words.
סופר The scribe who writes down, how much every one shall contribute.
סופר He that counted. Comp. מספר the number, He that counted the towers. They taxed even the towers.

נועז We cannot say, whether the נ is radical, or the characteristic prefix of the Niphal; the word is hap. leg.; it means a stranger or a strange man; to consider לועז═נועז speaking a foreign language, is incorrect.
נלעג לשון Mocked for his tongue. People usually laugh at a language, which they cannot understand.
Look upon Tziyon, etc. We need not look at the king of Ashur, we should rather look at Tziyon.
מועדנו It has here its usual meaning: our solemnities or our sanctuary; comp. מעדי אל The synagogues of God (Tehillim 74:8).
כאהל═אהל As a tent.
יצען Hap. leg. It means, shall fall.
יתדותיו ובל יסע Not one of the stakes thereof shall ever be removed. חבליו The cords thereof.
But there, etc. This tent shall not be removed, but Hashem will be there unto us as a stronghold, like a place surrounded by rivers.
נהרים יארים Rivers, streams. Asyndeton; comp. שמש ירח sun, moon (Chavakuk 3:11).

ידים Space. A place of broad rivers. A place surrounded on all sides by rivers, בל תלך בו וגו׳ wherein shall go no, etc. None of the rivers will be passed by any ships with oars; the people will have no cause for fear, either from the sea or from the continent. Thus this verse contrasts with the words Thine heart meditates terror (ver. 18)

For Hashem is our judge, etc. There will be no judge to say to this person and that pay so and so much for the tribute, nor will any scribe write down, who shall go to the king with the tribute; for Hashem alone will be our judge, our scribe, and our king.
Thy tacklings. The Ashuri army is adressed.
נטשו Are loosed. Comp. ונמשתה thou shalt let it lie still (Shemot 23:11). The meaning of this figure is: the ship will go down, and her riches will then be thrown out again by the sea.

תרנם וגו׳ בל יחזקו כן They, that is, the sailors, cannot strengthen their mast, nor spread the sail. עד שלל The prey of a spoil. Comp. אדמת עפר the dust of the earth (Daniel 12:2). עד Spoil. Comp. Bereshit 49:27.
הרבה ═ מרבה Great. The lame shall take prey. How much more the others.
And the inhabitant of Tziyon shall not say again, I am sick; for all the people shall be forgiven their iniquity.
ומלאה And its fulness; that is, those beings of which it is full.
תבל The inhabited part of the earth.
צאצאיה The things that come out of it. It is derived from יצא to go out.

For the indignation, etc. All commentators refer this prophecy to the Messianic period, except R. Moshe Hakkohen, who says, that Edom was destroyed in the time of the invasion by the Ashur, and that all these chapters (xxiv—xxxiv) are connected with each other.
צבאם Their armies.
באשם Their stink. It is a noun derived from באש after the form of קׂדֶשׁ holiness.
ונמסו And shall be melted. Niphal of מסס to melt.

And all the host of heaven, etc. When the fatal day approaches to man, the sun darkens to him, as it is said in the description of the approaching death (Koh. 12:2). I think, that by these words the support is to be understood which each nation receives from its representative above; comp. Daniel 10:20.
ונמקו And shall be dissolved. Niphal of מקק to dissolve. ונגלו And shall be rolled together. Niphal of גלל to roll; comp. מגלה roll (Yirmiyahu 36:28)
For my sword, etc. This verse confirms my remark concerning the heavenly decrees.
עם חרמי The people of my doom. The people which I desire to see doomed to punishment.
The sword of the Lord. The divine decree.
הודשנה Is made fat. Many think it is a form composed of the Hophal and Hithpael, but wrongly; it is an irregular form; it is derived from דשן to be fat; comp. דשן fat (30:23).
כרים Lambs. Comp. Devarim 32:14. — The nobles are figuratively called lambs; comp. אילי מואב the chiefs of Moav.

Botzrah. According to some it is the name of the town now called Constantinople; this is impossible, because since the foundation of that town, there have not yet elapsed a thousand years; Botzrah is a province in Edom.
With them, with the lambs and goats; by the unicorns and bullocks the kings of Edom are meant.

For it is the day of Hashem’s vengeance, etc. This verse shows that the prophecy refers to the Messianic period; some believe, that it was fulfilled already in the time of Nevuchadnetzar, after the conquest of Tziyon; comp. The cup will be passed also to thee (Eichah 4:21).
The year of recompences. Comp. Thy reward shall return over thine own head (Ovadyah 15); these words refer likewise to Edom.

And the streams thereof, etc. This really happened or will happen in a miraculous way, as some believe; others are of opinion that this verse is to be taken figuratively: None will remain there to drink the water, as if it were changed to pitch.
בוערה Burning. This word shows that the ת of זפת is the feminine termination.
It shall not be quenched. The fire thereof shall not be quenched.
לנצח נצחים For ever and ever. For periods without end.
קפוד Hedgehog. Well known; the root of this word is met with in קפדתי I have rolled together (38:12).
And he shall stretch upon it, etc. Lime and stones are materials used by the builder.
תהו, בהו Emptiness, confusion. These words are similar in meaning to שממה desolation.
חוריה The nobles thereof. They are compared with the white colour; the people of the lower class are called the black (Mishlei 22:29).
יקראו They shall be called. Lit., They—the people—will call them. למלוכה ═ מלוכה to the kingdom.
אפס Nothing.
ארמנותיה Over her palaces. The preposition על is to be supplied. ועלתה סירים And thorns shall come up. Lit., And each of the thorns shall come up. סירים Thorns. Comp. Koh. 7:6. קמוש The same.
תנים Dragons. Comp. Iyov 30:29.
חצר ═ חציר A court. Comp. יָשֵׂשׂ (Divrei Hayamim II 36:17) ═ יָשִׂישׂ (Iyov 15:10), old. It can also be taken in its usual meaning: grass.
ציים The wild beasts of the desert.
איים Kites. It is the plural of אַיָה (Vayikra 11:14), although it has the masculine termination .ים.
שעירים An animal, similar to the wild goat.
הרגיעה Shall rest.
לילית The screech owl. A bird that flies abroad by night.
קפוז The great owl. It is not the same as ;קפוד it is some other bird.
ותמלט And lay. Comp. והמליטה זכר and she was delivered of a man-child (66:7).
ובקעה And break. It is the nature of this bird to break its eggs.
ודגרה And gather. Comp. דגר he gathereth (Yirmiyahu 17:11).
דיות Vultures. It is the plural of דַיָה (Devarim 14:13)

Seek ye out of the book of Hashem and read: none of these shall fail, etc. None of the divine decrees, which are written down with the finger of Elokim, shall fail; all of them will be fulfilled in Edom. Or: None of those, for which Edom is said (ver. 13, 14) to become the habitation, shall fail.
My mouth. The decrees that come from the mouth of Hashem.
ורוחו And its breath, that is, the breath of His mouth. It is a repetition of the same idea.
חלקתה Hath divided it. Both subject and object are feminine.
בקו By line. With the line of truth.

יששום. Some think that the preposition ב is omitted, and that יששו בם ═ יששום they shall be glad for them: this is not right; for what would be the meaning of בם? I think that מ is here substituted for the paragogic נ, which is frequently found in verbs. Comp. פדיון ═ פִּדְיוֹם redemption (Bamidbar 3:19).—The land of Edom alone shall be waste; but Palestine shall be the reverse. According to R. Moshe Hakkohen this prophecy refers to the deliverance of Yerushalayim.
It shall blossom. Palestine or Yerushalayim shall blossom.
גילת לב ═ גילת Joy of the heart. The ת indicates the construct state of the noun. Unto it. Unto the Levanon, according to some commentators.
They shall see. The inhabitants of Yerushalayim shall see.

Strengthen ye, etc. According to all the commentators except R. Moshe Hakkohen, this prophecy refers to the Messianic period; he refers it to the return of the fugitives in the time of Chizkiyahu, after the death of the king of Ashur.
Confirm the feeble knees, that they be able to walk.
To them that are of a fearful heart. To those that do not believe that such a miracle could happen. With vengeance against Edom or Ashur.
Then, when they see this miracle or hear of it.
Then shall the lame man leap, in his return to Yerushalayim.

And the tongue of the dumb shall sing. A figurative expression for they will find water everywhere; it is the reverse of the tongue of the suckling cleaveth to the roof of his mouth for thirst (Eichah 4:4)
השרב The parched ground. Comp. שרב heat (49:10) and שרבא the Chaldæan translation of חרב heat (Bereshit 31:40).
בנוה תנים רבצה That which had been covered with the dwelling of dragons. The desert.
חצר═חציר Court.
With reeds and rushes, that grow on the banks of rivers.
And an highway shall be there, etc. Although the rivers shall swell, still there will be a pathway, etc. מסלול An highway.
The way of holiness. So called because of the return of Bnei Yisrael to Yerushalayim.

The unclean shall not pass, etc. No heathen, that is unclean, will pass over it, although it is his own, out of fear: the redeemed alone shall walk on the highway; and furthermore, the wayfaring men, and fools, that are not acquainted with the way, shall not err therein, because it will be a highway.
No lion shall be there on that way.
Nor any ravenous beast, that could do harm, and frighten those that wish to return. But the redeemed shall walk there. Those that will return will be unmolested by enemies and wild beasts.

And the ransomed, etc. And those that return, will come to Tziyon with rejoicing and with everlasting joy upon their heads. The head is the principal seat of the soul. According to others the joy will be like a cover over their heads; this explanation is also admissible.
ששון ושמחה ישיגו Joy and gladness shall reach them. According to others: they shall obtain joy and gladness.

They are in meaning the same, although the one contains some additional words, which the other has not; the words may be compared with instruments, their meanings with the workmen. I shall now explain six passages.

1. In the book of Melachim (18:20) Thou sayest (but they are but vain words) I have counsel and strength for war; that is, thou hast said to thy people, that thou hast wisdom and strength for war, but this was only a word of the lips, thy strength consisted only in words. In the book of Yeshayahu (36:5) it is said, I say but vain words are counsel and strength for war. These are the words of Ravshake; he says: I believe, that thy counsel and strength for war consist only in words.

2. In the book of Melachim (19:14) ויקראם And he read them, viz., the documents (הספרים); in Yeshayahu (37:14) ויקראהו And he read it, viz., that document alone, which contained the blasphemies; in both, And spread it.
3. In the book of Melachim there is the addition of the words נהרי זרים═זרים, the rivers of strangers, after מים water.

4. In the book of Melachim (19:25) להשות וגו׳ To make equal, etc., to make fenced cities equal to heaps of ruins; in the book of Yeshayahu (37:26) להשאות to lay waste, etc., to lay waste fenced cities, that they be like heaps of ruins; comp. שואה desolation (10:3); or להשאות is the same as להשות, since א and ו frequently interchange.
5. In the book of Melachim (19:26) שרפה; in Yeshayahu (37:27) שדמה; though there be two different words, their meaning is the same, blasted.
6. In the book of Melachim (19:29) סחיש; in Yeshayahu (37:30) שחים; these two words are the same in meaning—that which springeth of the same. Comp. כבש and כשב lamb (Vayikra 3:7, and 4:32)
ויחי And was recovered. Comp. עד חיותם till they were whole (Jos. 5:8), ואתה מחיה and thou preservest (Nechemyah 9:6). It might also mean, And he lived.
בדמי. Some derive it from דָּם blood, and explain it, In the vigour; but the correct explanation is: In the cutting off. Comp. נדמה נדמה shall utterly be cut off (Hoshea 10:15).
שאל The grave, which is deep in the earth; the opposite of heaven, which is always above; comp. Tehillim 139:8: it does not mean hell.

פקדתי I am deprived. Comp. ולא נפקד and there lacketh not (Bamidbar 31:49); it is a poetical expression, as also used in Arabic. Some say that פקדתי is the same as ממני פקד was taken from me, and compare it with יצאוני are gone forth from me (Yirmiyahu 10:20); according to others it means I was remembered, in the same sense as and the Lord remembered (Bereshit 21:1).
The residue of my years. Comp. the number of thy days I will complete (Shemot 23:26). In my commentary on that verse I have explained it.

I shall not see Hashem, etc. Hashem is not subject to accidents, that a human eye should be able to perceive Him; He is, however, known by His works. The meaning of this verse is therefore: I shall not see any longer the works of the Almighty; I shall not understand the works of Hashem in this world, in the land of the living. These latter words are thus added as a kind of explanation of the preceding phrase. The pleasure which man has in this world in understanding the works of the Almighty is first mentioned; and then, in the words, I shall behold man no more, his pleasure in seeing his fellow-men.

חדל World. חדל is perhaps the same as חלד life, as כשב is the same as כבש lamb; comp. חלדי my life (Tehillim 39:6); it is possible that the word has the same meaning in the phrase מה חדל אני how long I am living (Tehillim 39:5). The life of man in this world is perhaps called חדל because man must at some time cease to be therein.

דורי My dwelling. Comp. מדור from dwelling (Tehillim 39:5); the word is frequent in Chaldee; דור generation (13:20) is perhaps to be derived from the same root; comp. for I am a stranger with thee, and a sojourner (Tehillim 39:13).
נִסַּע Is departed. The radical נ is replaced by Dagesh in the ס.
ונגלה And is removed. Comp. גלות exile (20:4).
ממני═מני From me. Comp. 22:4.

רועי Either my shepherd, the י being the pronominal suffix, or belonging to a shepherd, the י signifying relation, as in פנימי inner (Melachim I 6:26), אכזרי cruel (13:9); for the tent of the shepherd does not remain in one place.
קפדתי I folded together.
Like a weaver. Comp. And my days are swifter than the weaver’s shuttle (Iyov 7:6).
מדלה With pining sickness. Comp. דל lean (Shmuel I 13:4). With this illness, which I am suffering now,
יבצעני He will cut me off, that my life will expire; comp. ויבצעני and cut me off (Iyov 6:9).

מיום עד לילה תשלימני From day even to night it will make peace with me. It is an illness that keeps peace with the patient during the day, and makes war during the night; a fact often observed in cases of illness.תשלימני It will make peace with me Comp. תשלים it will make peace (Devarim 20:12)

שויתי I made equal; supply נפשי myself; or I compared the illness in its fierce attacks on me, with a lion which generally breaks the bones. From day even to night it maketh peace with me, to my great surprise, after the attacks during the night.

כסוס כעגור═כסוס עגור. Comp. כרע כאח לי as though he had been my friend, my brother (Tehillim 35:14). In the same way ככבש כאלוף ═ אלוף ככבש like a lamb, like an ox (Yirmiyahu 14:19). סיס and עגור are names of birds, a crane, a swallow. So did I chatter. The patient in his heavy illness mutters and speaks what no one is able to understand.
דלו They are lifted up. Root דלל, comp. דליו they are high (Mishlei 26:7).
עשקה לי It oppresseth me. The illness oppresseth me.

ערבני Undertake for me. Comp. ערוב be surety (Tehillim 119:112); according to some הרבני ═ ערבני destroy me; this is nonsense. The word ערבני, lit. pledge thyself for me, is an anthropomorphism; it means, sympathise with me in my troubles.
He hath spoken unto me. He said, I will add to thy days (ver. 5),

והוא עשה And himself will do it. The past is here used for the future; comp. נתתי I will give (Bereshit 23:13); or And himself hath done this kindness unto me, and still I shall go softly in the bitterness of my soul, when remembering these troubles, which I had to suffer.
אדדה I shall go softly. Hithpaël; there is no parallel to it in the Bible, but אדדם I went with them (Tehillim 42:5), and in the Mishna מדדה (Shabb. 18:2) in the well known meaning.

עליהם By them. By the words, hinted at in the phrase And he said (ver. 15). עליהם יחיו By them they live. By thy words and acts the living beings exist. ולכל And always. The word עת time is to be supplied.
ותחלימני So wilt thou recover me. Comp. יחלמו they are strong (Iyov 39:4); חלום strong (Talm. Bab. Rosh Hashanah 28)

Behold when I hoped for peace, etc., when I was in the middle of my years, (Chizkiyahu was 39 years old, when he was taken ill); for when the choler is predominant in man, he is ailing in his youth, but healthy in his old age; the reverse takes place, if the phlegm is predominant; but the middle years are generally expected to be peaceful.
מר לי מר I had great bitterness. The repetition indicates emphasis. Some derive מר from תמורה

the reverse. בלי Some compare it with בלתי I am waxed old (Bereshit 18:12), and consider it as a noun like פרי fruit meaning corruption. Others say that בלי means in this verse not, and that the sentence is inverted. The first explanation is preferable: And thou hast desired my soul, and brought me up from the pit of corruption.

For thou hast cast all my sins behind thy back. A figure taken from man, that does not see, what is behind his back; for we know, that God, the Creator of all bodies, has no body. This verse proves the assertion of some authorities, that in consequence of a sin committed by him, Chizkiyahu should have died earlier; and since, as they otherwise stated, he who dies before his fifty-second year suffers the punishment כָּרְת to be cut off, he was grieved, that he should be punished with כָּרְת, not being conscious of having committed a sin deserving it; he says therefore: Remember now, how I have walked before Thee, and have done what is good in Thine eyes (ver. 3); he mentions two things, the thought and the practice. Tradition says, that he had not yet obeyed the commandment to marry.
For the grave, etc. The body which is in the grave; the negation לא is to be repeated after מות: death cannot celebrate thee; comp. Mishlei 21:14.

ישברו They hope. Comp. Tehillim 145:15. Many are surprised to find here the prophet declaring such things, as if denying the truth of the resurrection of the dead; but the body has no power, no knowledge, when the soul has left it; and why should we be surprised at it? Man has sometimes no understanding when the soul is in the body, much less after his death.

The living, the living. The word חי living is repeated as if to say he who is living, as I do, or he who has recovered from illness. Shall praise thee, shall give thanks in words, in which soul and body appear to unite. According to some the first חי refers to Hashem; but there is no necessity for this assumption.
Thy truth. These acts of truth.
Hashem. Supply hath said, or will say, or will command.
And my songs, the songs which I shall compose. We will sing. I, and the singers in the temple, will sing, all our life.

Let them take a lump of figs, etc. This is a miracle, because the figs are injurious to him who suffers from the scab; and the reason that the future forms וימרחו ,ישאו are used, is, that here only the command is reported.
דבלת תאנים A lump of figs. Figs, that are opened, pressed together, and form a mass which is cut with a knife.
וימרחו And lay it for a plaster. The word has a similar meaning in Arabic; what it means is well known.
ויאמר חזקיהו Chizkiyahu also had said before, What is the sign, as mentioned above (38:7)

This chapter has been placed here for the following reason: in the preceding chapter it is predicted that all the treasures of the King, and even his sons, will be carried away to Bavel; this sad prediction is properly followed by the words of comfort.

These first comforting promises, with which the second part of the book of Yeshayahu begins, refer, as R. Moshe Hakkohen believes, to the restoration of the temple by Zerubavel; according to my opinion to the coming redemption from our present exile; prophecies concerning the Babylonian exile are introduced only as an illustration, showing how Koresh, who allowed the captive Yehudim to return to Yerushalayim, …. About the last section of the book there is no doubt, that it refers to a period yet to come, as I shall explain.—It must be borne in mind, that the opinion of the orthodox, that the book of Shmuel was written by Shmuel, is correct as regards the first part, till the words And Shmuel died (Shmuel I 25:1); this remark is confirmed by the fact that the book of Divrei Hayamim contains the names (of the descendants of David) in genealogical order down to Zerubavel.—The words Kings shall see and arise, princes and shall worship (49:7) support this view, though they might also be explained as follows: Kings and princes will arise, etc., when they hear the name of the prophet, even after his death. The reader will adopt the opinion which recommends itself most to his judgment.
Comfort, etc. Hashem addresses His prophet or the chiefs of the people. The repetition of the words Comfort ye is to indicate, that the comfort is to be administered immediately or repeatedly.
דברו על לב Speak ye comfortably. The expression דבר על לב speak to the heart means always to speak kindly, so as to remove sorrow and regret for things which have already past; comp. Bereshit 50:21.
Yerushalayim. The congregation of Yisrael is meant.
צבאה Her time. Comp. צבאי my appointed time (Iyov 14:14); צבא (ib. vii .1). The commentators generally take it in its usual sense; her host; but the first explanation is the right one.

נרצה Is accomplished, that is, is finished and at an end; comp. עד ירצה till he shall accomplish (Iyov 14:6); תרצה shall accomplish (Levit. 26:34); נרצה עונה has the same meaning as the phrase תם עונן the punishment of thine iniquity is accomplished (Eichah 4:22).
Double. Twice as much affliction as other nations had to suffer.
בכל For all.
The voice of him that crieth, of him, that brings the good tidings.
Prepare ye, etc. These words are addressed to all nations.
The way of Hashem. The way of those that have been in exile and return to the holy mountain.
Make straight, etc. Repetition of the same idea.

Every valley shall be exalted. Every valley that is now low, shall then be exalted. The word גֶּיא valley is not in the construct state as in 22:1, and Ez. 39:11. It is, however, possible that it is in the construct state and some genitive is to be supplied; comp. מִלֵּיל (21:11).
העקוב The crooked. It is the opposite of מישור straight; comp. עקוב deceitful (Yirmiyahu 17:9).
והרכסים And the rough places. Comp. מרכסי from the crookedness of (Tehillim 39:21)
And the glory, etc. When Hashem will perform this miracle, then His glory will be revealed.
The voice said, etc. This verse explains the glory of Hashem to consist in the fact that His word alone is fulfilled, not so the word of man.
The voice. The angel. Said unto the prophet. כחציר═חציר Like grass. Comp. כשמש═שמש as sun (Tehillim 84:12).
As the flower of the field, which flourisheth in the morning and groweth up, but is cut down and withereth in the evening (Tehillim 90:6)
חציר Grass. The fresh grass; the word has the same meaning in Arabic.
נשבה Bloweth. Comp. וישב and he drove away (Bereshit 15:11), though of a different conjugation.
כחציר═חציר Like grass. העם All people.
The grass withereth, etc. Since he is like grass, he will wither; since he is like the flower, he will fade away; but the word of Hashem shall stand—יעמוד═יקום—and none will frustrate it.
רוח ה׳ The wind of Hashem, that is, the wind, which is sent by Him, נשבה בו Bloweth upon it, that is, upon the grass, and it becomes dry.
מבשרת That bringeth good tidings. The feminine is used because עדה the congregation is to be supplied, but not because it signifies a female person.
בחזק With strong hand, יד hand is to be supplied; as to the use of יד as a masculine noun, comp. Ez. 2:9.

שכרו His reward, that is, the reward which He will give to him that hopes for Him. ופעלתו And his wages. Comp. פעלת שכיר the wages of him that is hired; פעלה lit. work signifies also the wages for the work.—I think that this explanation is not supported by the context, and that the sense of the sentence is: God does not ask for any wages ; He is not like a hired shepherd, but כרעה עדרו (next verse) like one, that feeds his own flock.
And carry them in his bosom. Namely those that cannot walk.
עלות Those that are with young. The word is derived from עלה to go up.
ינהל He shall gently lead.—Hashem will bring together those that are in exile, and heal those that are suffering.

Who hath measured, etc. There are some that ask, How is it possible that such a thing shall happen? The answer is that the same Supreme Being will cause it to pass, who has created the whole universe, who knows the quantity of the water in the sea, as if He had measured it with His hand.
בשעלו In the hollow of His hand. Comp. כשעלי for handfuls (Ez. 13:19).

And meted out heaven with the span. He knows the measure of heaven, which He has stretched out like a curtain; He has created it with His omnipotence, according to His wisdom, as if He had measured it with the span. The words of the text are an anthropomorphism.
וכל And measured. Comp. וכלו, the Kasdi translation of וימדו and they measured (Shemot 16:18).
בשליש In a measure. שליש is very likely derived from שלש three, but we do not know at present the capacities of ancient measures. Comp. בשליש in great measure (Ps. Ixxx. 6).
בפלס In a balance. It is called in Arabic Kriston and consists of one long arm. The word פֶלֶס is of the same root as פַלֵּס weigh (Mishlei 4:26).
וגבעות במאזנים And hills in scales. He places two hills in the two scales and weighs them against each other. All this is said figuratively.

רוח יי The spirit of Hashem. The Gaon says that תוח the wind (air) has not yet been mentioned with the other three elements in the preceding verse, and that יי Hashem is the answer given to the question, and the meaning of the phrase is: Who has directed the wind? Hashem. I do not agree with this explanation, because it is said את רוח, and besides, the second half of the verse has no sense at all if this explanation be adopted. I explain the verse thus: Who has directed the spirit of Hashem: רוח is in the construct state; comp. אלהים רוח (Bereshit 1:2); the interrogative pronoun מי who, is to be supplied before the second part of the verse: And who is the man, to whom Elokim communicated His counsel, why He created things in such and such a manner.
נועץ It is the past of Niphal; the ע has therefore a Pathah; it means, He took counsel.
ויבינהו And gave Him understanding. And taught Him the path of judgment, how to fix the punishment for every sin,
and taught Him knowledge (דעת), to know future events.
כמר מדלי As a drop of a bucket, as a drop that falls from the bucket. מר drop is hap. leg.
וכשחק And as the small dust. Comp. ושחקת and thou shalt beat (Shemot 30:36).—Since all people are vain before Him, with whom could he have taken counsel?

יטול He throweth; comp. ויטילו and cast Him forth (Yonah 1:5), though of a different root. According to R. Yonah ימול is Niphal, but that is very improbable; it can also be explained He taketh up and compared with נוטל carrying (Mishnah Shab. 17:2).

And Levanon is not sufficient, etc. God does not want burnt offerings; Levanon would not suffice for fuel, if He wanted offerings. Levanon is mentioned by the prophet simply as an example which his hearers can understand ; in reality, however, he refers to all the woods of the earth. The same remark applies to the words and the beasts thereof.

All nations, etc. All divisions of nature are reviewed by the prophet; viz. first the nations (ver. 15), that is, man, and then (ver. 16) plants and beasts.—The meaning of this verse is: since all is as nothing before Him, etc.

מאפס Less than nothing. The מ denotes here the same as in מהבל lighter than vanity (Ps. Ixii. 10).—It is surprising how the Gaon could place men above angels, he must certainly have read this chapter.
To whom then, etc. They are without knowledge, but Elokim is omniscient (Jos. 22:22).
הפסלּ The image, which is cut of stone or wood.
נסך Melteth. Comp. ענל מסכה a molten calf (Ex, 32:4).
ירקענו Beateth it. Comp. וירקעו and they did beat (Shemot 39:3), רקיע expanse (Bereshit 1:6).
רתקות A kind of chain. Comp. הרתוק the chains (Ez. 7:23)

המסכן תרומה Some explain מסכן to be identical with סוכן treasurer (22:15), and supply מסכן: the treasurer, namely, the treasurer of the oblation. According to others מסכן is an adjective; That which is stored up, namely the oblation, of which to make an image ;
the third person in יבחר he chooseth is explained by them to refer to the owner of the oblation.
To prepare a graven image that shall not be moved. To fasten it with nails.
הלא תדעו Have ye not known by your own common sense, which is the most important source of knowledge ;
הלא תשמעו have you not heard; have you not been informed by others;
הלא הגד מראש לכם hath it not been told you from the beginning, this is the lowest degree of knowledge.
From the beginning. From the first day of your existence; and even if you have no knowledge at all, have you not considered the foundations of the earth? etc.

חוג Circle. Comp. מחוגה compass (44:13), the instrument, which is used to describe a circle.—Here it is stated that the earth is round and not square, though no verse is required for the support of this statement; for it is known by convincing proofs. He who sitteth upon the circle of the earth. He whose glory fills the whole earth.
כדוק As a curtain. Resembling the form of a tent.—The heavens mentioned here are not the Ofanim.
וימתחם And spreadeth them out,
as a tent to dwell under them.—The meaning of the whole passage is: Hashem is He who sitteth, etc.
רוזנים Princes. Comp. רזון prince (Mishlei 14:28) ; the adjective has various forms.
