Yea, they shall not be planted, etc. They shall be like trees, that perished as completely as if they had never been planted. נטעו is Niphal; זרעו is Pual;
שרש is participle Kal.
נשף He shall blow. Comp. נשפת thou didst blow (Shemot 15:10). וגם And besides.

To whom then will you liken me, etc. The prophet addresses the idolatrous people, saying, Are there men more honoured by you than princes and judges? and yet you see that Hashem destroys them in a moment.
ואשוה That I be equal to him.
The holy. Hashem is too holy to be compared with one of His creatures, much less with the products of His creatures.

Who hath created these, these creatures that are here; and who is it, that bringeth out their host with number every day. This phrase refers to the daily apparent coming and going of the stars. It may also refer to the planets, each of which has its circuit defined by a number, which is known to the Almighty, but unknown hitherto to the wise men of the East and to all astronomers. It is, however, possible, that the prophet refers to the number of stars in the highest sphere, which no man, however wise, is able to tell.
By the greatness of might, which He possesses; and for that He is strong in power,
not one faileth to be numbered, or to preserve its substance; for no star is ever annihilated. איש signifies here an individual; comp. והאיש גבריאל (Daniel 9:21).

My way is hid from Hashem, that is, He does not see what I am doing. The same idea is contained in the words which follow: And my judgment passeth away from my Hashem, that is, He will not judge me according to my way.
הלא ידעת Hast thou not known by common sense; for he who is thinking can attain a knowledge of his Creator by convincing proofs.
אם לא שמעת Hast thou not heard, and learnt from others, who have studied.
The everlasting Elokim. As He was, so He will always be, without alteration.

בורא Creator. I have explained already (Bereshit 1:1), that ברא literally means to cut. The ends of the earth. The horizon, which is, according to the opinion of scientific men, no real line. Since Hashem is eternal,—the earth can testify it, which he keeps continually in the midst of the spheres, although it rests on nothing—
He fainteth not, neither is He weary, and there is no searching of His understanding; consequently, His might and wisdom will never depart from Him.

Some say, that the phrase my way is hid, refers to the troubles which Bnei Yisrael have to suffer, and which they imagine to be either unknown to the Almighty, or of such a nature, that even if He knew them, He could not remove them.
He giveth power, etc. How can He be weary, if He gives power to the faint, and strengthens him that is without strength. עָצְמָה Strength. It is a noun similar in form to חָבְמָה wisdom.
Even the youths who have strength, faint, etc.

יחליפו כח Shall renew their strength. Before one power is exhausted, the other is prepared for them by the Almighty. Comp. if it be cut down, (יחליף) it will sprout again (Iyov. 14:7). In Arabic this word has a similar meaning.

אבר Wing. Comp. Tehillim 55:7.—The sense of the whole verse seems to be this: Bnei Yisrael that trusted in the Almighty will be strengthened by Him, and He will bring them back to Yerushalayim; the Babylonians, who are now mighty, will be weakened.
החרישו ושמעו אלי ═ החרישו אלי Be silent and listen unto me.
And let the people renew their strength, if they can.
Let them come near, after having renewed their strength. Then let them speak, and let us come near together to judgment, to know, who is the mighty.

ממזרח The man from the east. The ancients refer this expression to Avraham, who defeated the kings (Gen. xiv.), and broke the idols; especially because of the words the seed of Avraham, my friend, (ver. 8). This is not impossible, but I refer it rather to Koresh; because all these chapters are connected by their contents; comp. calling a ravenous bird from the east (46:11) and I have raised up one from the north, and he shall come; from the rising of the sun shall he call upon my name (41:25); besides, the name of Koresh is distinctly mentioned 44:28 and 45:1.
From the east, Eilam was north-east of Bavel.
יקראהו He shall meet it or it shall meet him. לרגלו To his foot. Wherever he goes.
ומלכים ירד He will appoint rulers over hings. יַרְדְּ is Hiphil; he will cause to rule; comp. (the Kal) וירר and he shall have dominion (Bamidbar 24:19)

יתן כעפר חרבו he will turn his sword into dust, that is, the sword of every other king. Others explain it: he will make his swords as numerous as the dust, and his arrows shall fly about as thickly as stubble driven by the wind.
ירדפם He will pursue them, the kings. And pass in peace, that is, without weariness. ארח ברגליו לא יבוא As if he had not at all gone that path with his feet.

עשה Hath prepared. Comp. לעשות to dress (Bereshit 18:7). Who has done this? Hashem has done it, who is calling the generations from the beginning, before they come into existence; who knows all future generations, and cites each of them to appear in its right time.
The first of all generations that have hitherto existed. And with the last, with the last generations.
The isles saw the victory of Koresh.
They drew near. Those events drew near.
ויאתיון And came. It is here written like a perfect verb; the third radical ה is replaced by י.
They help every one, etc. All islands, all men, and all nations are now more anxious to worship idols, believing that they can thus be delivered out of the hands of Koresh.
מחליק He that smootheth. Comp. חלק smooth (Bereshit 27:11).
פטיש Hammer. A well known instrument Comp. Yirmiyahu 23:29.

הלם It is a noun derived from הלם to beat; comp. והלמה and she smote; it signifies the iron which is wrought by beating with the hammer. פעם The iron block, upon which the iron is hammered : the anvil; it is called פַעַם because of the beating upon it. It is also possible that the two words פעם הלם together signify one instrument.
אמר לדבק טוב הוא Saying of the joining, It is good. Till the joining is good.

But thou, Yisrael, etc. Those are worshippers of idols, says the prophet, but thou, Yisrael, art my servant; the name of Avraham is mentioned here, because he also was taken out from the midst of idolaters.
אהבי Who loved me. It is not the same as אהובי who is loved by me, the former being active, the latter passive.
From the ends of the earth. Bnei Yisrael were in Bavel, far away from their own land.

ומאציליה And from the chief men thereof, who are distinguished from the rest; comp. ואצלתי and I will take (Num. xi. אצילי .(17 . the nobles of (Shemot 24:11). ומאציליה can also be explained from between her arms.
תשתע The second ת is the characteristic of the Hithpael, correctly put after the first radical. אל תשתע Do not turn away. Comp. שעו מני turn away from me. (22:4)

הנחרים They that were incensed. It is the Niphal; Comp. חרי lit. the burning; נחרו were angry (Shir Hashirim 1:6). The Babylonians are meant; when God punished and destroyed Bavel, He released His people, who returned home to their country with the permission of Koresh.
מנצותך ═ מצותך Thy Contention. The נ is replaced by Dagesh in צ ; the form of the word is like that of מלקות. Comp. מצה strife (Mishlei 17:19); ינצו strive together (Devarim 25:11).
אפס Nothing.
For I, the Lord, etc. For this is a wonderful event, that Bavel was taken, that her armies were destroyed in their own land, and Bnei Yisrael remained unhurt.
Thou worm Yaakov, Yisrael had been considered by the Babylonians as worms. Fear not, that you will be killed together with the Babylonians.

עזרתיך I will help thee. The future is here expressed by the past (עזרתיך), because all the divine decrees concerning the future, are considered as sure as if they were already fulfilled; besides the difference between past and future exists only with regard to created beings.
למורג A threshing instrument. It is well known. Comp. המוריגים threshing instruments (Shmuel II 24:22).

חרוץ Decreed by law. Comp. חרצת thou hast decreed (Melachim I 20:40). It is not surprising to find here the word ישראל used as a masculine and feminine noun in one verse; it is used as feminine, as far as ערה congregation is understood, but it is not a feminine noun itself.
Mountains, A figurative expression for the Babylonians.
Thou shalt scatter them, etc. This verse indicates that the greater part of the Babylonians will perish, and also that Bnei Yisrael will take their spoil.
The poor, etc. In their return from Bavel to Yerushalayim.
נשתה Faileth. Comp. ונשתו and shall fail (19:5).
The Hashem of Yisrael, I (אני) of the preceding, refers to this sentence also, and is to be supplied before the Elokim, as is often the case.
שפים High places. It is the opposite of בקעות valleys. This also is wonderful, that rivers will be found on high places.
מדבר Wilderness. A plain that is not inhabited.
ארז שטה The cedar, the shittah tree. Asyndeton, like ירח שמש the sun, the moon (Chavakuk 3:10),
תדהר ותאשור. Names of trees. All these trees grow about rivers; they do not grow where there is a want of water.
That they may see, etc. That the poor may see with their own eyes, and take it to heart.
בראה According to my opinion, hath shaped it; according to others, hath created it, that is, has brought it from non-existence into existence, but not from one form of existence into another.
קרבו Produce. It is imperative Piel after the form of ברכו praise (Jud. 5:2).
עצומותיכם Your disputes, Comp. עצומים quarreling (Mishlei 18:18). It would, however, not be wrong to explain עצומותיכם your strong reasons, as the plural of the adjective עצום mighty, strong.
Let them bring forth, their idols.

The imperative produce is addressed to those Bnei Yisrael, who did not trust in God, but worshipped idols even in Bavel; they are told to produce (ריבכם) their cause, that is, their evidence, to show which is the righteous side. The imperative shew הגידו is addressed to the idols.
האתיות Theat things that are to come. Comp. אתה cometh (21:12).
לאחור hereafter it is the opposite of לפנים (Rut 4:7). And know etc. We shall then know that you have power to do good or evil.<
ונשתעה that we may relate. Comp. ואשתעי the Kasdi translation of ויספר "and he related" (Shemot 48:18). Some explain it "and we shall turn unto it," and compare it with אל תשתע do not turn away.
Ye. The idols are adressed.
מאפע of nothing. It is hap. leg.
תועבה=איש תועבה "An abominable man," or it is the same as תועבה "for an abomination." יבחר בכם Chooseth you, for worship.
העירותי I have raised. The Pathah under ה is caused by the ע which follows.
From the north, Eilam was north-east of Bavel. The word איש a man must be supplied : I have raised up a man from the north; Koresh is meant.

ויאת And he came. It is an irregular form, because of the first and third radical (א and ה) being weak letters; it would have been of the form וַיׅפֶן, but the א being silent, the Hirek under י is changed into Pathah as is usually the case with gutturals; ויאת is Kal.
And he shall come upon princes, etc. He shall come into the land or the camp of princes, and tread upon them, as upon mortar.
צדיק He is righteous. His words are true; it is the opposite of כזב false.
Behold, there is none that showeth, none that heareth the words of the idols; for they have mouths but speak not (Tehillim 115:5)
The first. The first relatively; it is the attribute to מבשר one that bringeth good tidings, which is to be supplied.
הנה הם ═ הנם Behold them. These are the words which the messenger will say to Tziyon, behold there they are. The repetition of הנה behold is to indicate the speediness of the appreach.
For I beheld and there was no man of the idolaters that could tell this.
They. The idols.
אין ═ און nothing as some explain ; the letters אֹ הֹ וֹ יֹ interchange. It can, however, also be taken literally. The meaning of the verse is, they are vanity, much more so their works.
נסכיהם According to some their images; comp. עגל מסכה molten calf (Shemot 32:4). I explain it their libations, that is, the libations which the idolaters offer to their idols.
My servant. Most of the commentators refer this expression to the pious Bnei Yisrael; the Gaon to Koresh; I to the prophet, who speaks here of himself, as in 49:6.
My spirit of prophecy.
He shall bring forth judgment. He shall proclaim all that which shall happen in future to all nations. According to the Gaon the prophet indicates by this phrase that Koresh will be a righteous king.
He shall not cry, as the judge is used to do. Nor cause his voice to be heard in the street, in order that people should flock unto him.
A bruised reed. This is a prolepsis, like And stripped the naked of their clothing (Iyov 22:6). He will not break a reed, is figuratively said for he will not act by violence.

ופשתה כהה לא יכבנה And glimmering flax shall he not quench. Flax is easily put out. Glimmering flax is here a prolepsis. כהה thin; comp. כהה hath become smaller (Vayikra 13:6). There is, however, some difference between these two words; that in Leviticus is a verb, the word used here is an adjective. The meaning of the whole verse is: The prophet does no harm to any nation by his prophecies; he is but proclaiming what is to come in future.
He shall bring forth judgment unto truth. The judgment upon each nation, as it is decreed by Hashem, is meant.
He shall not fail. The prophet shall not fail, with regard to the spirit, which is joined to his body.

Nor will he be broken, with regard to his body. ירוץ is a verb ע״ע; comp. רצוץ broken (ver. 3); its form is like that of יָרוּז, doth sing (Mishlei 29:6). The meaning of this phrase is: The prophet shall not die, or he shall not be overcome by any violence of man. Compare the similar phrase in the preceding verse. This latter explanation, I think, is the right one.

Till he have set judgment in the earth, till the truth of his prophecy be proved, and isles shall wait for his law, for the instruction contained in his prophecies; comp. 8:20, and my commentary thereon.
בורא שמים He that shaped the heavens. There is a line, by which they are bordered.
And stretched them out over the earth; comp. רקיע expanse (Bereshit 1:6).
רוקע He that spread forth. ק has Pathah because of the ע which follows; comp. הנוטע he who planted (Tehillim 94:9).
And that which cometh out of it. The plants which grow upon the surface of the earth.
לעם עליה נותן נשמה He that giveth a soul unto the people upon it, that is, to man.
ורוח להלכים בה And breath to them that walk therein, that is, to the animals.
Upon it is used in the first instance, because man walks upright.
I, Hashem, have called thee, etc. Hashem in these words addresses the prophet upon his own concerns.
And I will keep thee, that no evil shall befall thee.
For a covenant of a people. To establish the covenant of a people ; comp. 49:8
To bring out the prisoners, etc. To tell Yisrael that they shall be delivered out of the Babylonian exile. Comp. 49:9

That is my name, my real name. Besides the tetragrammaton there is no other proper name of Hashem in the Scripture. And my glory, that I tell the prophet what is to come, and that he reveals them in my name to honour me. ולא תהלתי═ותהלתי. The negative לא not of the preceding phrase לא אתן, refers to this one also.

Sing unto the Lord, etc. The prophet addresses the people in these words. They that go down to the sea, etc. For all the people of the earth will praise God at the return of Yisrael from the Babylonian exile (Kedar is therefore mentioned together with the inhabitants of the isles, and those that go down to the sea), when they hear of this extraordinary event.
The plain and the cities thereof shall lift up their voice, etc.
Every plain and the cities thereof, all villages which are inhabited by Kedar, etc.; the tribe of Kedar always lived in the plain. The inhabitants of the rock, the nations that live in the rocks.
ירנו Shall shout. Comp. הרנה the cry (Melachim I 22:36).
יצוהו Shall lift up their voice. It is used both in a good and a bad sense. Comp. צוחה crying (24:11).
They will give glory, etc. They will acknowledge that Hashem has done great things, and will say as follows :
Hashem shall go forth, that is, the divine decrees, that were secret hitherto, shall now be revealed.
Jealousy because of the Babylonians, that worship Bel.
יריע He shall cry. Comp. תרועה shout (Jos. 6:5).
יצריח He shall roar. Comp. צורח crying (Tzefanyah 1:14), though of a different conjugation.
He shall show Himself mighty by the victory over Bavel.
I have long time, etc. The first person refers to Hashem.
החשתי I have holden my peace. Comp. החשו hold ye your peace (Melachim II 2:3).
אתאפק I refrained myself. Comp. להתאפק refrain himself (Bereshit 45:1).
אפעה Will I cry. Hap. leg. According to some it means viper, and כיולדה אפעה וגוי is explained by them as follows : like one that beareth a viper, so shall I be desolate and sighing at once.
אשם I shall be desolate. It is Niphal of a verb ע׳׳ע (שמם).

אשאף I shall sigh. Comp. שואף sighing (Kohelet 1:5). אשם Refers to the feeling of the heart, אשאף to the utterance of the mouth. This verse is addressed to those who will assert, that Hashem is unable to help His people.
I will make waste, etc. How can they think thus? Do they not see, that I lay waste mountains and hills, and dry up all their herbs, and make rivers into islands, that people can dwell therein.

And I will bring the blind by a way that they knew not; for even the blind, if accustomed to a path, go there without a guide. I will make darkness light before them, and crooked things straight. Some refer this to the return of Bnei Yisrael from Bavel.
They shall be turned back, etc., for I have the power to do as I like, not so the idols.
מסכה Molten images. The plural פסלי images must be supplied from the preceding phrase, because of the pronoun אַתֶּם ye which follows.
Ye deaf etc. Hearing and seeing originate in the heart; those that are deaf and blind in their hearts are, therefore, called here deaf and blind.
Who is blind, etc. This verse proves the correctness of my explanation.
You are blind who say that none is so blind as the prophet.
כמלאכי As my messenger. Comp. חגי מלאך יי Chaggai, the messenger of Hashem (Chaggai 1:13).
כמשלם As he that is righteous. Comp. ישולם is recompensed (Mishlei 11:31) ; שַׁלֵּם to pay (Shemot 22:5); פשלם lit., he who is recompensed, that is, the righteous.
As the servant of Hashem, who, though not a prophet, serves Hashem.

ראות Seeing. It is an irregular form; it is a combination of the two infinitives, the construct (רְאׁת) and the absolute (רׇאׁה). The meaning of the verse is: they will perceive many words of God, but their soul or eye will not retain them ; their ears will be open, they will not be closed, and still, strange to say, they will not hear.

Hashem is well pleased, that they do not see; He will show His justice and exalt His law, so that all those that forsake it shall be afraid. This verse may also be connected with the next, thus : Hashem showed His justice, and made those, that said of the prophet, that he is blind, robbed and spoiled, etc.
שסוי Spoiled. This is a verb .שסה) ל׳׳ה) Comp. שוסים spoiling (Shmuel I 23:1).
הפח Breathing. It is infinitive and has the same meaning as נפח, though of a different root (פוח).
בחורים In holes. Comp. חור hole (11:8). They are imprisoned, occupying the lowest dungeons of all the captives.
הׇשַׁב The Pathah is substituted for Zeré because the word is the end of the verse ; השב is transitive, and means restore, namely the spoil.
Who among you will tell this, will tell things like those which the prophet, whom you declared to be blind, proclaimed. לאחור For the time to come. Comp. תאחרו you keep me waiting (Bereshit 24:56);
לפנים in former time is derived from פנה it has turned away ; it is gone.

Who gave Yaakov, etc. Then the people will confess and say: who has given us for a spoil? Certainly Hashem, it is He (זה═זו this), against whom we have sinned, and in whose ways our forefathers refused to walk.
Upon him. Comp. Bereshit 49:22. Upon every one of our forefathers.
חמה חמת אפו═חמה אפו The fury, the fury of His anger, Comp. האהלה אהל שרה ══ האהלה שרה into the tent, the tent of Sarah (Bereshit 24:67).
ותלהטהו And it burned him. Comp. להט flame (Bereshit 3:24).—They will confess that their forefathers were blind with regard to their hearts, and had no understanding.
But now, etc. Now, says the prophet, since you have confessed, Hashem will redeem you.
I have called you by My name. I have given you a great distinction; comp. I have called by name Bezaleel (Shemot 31:2); and the distinction is further described in the words thou art mine.

When thou passest through the waters, etc. The peoples are in Scripture compared with rivers and also with fire; comp. A fire is gone out of Cheshbon (Bamidbar 21:28). By the waters and the fire the armies of Paras and Madai are meant, that were to conquer Bavel.
I gave Mitzrayim for thy ransom. The Mitzrim shall be afflicted by the kings of Madai.
Therefore will I give men, whom I have created, as I have created thee.
From the east. From Bavel.
From the west. From Mitzrayim and Ashur. Comp. Ezr. 6:22.
Give up my children.
ולתימן And to the south, תימן is derived from ימין the right.—He will bring them together from the four corners of the earth.
My sons, my daughters. The males and females.
קורא ═ נקרא that calleth, as some explain; but this is wrong. It is to be taken literally. Every one that is called by my name, that is, all that belong to the people of Hashem.
And for my glory. To be a glory to my name.
בראתיו I have formed it, namely, that nation.

עשיתיו I have established it.—R. Salomo, the father of metrical poetry in Hebrew, explained this verse to contain the principles of the creation of the universe ; but this explanation is not in accordance with the context.
הוציא To bring forth, It is infinitive.
A blind people, that were blind formerly, although they had eyes. Thus there is a connection between this and the preceding chapters.

Let all the nations be gathered together, etc. If some should say that Bnei Yisrael did not know these future events, for they were blind ; but of other nations and their wise men, some knew them perhaps, the question is put, Who among them can declare this, viz. that which shall happen in days to come, and show us former things, past events, which they had announced before they took place.
Let them bring forth their witnesses, that they may hear it.
ויצדקו that they may be justified with regard to their words; and
let them hear, that is, let the witnesses hear the same,
and say, It is truth, it was so.
Ye are my witnesses, etc. Yisrael is addressed. And my servant. The prophet.
I am he. This is the sublimest expression of the unity of God; for every other being is different from its real form.

Before me, after me. According to some, before me means before the revelation on Sinai, and after me, after the revelation. But it is not at all necessary to depart from the literal meaning of the words: No Hashem was before me, and none will be after me, because Hashem is the first and last. The expression formed (נוצר) is applied here to the word Hashem, in order to imply that a god besides Him can only be one formed by man. Shortsighted people think, that the expression formed used in reference to the Creator, slipped out of the mouth of the prophet; but this is by no means the case ; such critics do not conceive the true meaning of the verse.

I, I. The word is repeated, as if to say, I do not change as the host of heaven does with regard to its centre, nor as earthly things do with regard to substance and form; I can therefore help at every time.
I have declared in Mitzrayim, to save you.
And I have caused to hear. I have caused you to hear my voice on Sinai.
There was no stranger among you. Bnei Yisrael alone were there.
And you are my witnesses. You were informed of it by your fathers.
And I am Hashem continually; comp. I am Hashem, I change not (Malachi 3:6)
Before the day was, etc. I was God before the existence of day. Therefore, the word גם yea is added.
מהיות יום:═מיום When day was not yet.
I am he; and since I am God, who can be delivered out of my hand ;
I do my desire and will, and none can frustrate my doing.

שלחתי I was sent. Some think that the first person I refers to the prophet; but I am of opinion that Hashem is speaking, because this verse begins, Thus saith Hashem, and the next verse, I am Hashem, The meaning of the phrase is: I have come so hastily, as if I were sent. A very learned man in Spain conjectures, that the Divine Glory, the same heavenly prince of Yisrael that has been sent to Bavel to redeem Yisrael, is speaking to the prophet.
והורדתי בריחים And have brought down the bars of Bavel, that is, I caused Bavel to be conquered; comp. He hath destroyed and broken her bars (Lam, 2:9). The bars of the gates of the place are meant.
וכשדים באניות רנתם And I shall bring down the Chaldæans from their ships of joy, in which they are.
Your holy one. For I shall be your King, to save you.
Which maketh away in the sea. This shows, that the fleet of the enemy will arrive and defeat the Babylonian fleet.
Which bringeth forth the chariot and horse, תיל ועזוז the great and powerful army on land; the army of the Chaldæans is meant, that went out to fight against the Paras.
דעכו It is Pual, and means they are extinct; comp. ידעך shall be put out (Mishlei 20:20)
Remember ye not by words, the former wonders.
Neither consider them in your minds.

A new thing. The taking of Bavel, or the fact that Bnei Yisrael alone will escape; the latter seems the more probable explanation. I will even make, etc. I shall, besides, produce water in the wilderness for the benefit of those who will return from Bavel to Tziyon.

The beast of the field shall honour me, for the good which I am doing for it. The dragons are mentioned, because they live in the wilderness. To give drink to my people. I shall do this unto the beasts for the sake of my people.
זה ═ זו This. This people, that returns from Bavel, is mine.
But thou hast not called me, etc. All the good I do to Bnei Yisrael, I am not bound to do; for even Bnei Yisrael in Bavel have not sought me.
כי יגעת בי That thou be weary of me. Thou hast even not called me; how then shouldst thou be weary for my sake.
ישראל O Yisrael. It is in the Vocative case.
Thou hast not brought me burnt offerings in Bavel.
Neither hast thou honoured me (זבחיך) with thy sacrifices, with thy peace-offerings. I have not caused, etc. I have not asked thee to serve me with oblations.
Nor wearied thee with incense, to buy incense for me.
קנה בשם═קנה Sweet cane (Shemot 30:23).
וחלב זבחיך And with the fat of thy sacrifices, of thy sin offerings. Supply the preposition ב with before חלב fat; comp. בששת═ששת in six (Shemot 20:11).

But thou hast made me to serve. This is an anthropomorphism. Through thy sins I was considered by the nations as a slave that has no authority; the same idea is contained in the words which follow: Thou hast wearied me, etc.
For my sake, that my name be not profaned, I shall blot out thy transgressions.
Put me in remembrance, etc. If thou reply that thou hast not sinned against me while being in thy land, and yet I have cast thee out, then put me in remembrance.
נשפטה Let us plead together. Let us be ready for judgment.
Declare thou thy cause, that thou mayest be justified.
Thy first father hath sinned. Yerovam, when chosen by Bnei Yisrael, to be their king, without the consent of Hashem.

ומליציך And thy interpreters. Either the princes, the interpreters of the king, are meant, or the Leviyim, the interpreters of the priests. Some explain אביך by thy teachers. Comp. Melachim II 12:13; Bereshit 4:21; 45:8, and מליציך by thy pupils. As to מליץ interpreter, comp. Bereshit 42:23
The princes of the sanctuary. The priests; comp. Divrei Hayamim I 24:5
Yet now hear, etc. This evil I have brought upon thee for thy wickedness,
but now hear the good which I shall do unto thee.

From the womb. With this expression the prophet alludes to Yaakov (comp. Hoshea 12:4; in my commentary thereon I shall explain it), or metaphorically to the time, when Yisrael was declared to be the people of Hashem.
ישרון Jesurun. It is originally an adjective derived from ישר right; there is no other instance of this form.

For I will pour water, etc. As I pour water over the place that is thirsty, so will I pour out the spirit of my holiness, or of my salvation, etc. אֶצּׁק I will pour out. The Dagesh in צ compensates for the י which is omitted; comp. אצרך I shall form thee (Yirmiyahu 1:5)

And they shall spring up. The pronoun they refers to My spirit, and My blessing, of the preceding verse; according to others to thine offspring. בבין חציר Like grass. Lit., between the grass, that is, as if they were between grass. They will increase and multiply.
One shall say, etc. They will be numerous, and the majority of them will be faithful to Hashem, and desirous of returning to His house.
And another shall call himself by the name of Yaakov, in order to show to all nations, how proud he is of belonging to the holy people.
בידו═ידו With his hand. And another shall subscribe unto Hashem, that he is willing to go to the sanctuary of Hashem.

יכנה He will surname himself.—Many refer this verse to proselytes; comp. Ten men shall take hold, out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Yehudi, saying, We will go with you; for we have heard that God is with you (Zec. 8:23)
The King of Yisrael, When Bnei Yisrael were in their own land. And his redeemer, when he is in exile.
Hashem of hosts. He is always king, and the hosts of heaven testify it.
I am the first, the first king.
And who is like me, that is, Who pretends to be like me.
יקרא Shall lift up his voice.
And shall declare it, namely all that has passed.
עם עולם The ancient people. עולם means here of old.
ואתיות And the things that are coming. It is like a perfect verb. למו For themselves, that is, in order to show that they know it.
אל תרהו Be ye not afraid, תרהו is hap. leg; those that identify it with תראו are wrong, on account of the absence of the radical י —
Be not afraid, when those calamities befall Bavel.

Have I not told thee of it long ago? Ye are even my witnesses, and you will see whether there is a God beside me; There is no God בל ירעתי whom I know not to be vain and powerless. According to some, whom I chastised not; comp. ויודע and he chastised (Jud. 8:16). I think that the prophet speaks here of the host of heaven.
They that make a graven image, are all of them vanity. They themselves as well as their images are vanity.
וחמוריהם And their delectable things. The objects which they ornament with figures, that they be charming to the eye, namely the idols.
And they are their witnesses, to testify that the images see not, nor know.
That they may be ashamed. Connect this phrase with they are their witnesses.
Who hath formed, etc. Is there any thoughtlessness like this, to attempt to form a god? God. So called in the sense of him who formed the image.
נסך He hath molten. Comp. מסכה molten (Yirmiyahu 7:5)
His fellows. The priests of Ba'al, or the artificers of the idols; the latter explanation is the better.
Let them all be gathered together and be ashamed.
חָרַשׁ Smith. In the construct state the ר has Pathah, in the absolute it has Kamez, without exception.
מעצר A cutting instrument of iron.
מקבות Borer. An instrument used for making a hole.
יצרהו He fashioneth it. Comp. צורה form, or, what is still better, יצירה formation.
He is hungry. The smith is hungry.
The carpenter, etc. After having mentioned the mason and smith, he speaks of the carpenter.
The carpenter stretches out his rule, etc. This is just the mode of proceeding of those workmen.
יתארהו He forms it or he draws the outlines; comp. ותאר הגבול and the border was drawn (Jos. 15:9).
שרד A kind of drug used for dying. The word is hap. leg. יעשהו He finisheth it.
מקצעות Rulers. This is the opinion of R. Yonah.
מחוגה Compass. Comp. חוג circle (40:22). It is an instrument used for drawing a circle.
According to the beauty of a man, that is, the female, according to the opinion of some ; but I think that it is in reality only a repetition of the preceding idea.
לשבת בית That it may remain in the house. That it be like a man, who dwells in his house.
He heweth him down cedars, etc. Some cut the idols out of cedar wood, others of. תרזה cypress. It is the name of a tree.
ויאמץ לו And he planted it.
אורן It is either the name of a tree, or it means root.
וגשם And the stem. Lit., the substance comp. גשמא in Chaldee, and in Arabic <ara/> body. According to others: rain ; the meaning of וגשם יגדל is then, and the rain will cause it to grow.

לבער To bum. Then shall it be for a man, etc. Some warm themselves by the fire, others kindle it, etc. ישיק He kindleth it. Comp. נשקה was kindled (Ps. Ixxviii. 21); the meaning of נשק is similar to that of בער to burn.
ויסגד And falleth down. This word is frequently met with in Arabic and Chaldaic.
האח Aha. Interjection of joy; comp. Tehillim 35:21.
אור Fire, Comp. 31:9.
ראיתי I have seen. It is to be taken literally. R. Saadiah explains it I enjoyed, but he has no parallel instance to support his rendering.
A god according to his idea.
His image. This is the explanation of the expression a god which precedes.

לא ידעו ולא יבינו They have not known nor understood. The seat of knowledge (רעת) is in those cavities of the brain that are nearer to the forehead; the understanding (בינה) is in the middle one, that is also in the middle of the head.
טח He hath shut. Comp. וטח and he shall plaister (Lev, 14:42); it is a transitive verb; Hashem is understood as the subject to it.
עיניהם Their eyes. The eye of each of them; this construction is not at all rare.
His heart. His intellect, which is the principal part of man.
במו=ב In. Comp. כמו=כ as (Tehillim 58:10).
ויתרו And the residue thereof.
בול It is hap. leg. It means, according to some authorities, an image, or a statue. R. Moshe Hakkohen compares it with בול plant (Iyov 40:20).
He feedeth on ashes. He is like a man who feedeth on ashes, that hurt and do no good. It may also be compared with Efraim feedeth on wind (Hoshea 12:2).
הותל Foolish. It is an adjective; the form of adjectives is not constant. The form of הותל is like that of מועדת out of joint (Prov.xxv. 19).
לב הותל הטהו A foolish heart hath turned him aside.
The verb הטה is always used in an unfavorable sense: to turn from the right way. As to the phrase אחרי רבים להטות (Shemot 23:2) I have given my opinion.
Remember these, those which I have done, when thou wast in thy land.
For thou art my servant. Since thou hast been my servant, confess thy former sins; I am desirous to keep thee as my servant.
אתה Thou. Thou alone.
תנשני is Niphal, and I think that the meaning of לא תנשני is: Thou shalt not be forgotten of me. The meaning of the verse is: Remember me, and I will remember thee.
As a thick cloud, that passeth away; when the sun comes out, it is no more.

Sing, 0 ye heavens, etc. This is a figurative expression ; it means: great rejoicing will be through Yisrael, for through the redemption of Yisrael the glory of Hashem will be revealed to the whole world.
That maketh all things, which I desire; you may infer it from the fact, that I, by myself, stretch forth the heaven.

מאתי By myself. Lit., from myself, that is, by my strength; for Hashem is incorporeal. It is written in two words, מי אתי. who is with me, which is the same as I alone. Consider well the words of the text: who stretcheth forth the heavens and spreadeth abroad the earth ; they teach us that it is Hashem who is continually keeping heaven and earth in existence.

בדים Liars. Comp. בדיך thy lies (Iyov 11:3). More probably בדים is connected with בדד alone, and signifies such, persons as pretend to be able to emancipate their souls from, the influence of the body, which some in reality can do.
וקוסמים And astrologers. Lit., men that decide by reason, and say that and that will happen; while בדים foretell the future not by reasonable means.
Wise men. Persons, who divine from the liver or shoulder, and soothsayers.
His servant. The prophet himself. The word of his servant, that Yerushalayim shall be inhabited.
תושב Thou shalt be inhabited. Root ישב to dwell. Comp. תורד thou shalt be brought down (14:15) from ירד to go down.
Her decayed places. The decayed places of every city, or of Yerushalayim.
מצולה═צולה (Yonah 2:4) The deep. A figurative expression, signifying Bavel, that was full of men and wealth like the deep of the sea.

That saith to Koresh, etc. This verse proves that Yerushalayim was built in the days of Koresh; the words thy foundation shall be laid contain an allusion to the fact, that Koresh ordered the temple to be built, but after its foundation had been laid by Zerubavel, prohibited its further restoration; it is therefore clear, that Daniel made no mistake in his calculations, as I have already explained.
His anointed. According to some, the prophet; others think that Koresh is meant; either explanation is admissible; comp. Hashem hath anointed me (61:1), and Anoint Chazael to be king (1 K. 19:15).
לרד To subdue. It is infinitive of רדד ; comp. הרדד who subdueth (Tehillim 144:2); as to its form comp. לְעַד to prey (Tzefanyah 3:8)
I. The support of Hashem or the heavenly prince of Paras is to be understood; comp. Daniel 10:20.
והדורים The crooked places. It is the opposite of ישר straight. Some derive it from הדר glory; it means mountains, and is as to its form either adjective or participle passive.
דלתות The doors that are in the gates of the city.
And I will give thee the treasures of darkness. Koresh will take the spoil of the countries.
That thou mayest know. For before that he did not fear Hashem.
For Yaakov my servant’s sake, etc. All this success is not granted to thee for thine own sake, but for Yisrael, that thou shouldst send back the captives of Yisrael and rebuild Yerushalayim.
I have named thee. Comp. I have called thee by thy name, thou art mine (43:1)
I am Hashem, I alone know what will happen in future; as the victory of Koresh shows.
I shall gird thee. I shall strengthen thee, although thou hast not worshipped Me.
That they may know, etc. I have besides given thee strength, in order that My name shall be known everywhere, that I am alone the Lord, and that there is none beside Me.
I form the light, etc. Things which are opposite to each other are mentioned in this verse.
ובורא חשך And causeth darkness. ברא has here the same meaning as גזר to decree; for darkness is nothing by itself, it is but the absence of light.

The same is to be said concerning ובורא רע And causeth evil. By evil war is meant as the opposite of peace, or the sickness under which man labours, as being at war with his constitution. These antitheses are used to indicate that in the same way God will strengthen Koresh and weaken the king of Bavel.
Drop down. This is a command to the angels that they shall drop righteousness, and cause salvation and truth to succeed.
אני יי בראתיו I, Hashem, have created for him, have created righteousness for Koresh; he will establish righteousness in the world.
הוי Hi! Interjectio vocandi. The prophet calls unto him, that does not believe in the words of Hashem, who foretells these future events.
רב את יוצר That striveth with his maker. יוצר has here the same meaning as in Tehillim 2:9; namely potter.
The potsherd. The man who is like a potsherd of earthenware.
Shall the clay say to him that fashioneth it, What makest thou? This cannot be ; but he who fashions the clay does what he wishes.

ופעלך אין ידים לו Or thy work, etc. Or shall the clay say to him who fashions it, What thou doest is not done by thy hands. I think that this phrase contains the same idea as the preceding, namely : Thy work is made without hands; thou hast no power to do it as thou likest.

He that saith to his father, etc. Or can the son before his birth say to his father, What wilt thou beget, or to the woman, that is, to his mother, what wilt thou bring forth? תחילין Thou will bring forth. Comp. כי חלה נם ילדה ציון Tziyon travailed, she brought forth (66:8)
And his maker. I am he who made Yisrael.
שְׁאׇלוּגׅי Ask me. It is imperative like שְׁמׇלוּגׅי hear me (Bereshit 23:8), the kamez being substituted for zeré because of the guttural letter (א) .

,mubhWill ye command me. It is a question.—As the potter knows what to do with the clay, so I know what to do with Yisrael, who is my son. The other nations, the Non-Israelites are addressed in these words.

I have made the earth, etc. How will you command me concerning my children, when the whole universe belongs to me? I have created earth and man upon it; my hands have stretched out the heavens, and all their hosts have I commanded, and consequently they were created. I commanded is poetically said for I spoke as in the verse He commanded and they were created (Tehillim 148:5)
I have raised him, namely Koresh.
And I will make straight all his ways, and all this only because He shall build, etc.

The labour of Mitzrayim, etc. This verse shows that Koresh was also to conquer Mitzrayim, and to carry the inhabitants thereof away into captivity; the way, as is well known, led through. Palestine, which is situated in the midst between Eilam and Mitzrayim.
Men of measure. Men of great measure; for all men have a certain measure; comp. show thyself a man═show thyself a brave man (Melachim I 2:2).
Surely God is in thee. These are the words which they will confess and declare; this was in fact the case after the return of Yisrael from the Babylonian captivity.

Verily thou art a Elokim, etc. Then they will confess to Elokim and say, It is true that thou art Elokim who hid himself from the people in which He delighted, and now thou art the Elokim of Bnei Yisrael, who helps them. Some say that אל נסתר ═ אל מסתתר invisible Elokim, and explain the verse thus: Elokim, though invisible, revealed himself for the sake of Yisrael. This explanation, however, is not supported by the rules of Hebrew grammar, מסתתר being Hithpael, and signifying who hid himself.

They shall go with confusion, etc. They that make the idols, and come with honour to those that send for them, shall go, etc. צירים Messengers. Comp. ציר an ambassador (Yirmiyahu 49:14). הלכו They shall go. They shall return to their land.
Yisrael is saved by Hashem. Therefore they will not be ashamed, as those men have been put to shame, that made vain things which cannot help in times of trouble.
עד Innumerable.
He hath established it, as the habitation for men and beasts.
תהו In vain.

I have not spoken, etc. I have not made the earth in vain, how then should I say to Bnei Yisrael Seek ye me in vain. Many refer this verse to the revelation on Sinai; but I refer it to those future events, of which the Lord informed the prophet, and which the prophet announced to Yisrael and all other nations ; this may be gathered from the words מגיד מישרים I declare things that are right.
הקבצו ובאו התנגשו Assemble yourselves and come, draw near. These are imperatives.
Ye, that are escaped, etc. The Babylonians are addressed.—I called thus long ago, but they have, no knowledge that set up, etc.
Tell ye the truth.
And bring near your wise men.
יועצו Let them take counsel. It is Niphal of יעץ
And be ye saved. This is the same as and you will be saved; it is in your own power.
By myself, who am eternal. I have sworn. I have made a decree, which will not be undone.
דבר צדקה ═ צדקה a righteous word. Comp. צדקה she hath been righteous (Bereshit 38:27).

That unto me, etc. These things here foretold I shall do, till unto me every knee shall bow and every tongue shall swear to belong to me. לי unto me must be repeated before תשבע shall swear ; it is an ellipsis, such as is frequently met with. Comp. And shall swear by His name (Devarim 6:13)

לי Unto me. The pronoun of the first person refers to the prophet. He declares, that he does not know these future events by the aid of his reason, but by Hashem alone, who informed him of these things of righteousness and strength. It is more correct to explain the verse thus : Surely in Hashem, alone is righteousness and strength, the words לי אמר are a relative sentence signifying who spoke unto me.
עדיו To Him. Comp. Am. 4:6
In Hashem. In faithfully believing in Hashem.
Bel. The idol of the Babylonians; the same is the case with Nevo. The latter is explained by some to signify the sun.
קורס It is connected with קרסים taches (Shemot 26:11); its meaning is well known.
Upon the beasts and upon the cattle, upon which man is carried. This sentence is therefore followed by the words
נשאתיכם עמוסות משא לעיפה the beasts which carry you were heavy loaden; you are a burden to the weary beast. עיפה is an adjective, and refers to the beast that carries the burden.
They bow down. The beasts that carry the idols, bow down.

The burden. Their idols. נפשם Their souls, that is, the persons carried by the beasts, are gone into captivity. They were also carried away as captives. Others explain the verse thus : They, that is, all the idols that are left in Bavel, and are not yet mentioned, stoop and bow down, and cannot deliver the burden, for they must go themselves into captivity.
Which are borne by me, etc. The idols of Bavel are carried by their worshippers, but I, the Elokim of Yisrael, carry Bnei Yisrael.
From the belly, that is, since the day they were born.
And even to old age, etc. This is a figurative expression; it means since the day they had become the people of Hashem for ever.
I have made Bnei Yisrael; I am, therefore, not like the gods of Bavel; the Babylonians make their gods. And I will carry and deliver Bnei Yisrael; while the idols cannot deliver the burden.
And make me equal, that we two should be similar.—This verse is addressed to the idolaters.

הולים They lavish gold, etc. Many compare this word with אזל is spent (Shmuel I 9:7), and assume here the elision of the first radical (א) ; but it is in fact hap. leg.; for אזל is intransitive. הזלים means who give. מכיס Out of the bag. The bag is a part of the balance; comp. בכיסך in thy bag (Devarim 25:13). The succeeding בקנה has a similar meaning; it is hap. leg.
תחתיו In his place.
לא ימיש It shall not move itself. ימיש is a transitive verb. It may also be explained to be a neuter verb meaning it shall move, but the former explanation is better.
The word יצעק One shall cry is to be repeated after ומצרתו and out of his trouble.

והתאששו According to some And be founded ; comp. אשיותיה her foundations (Yirmiyahu 1. 15) and אושיא walls (Ezr. 4:12). R. Hai deriving it from אש fire explains והתאוששו be burnt. R. Saadiah derives it also from אֵשׁ, but explains it: be flamed; comp. this word was in mine heart as a burning fire (Yirmiyahu 20:9). Bring again to mind this thing.
ראשנות The former things. The things that have passed ; the word מעולם of old is therefore added. I am God. Thus you shall know that I alone am God.
Declaring the end from the beginning, that is, declaring the event before it happens; for who can annul my decree; my counsel stands for ever, and I will do all my pleasure.
A ravenous bird. Koresh. He is called a bird, because he flew, as it were, to fulfil my will.
I have spoken this decree. אביאנה I will also bring it to pass. יצרתיה I have formed it by a heavenly decree, I will also do it on earth.
Stouthearted, that do not believe in the word of Hashem, but are hardened in their hearts.
I bring near my righteousness, to show it, and therefore It shall not be, etc.
לא תאחר Shall not tarry. Literally : shall not stay itself with me too long before coming, for תאחר is a transitive verb. It is a figurative expression.

ונתתי And I will place is to be repeated before לישראל. The phrase תפארתי לישראל is therefore to be rendered thus : And I will place my glory in Yisrael. It may also be explained thus : to Yisrael, who is my glory; comp. in whom I will be glorified (49:3); the latter explanation is the better.
Virgin. Bavel is like a virgin, that has not yet been deflowered.
בת Daughter. It is here figuratively used for people.
There is no throne for thee any longer.
ענוגה Tender. It is an adjective similar in form to אדומה red (Bamidbar 19:2)
Take the millstones, etc., as handmaids do; for thou wilt go into captivity.
Meal. This is a prolepsis. Comp. And stripped the naked of their clothing (Iyov 22:6).
צמתך Thy crown. The hair upon the head.

שובל Locks. The hair that hangs down over the cheeks. R. Moshe Hakkohen compares שובל with שבלת the channel of the river (27:12), but I consider it as hap. leg., and its meaning can only be found from the context, without being supported by any. parallel passage.
Pass over the rivers, in order to grind.
תגל Shall be uncovered. It is Niphal of גלה .

ולא אפגע אדם And I shall not accept the intercession of any man. פגע means to entreat; comp. אל תפגעי בי entreat me not (Rut 1:16); when פגע is constructed with the preposition ב, then the noun, to which the ב is prefixed, is the object to the verb. Some render the meaning of this sentence in the following way: I shall not take vengeance on thee, and I shall not meet a man (comp. ויפגעו and they met, Shemot 5:20) sc. standing in my way, or telling me not to do it, or I shall not meet a man, whom 1 should not cause joy by this.
Our redeemer, etc. Then Bnei Yisrael will say, this is our redeemer, etc.
יקראו לך Thou shalt be called. Lit. They, the people, will call thee. Comp. Bamidbar 26:59; there are many other instances like it.
I was wroth, etc. When I was angry with my people, thou didst not show mercy to them, etc.
The ancient is especially mentioned because of the failure of his strength and because of the regard due to him.
And thou saidst, in thy heart, etc.;
but thou ought to have taken to thy heart These things, which I have done for my people.
Neither didst thou remember the latter end of it. That is, the latter end of the pride; or thou didst not remember what the future of my peculiar people was to be, when I was angry with them.
עדינה Given to pleasures. It is an adjective; עדנה pleasure (Bereshit 18:12) is of the same root.
אפס═אפסי None, The י is paragogic; comp. מן═מני from (Shoftim 5:14).
A widow. The king of the country is metaphorically called the husband.
שכל The loss of children. It is a noun similar in form to כפר hoar-frost (Shemot 16:14); שפט judgment (Divrei Hayamim II 20:9)
These two. The loss of the kingdom and the death of the children.
כתמם In their perfection. When the evils were complete. תמם is an infinitive.—All these evils came over thee for the multitude of thy sorceries, etc.
And thy knowledge. The prophet here alludes to that rationalism which denies the existence of Hashem.
רוֹאׇגׅי Seeth me. The א has Kamez, because it is a guttural letter.
Thy wisdom. That which was wisdom in thy imagination.
שובבתך Hath perverted thee, has made thee obstinate, that thou art not inclined to return from thy evil way.
ואפסי And none. It has here the same meaning as above (ver. 8). I am, and none else beside me, I am wise, and there is none as wise as I am.
יום רעה═רעה A day of evil.
לא תדעי שחרה Thou shalt not know its light. It will be like a night, which is not relieved by daylight; שחר means light.

הׂוׇה Mischief. It is derived from הוה to become; comp. ואתה הוה that thou mayest become (Nechemyah 6:6); it signifies an evil that comes suddenly; of the same root is והותי and my calamity (Iyov 6:2).
כפרה To put it off by ransom; comp. כפר ransom (Shemot 30:12); or to annul it; comp. יכפרנה will remove it (Mishlei 16:14).
שואה Desolation.
נא Now.
בחבריך With thine enchantments. It is a plural noun, of the same root as וחבר חבר or a charmer (Devarim 18:11).
הועיל To profit. It is Infinitive.
תערוצי Thou mayest prevail. Comp. עריץ strong (29:20)
עֲצׇתׇיׅךְ Thy counsels. It is an irregular form, a combination of the singular and plural; comp. מֲכּׂתְךְ thy plagues (Devarim 28:59), which shows the same peculiarity in the opposite order.

הברי שמים Astrologers. Some derive הברי from ברר to be clear, because the astrologers cannot know the exact time unless the heaven be clear and cloudless. This is far-fetched ; besides, the ה is radical, and the word is in form similar to שמרי watchmen of (Shir Hashirim 5:7).

מודיעים לחדשים The monthly prognosticators. This is their wisdom; they look to the stars for the knowledge of changes in the weather, and of events concerning the countries, only at the time of the conjunction of the planets, which is the source of their wisdom, and is here indicated by the word מאשר יבאו עליך .לחרשים

From these things that shall come upon thee. This phrase is not to be joined with מודיעים לחדשים, but with ויושעוך and save thee, though distant from it; comp. אשד עבדו שם הגוים אשר אתם יורשים אותם את אלהיהם wherein the nations which ye shall possess, served their gods (Devarim 12:2)
Fire. The host of the enemy. Comp., There is a fire gone out of Cheshbon (Bamidbar 21:28).

לחמם To warm at. It is infinitive of a verb (חמם) ע״ע, written in full, and similar in form to לשכב to lie (Bereshit 34:7).—The meaning of the whole sentence is: they will perish and no remnant will be left of them.
Thus were they, those wise men.
With whom thou hast laboured. To whom thou hast given money.
Even thy merchants, which were not from thy land, but had been thy friends.—When thy fall cometh, they all forsake thee.
Out of the waters of Yehudah. That is, out of the seed of Yehudah. Comp. The fountains of Yaakov (Devarim 33:28).
Not in truth. They utter with their lips that they are Hashem’s people, but do not think so in their hearts nor show it in their deeds.
For they call themselves of the holy city, namely children of Tziyon.
And stay themselves upon the God of Yisrael with their lips.
I have declared, etc. Hashem will say to the unbelievers, Have I not often foretold you coming events before they happened (ראשנות)? The past tense is therefore used : and they came to pass.

מדעתי I know. As I knew the former things, so I know also that thou art hardened in thy heart. The second person refers to those Bnei Yisrael who do not believe in God. And thy neck is of iron. Thou dost not depart from thy way, as if thy neck were of iron. And thy brow brass. And thou dost not blush, as if thy forehead were brass.

I have even from the beginning, etc. This is the explanation; I foretold thee coming events, in order that thou shouldst not say when they happened, that thy idols worshipped by thee in thy land had prepared them, that by their decree the events took place,
Hath commanded them. It is the same expression as used of the Almighty (45:12)
Thou hast heard, see all this. What thou hast heard, all has come.
And will not ye declare that this is the case? Behold, I have shewed thee new things from this time,
even hidden things, that are kept (בצורות═נצורות) with the Omniscient alone.
נבראו They are decreed.

And before the day, on which I told you. ולא שמעתם Thou heardest them not. The ו introduces the principal sentence, as فَ in Arabic; comp. אברהם ביום השלישי וישא when the third day came, Avraham lifted up (Bereshit 22:4)

Yea, thou knowest not, etc., I knew, etc. That is, I know it for certain, that thou hast not heard of it, or I knew it, that thou wouldst not listen, that thou wouldst be treacherous against me, and not believe in my words.

From the womb. I knew thee since thou camest to existence. In the opposite sense this expression is used in Yirmiyahu 1:5: Before I formed thee in the belly, I knew thee. And thou wast called a transgressor from the womb. This refers to the decrees of the Almighty. I shall fully explain this subject in my commentary on the book of Yirmiyahu.
פתחה Hath opened itself; it is an elliptical expression.
For My name’s sake, Yisrael is called the people of Hashem.

אחטם Wrath, It is hap. leg.; comp. אף═חטם nose in Rabbinical Literature. Supply אאריך before אחטם : I will defer my wrath; also למען for the sake of is to be repeated before תהלתי : and for the sake of my praise.
I have refined thee, by the exile.
במצרף כסף═בכסף In the silver refinery, I have refined thee, by taking away the dross, that is, the wicked.

בחרתיך I have chosen for thee, Some say that בחנתיך═בחרתיך I have tried thee; in that sense the word is hap. leg. I take it in its usual meaning, I have chosen for thee to refine thee in the furnace of affliction, not in the silver refinery.

יחל Should be polluted. It is the Niphal of a verb (חלל) ע״ע; as to the use of the first person in למעני and third person in יחל, comp. ונשאר אני and I was left (Ez. 9:8); הנני יוסיף behold, I will add (38:5).
מקראי Called by me. They are called the children of Hashem. You ought to believe that Hashem is the first and last; this would be a true belief, for my hand, etc.
ידי Mine hand. My left hand.
It is a figurative expression; the right hand is used in connection with the heavens, because they are higher in rank than the earth.
אף has in this verse the same meaning as כי for.—It is true that I am the first and last, because I created every thing.

טפחה Hath put round, Comp. טפחתי I have swaddled (Eichah 2:22). Others explain it: Hath measured with the handbreadth יעמדו יחדיו —.(טֶפַח) They stand up together. From this phrase some of the commentators derive their opinion, that heaven and earth were created simultaneously, not consecutively. The literal meaning, however, is: I have made them, and when I call them to do My will and desire they stand both before Me like servants; comp. למשפטיך עמדו they stand up according to Thy ordinances (Tehillim 119:91). For else how should Hashem call them, when not yet existing.
These. The coming events.
Hath loved him, namely Koresh.

His pleasure. The pleasure of Hashem. Koresh will perform the will of Hashem concerning Bavel, and show His arm against the Chaldæans. It is, however, also possible, that the possessive pronoun his (ו) in his pleasure and his arm refers to Koresh.
I, even I. The word I is repeated to express the idea: I who am always the same.
I have called him, namely Koresh.
Come ye near unto me, unto the prophet.
I have not spoken in secret from the beginning of this plan and this divine decree.

From the time that it was, there was I. The Gaon finds here an indication that the soul exists before the body; but he is wrong, because it is said, They are decreed now, and not from the beginning (ver. 7). The meaning of the sentence is the following: When this decree was made by Hashem unto the angels, the representatives of the respective countries (comp. Daniel 10:20), I was also there.
ורוחו And His spirit, that is His angel. The Gaon says, that ברוחו═ורוחו by His spirit; comp. דרשו יי ועזו seek Hashem in His strength ; but there is no necessity to assume that.
Thy redeemer, etc. The words which follow are to announce the reward of those that listen to the words of Hashem.
לוא Oh that. The א is paragogic; comp. ההלכוא that went (Jos. 10:24).
ויהי Then had been. The ו has here the same meaning as فَ in Arabic. Thy peace had been as a river, that does not cease to flow.
And thy righteousness, etc. And thy righteousness had been continuous as the waves of the sea.
Thy seed. The number of thy children.
בטנך═מעיך Thy womb.
כמעותיו As its bowels. The possessive pronoun refers to the sea, the waves and sand of which have just been mentioned (ver. 18 and 19); by the bowels of the sea the roe of the fish is meant.
His name. The name of thy seed.
Go ye forth, etc. Now the prophet addresses those in exile.

Utter it, etc. Make it known publicly; not alone that He will redeem His people, He will do wonders to them at their return to Tziyon. ולא צמאו That they will not thirst in the deserts, through which Hashem will lead them.
Out of the rock. Where no water had been before.
ויזבו And gushed out. Comp. זב running (Vayikra 15:2)

There is no peace unto the wicked, that is, unto the wicked of Yisrael, as some explain, or unto the Babylonians; for this blessing shall be for Yisrael alone, but there shall be no peace for the Babylonians.
Unto me, that is unto the prophet.
From far. That live far away; or things that will happen in remote future.
Hath called me from the birth, I shall explain this in the commentary on Yirmiyahu 1:2.

And He hath made my mouth like a sharp sword, to speak elegantly; or, as was the case in his prophecies against Bavel, to speak sharply; and the meaning of the whole phrase is accordingly : Although Hashem has made my mouth like a sharp sword against the Babylonians, neither the Babylonians nor the wicked men in Yisrael, could do any harm to me,
because God hath hid me in the shadow of His hand, which is to the prophet as the sheath to the sword; comp. in His quiver hath he hid me.
ברור Polished, when seen.
And said. And Hashem said. ישראל
Yisrael. That is, Thou art a Yisraeli of whom I am proud; or Thou art Yisrael, thou art estimated in mine eyes like all Bnei Yisrael together. I prefer this latter explanation.
Then I said. Then I, the prophet, said.
I said to myself,
I have laboured in vain. I have troubled myself in vain to rebuke Yisrael; they do not hearken.
My judgment is with Hashem. He will reward me for my trouble. ופעלתי And my wages. Comp. שביר פעלת the wages of one that is hired (Vayikra 19:13)
That formed me, etc. Hashem formed me, that I should rebuke Yisrael, till they returned to Him.

לא Unto him. The original reading is לו unto him, as the Masorah recommends; comp. Tehillim 100:5; there are some more instances of the same kind. According to the Gaon, the meaning of לא יאסף is: Will not die; he generally explains both the Keri and the Ketib; but what I said, is nevertheless right, and לא of the text is the same as לו, as the Grammarian R. Jehudah explained.
It is a slight thing, in mine eyes, that thou shouldst be a servant to bring Yisrael back to their land by thy word.
ונצורי And the ruins of. Comp. נצורה desolate (1:8).—
Not alone wilt thou bring Yisrael back, but I will give thee for a light of nations.
להיות ישועתי. That my salvation may be, that is, that my salvation maybe published before it comes, unto the end of the earth
Thus saith Hashem, etc. The prophet continues to speak of himself: Thus says Hashem unto me, who am despised of the wicked men. לבזה To him who is despised. בזה is an adjective.
מתעב It is either a causative verb, meaning: causing to abhor, that is, saying things, for which the nations abhor him; or a transitive verb: abhorring, that is, abhorring all idolaters.
To a servant of rulers, that is of the nobles of Yisrael, as they consider themselves, or of the Babylonians. The latter rendering is preferable.

Kings shall see and arise. I have already alluded to the inference that may be drawn from those words (40:1). Most of the commentators explain this sentence thus: Kings, like Koresh, will rise and worship, when they hear the words of the prophet.
Because of Hashem. For He remains faithful to His word.—
The suffix ך in ויבחרך and He chose thee, shows that this explanation is right.

בעת רצון עניתיך In an acceptable time I have heard thee. This expression is likewise a proof of the correctness of my opinion. Many, in opposition to the context, refer the pronoun thee to Koresh. R. Moshe thinks that the preposition ב in בעת רצון has the same meaning as in במרחב יה (Tehillim 118:5), namely: with. It is not at all unlikely that his opinion is right.
That thou mayest say, etc. This shows that the prophet announced this to the Yehudim before they returned from the Babylonian exile.
And their pastures in all high places. And they shall find their pastures, etc.
They will not, etc. When they return to Tziyon.
שרב Heat. Comp. 35:7. Nor the sun smite them. Comp. The sun shall not smite thee by day (Tehillim 121:6)
And I will make all my mountains a way, etc. The mountains will be lowered, and the paths which are low will be exalted.

As to the use of the masculine plural ירומון, together with the feminine מסלות, comp. תמצאו ye (daughters of Yerushalayim) find (Shir Hashirim 5:8). The origin of the seeming irregularity is to be found in the indifference of the Hebrews as to the use of the plural masculine for the feminine, so long as the idea of plurality is clearly expressed. Others explain the verse thus: Those that will return, will be so numerous, that they will have to walk high on the mountains. According to their opinion ירמון means: they—that will return—will be high, as if the prophet said: they will walk high on my paths (ועל מסלתי)
From far, from the east.
From the north, from Bavel.
From the west. From Ashur. Comp. Ezr. 6:22.
מארץ סינים From the land of Sinim. A land near Mitzrayim. The name סינים is perhaps connected with סנה bush.

Sing, etc. This is a figurative expression; or the purity of the air is to be considered as the singing of the heavens, the productiveness of the fields and gardens as the singing of the earth, and the singing of the mountains can be explained in a similar way.
But Tziyon said before the redemption, that Hashem forgot her. Tziyon. The congregation of Yisrael.
Can a woman, etc. This is mentioned, because Hashem has given to woman a natural disposition to have pity on her children.
עולל═עול Sucking child. Comp. Yirmiyahu 6:11; Is. 65:20.
That she should not have compassion, etc. Repetition of the same idea.
גם אלח תשכחנה Yea, they may forget. There are cruel women, that forget their children or themselves; or there are women that forget these,
yet will I not forget thee. Her sucking child is mentioned, because the mother has usually more compassion for the little one that has no strength.

I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands. According to the Gaon, the clouds are meant by the palms of my hand; but I say it is an anthropomorphism, meaning: I shall see thee continually; the second part of the verse, the parallelism of which divides it into two similar halves, confirms the correctness of this explanation.
Thy children, etc. Thy children have come, and all thy destroyers shall go away from thee.

All of them. All of thy children. R. Moshe Hakkohen explains the expression thus: Thy children as well as thy destroyers, that is, the wicked, gathered themselves, etc. According to this explanation the future יֵצֵאוּ is used instead of the past יׇצׇאוּ. But it is not necessary to assume this irregularity here.
As I live. The decree shall not be annulled; as truly as I am living, it will be acted upon.
כקשורי כלה ═ ככלה As the ornament of the bride round her neck.

תחת חרבותיך ═ חרבותיך Instead of Thy waste places. Comp. פשעי for my transgressions (Michah 6:7); פרים instead of calves (Hoshea 14:31.) The verse can also be explained thus: They were thy waste places before, but now,
Thou shalt be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants, by reason of the multitude of inhabitants, all of whom are thy children; because they that swallowed them up, will be far away.
גשה לי Give place unto me. Lit. Go thither for my sake. Comp. גש הלאה stand back (Bereshit 19:9)
נלמודה Desolate. Remaining lonely; comp. גלמוד solitary (Iyov 3:7). It is an adjective, of a quadriliteral root.
וסורה And removing to and fro. It is an adjective, and not a participle passive; for סור to depart is a neuter verb.
איפה where. It is a compound of two words אי and פה

Behold, I will lift up My hand, etc. As a man lifts up his hand, that he may be seen. This phrase as well as that which follows: And set up my standard, are the same as I shall make known this my salvation.
And they shall bring thy sons. By they the Non-Israelites are to be understood.
בחוצן In their lap. Comp. חצני my lap (Nechemyah 5:13)
אומניך Thy nursing fathers. Comp. ויהי אמן and he brought up (Est. 2:7). It is a figurative expression for the great honour which will be shown to Yisrael.
Shall the prey, etc. These words are put into the mouth of Yisrael by the prophet. How is it possible, the people ask, that Yisrael should be delivered from the power of the heathen nations ?
המלקח The prey, which he has taken, that is, the captives.
ואם שבי צדיק ימלט Or shall the righteous captive be delivered, because of his righteousness, after having been taken by the mighty.
The captive of the mighty. The captive which the mighty man has taken, will be taken away from him.
עריץ The terrible. It is an adjective with transitive meaning: causing terror; comp. אימים (Bereshit 14:5).

Moreover, I will contend with him that contendeth with thee. I shall make war against those that attack thee. יריבך that contendeth with thee. Some derive it from ירב; others by metathesis from ריב; according to the Jerusalemite the relative אשר who must be supplied before יריבך, which he explains to be the third person singular masculine future of ריב; he overlooked, however, the parallel instance of יריבי that strive with me (Tehillim 35:1). In short it is an irregular form.

מוניך That oppress thee. Comp. ולא תגו ye shall not oppress (Vayikra 25:17). Others say that it means: thy numberers, comparing it with מונה that telleth (Yirmiyahu 33:13), because Yisrael is compared to a flock of sheep.
מדמם = דמם With their own blood. An ellipsis is as frequently found in poetry.
ספר כריתות Bill of divorcement.

Of your mother and her husband.—This verse seems to contradict the prophecy of Yirmiyahu, I had put her away and given her a bill of divorce (3:8); but in fact the latter refers to the kingdom of the ten tribes which will never again be established; comp. She shall no more rise (Am. 5:2); but Yeshayahu speaks of the kingdom of the house of David, which will be restored by Messiah.
Wherefore when I come, etc. This verse proves that already prophets have tried to make Yisrael return to the Lord.
Behold I dry up, etc. This proves that the power of God will not fail in redeeming Yisrael.

מלבוש קדרׂות ═ קדרות With black cloth, that is, with clouds. Some understand it to refer to an eclipse of the sun, when the sky becomes obscure in the middle of the day, and appears as if covered with sackcloth, which is usually black.
Hashem hath given me, etc. The first person refers to the prophet.
למודים Learning. It is an adjective; comp. למד מדבר used to the wilderness (Yirmiyahu 2:24); כלמדים as the pupils (at the end of this verse).

לדעת לעות את יעף דבר That I should know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary. The infinitive לעות is governed by לדעת to know; it is derived from עת time, or it is hap. leg. By him that is weary, the pupil is meant, who has a hard lesson to learn, of which he soon becomes tired and weary.
He wakeneth, etc. Hashem stirreth me up every morning; he stirreth up my ear that I may listen as pupils do; for I am a pupil of Hashem.
Hashem Hashem hath opened mine ear, etc. Since Hashem hath opened mine ear, and revealed His plan to me, I have not objected to be His messenger.
I gave my back, etc. I did not care that I had to expose my back to strokes for the sake of His name.
I shall not be ashamed. Hashem will fulfil all the words prophesied by me.
Near is, etc. Near is the time, when I shall appear as justified in my prophecies; then I shall say, Who will, etc.
Behold Hashem, etc. Since Hashem assists me, who will condemn me ? And all those that condemn me by their words, they will wax old as a garment. יבלו They shall wax old. They shall perish.
Who is amongst you, etc. The prophet now addresses those same people, that condemn him.

That walked in darkness, etc. The relative pronoun refers to ירא יי him that feareth Hashem. The meaning of the sentence is, Who is among you, etc., that does not run after material honours and pleasures; let him trust in Hashem, etc. According to others, the words that walketh in darkness, describe His servant, the prophet, and the meaning of the whole sentence is, Who is among you, etc., that is, there is none among you, that feareth Hashem, because you see the prophet obtaining no honours from the people. This is the right explanation, and it is confirmed by the words which follow.
זיקות Sparks. The meaning of the word must be found from the context. מאזרי Who compass yourselves.
This. This decree.

למעצבה תשכבון Ye shall lie down in sorrow. You shall die in sorrow. Comp. וישכב דוד and David slept, that is, and David died (Melachim I 2:10); there are, besides, a great many instances of the use of the verb שכב in this sense.
Hearken to me. The prophet speaks now to the good people, who believe in the words of the prophets.
Look, etc. Be not surprised how Tziyon can again be filled with her children as before, but look, etc.
Look unto the rock. Comp. Behold, I will stand before thee there upon the rock (Shemot 18:6).
Unto the rock. Unto the name of the rock, of which you are hewn; that is, unto the name of Avraham.
מקבת The hole. Comp. ויקב and bored (Melachim II 12:10).
To the hole of the pit, etc. Sarah is meant.

תחוללכם That bare you. According to R. Yonah, it is future, like ,תשובבכם instead of the past חוללתכם. R. Moshe Hakkohen believes it to be an adjective, although there is no other adjective of the same form.
וַאֲבׇרְכֵהוּ And blessed him. The ו has Pathah, because ואברכהו is future: it means, I told him that I should bless him; and so it was. In the same way.
Hashem shall comfort Tziyon, etc. Thus the connection of this verse with the preceding one is explained. He hath comforted all her waste places, by the multitude of her children, of her inhabitants.
Hearken unto me. The first person in this verse refers to Hashem.
A law. The word of God proclaimed by the prophet.
ארגיע I will make to rest. Comp. המרנעה the rest (28:12). One of the commentators explains it: I will do in a moment, without delay. The first explanation is better.
Is near, to be seen.
זרועי Mine arms, is the subject. עמים The people is the object. The isles shall wait upon me, etc., at that time.

Lift up your eyes, etc. Philosophers derive from this verse the doctrine of the immortality of the soul of man; their doctrine is right; but this verse certainly does not contain it. השמים The sky. הארץ The inhabited part of the earth. Both may perish, but the salvation of Hashem, His faithfulness, His righteousness remains for ever.
The reproach of men. The reproach of the Babylonians and the heathen peoples that have been brought to Bavel as captives.
סס The worm. It is hap. leg. But my righteousness shall be for ever. Comp. And His righteousness endureth for ever (Tehillim 112:8).
עורי Awake. The accent is on the last syllable; there are many instances of this exception.
Put on strength, O arm of the Lord. The strength is, like the garment, an ornament of the arm.
רהב Tyrant. Comp. רהבים tyrants (Tehillim 40:5; 87:4).
מחוללת Causing terror. Comp. חיל trembling (Shemot 15:14). He has caused terror by the miracles done in Mitzrayim.
The dragon. Paroh is meant; comp. I am against thee, Paroh, king of Mitzrayim, the great dragon, etc. (Ez. 29:3)
Which hath dried the sea. This refers to the division of the Red Sea. מי תהום רבה The waters of the great deep. Repeat הטחרבת which hath dried before these words.
השמה That hath made. It is in form similar to השבה that hath returned (Rut 2:6). The second part of the verse is a mere repetition of the idea contained in the first.

And the redeemed, etc. The connection between this and the preceding verses is: Awake, O arm, etc., and then, when this is the case, the redeemed of Hashem shall return. I have explained this already (35:10)
I am he that comforteth you. The pronouns I and you, refer to the prophet and the people respectively.
Thou. It is generally believed that Yisrael is here addressed; but I think, that the prophet speaks to his own soul, in a prophetical spirit; comp. And I have put my words in thy mouth (ver. 16).
כחציר═חציר As grass. Comp. אש אכלח as consuming fire (Devarim 4:24)
And forgottest. It is as if thou didst forget. The prophet, in his prophetical spirit, speaks thus to his own heart. The Lord thy Maker, who is omnipotent; for heaven and earth are in His power.
The oppressor. Comp. I gave my back to the smiters (50:6).
To destroy, that is, to kill men. And where is, etc. Where is now the fury of the oppressor.

צועה The captive exile. Comp. צועים oppressors. וצעוהו and they shall oppress them (Yirmiyahu 48:2). The literal meaning of the word, though a participle active, is bound; he who is oppressed, and is in distress, is, as it were, bound. This meaning of the word is proved by the words which follow: that he may be loosed.
And that he should not die. The prophet is meant.
Nor that his bread should fail, as was the case with Michayhu and Yirmiyahu, who received but scanty food (Melachim I 22:27; Jer. xxxvii.)

רגע Who stilleth. Some say that גער ═ רגע who rebuketh, by metathesis; others compare it with מרגוע rest (Yirmiyahu 6:17), and render it who giveth rest; I approve of this latter explanation. ויהמו גליו Whose waves roared, that is, whose waves have been roaring. The meaning of the verse might also be the following: I am he who stilleth the sea, but I am also he who commandeth that its waves shall roar. Sea and waves are figurative expressions for the oppressors.
I have covered thee to protect thee against him, who was ready to destroy (ver. 13).
To plant the heavens. A figurative expression for the announcement to be made to the countries that they shall be restored to their former happiness.

ליסוד To lay the foundations. It is the infinitive; the radical י is silent, according to the rule; the word ליסוד is, however, in form similar to the perfect verb; comp. לישון to sleep (Kohelet 5:11)
Which hast drunk, etc. Yisrael is compared to a man that is drunk, and is not aware of what is done unto him; he lies down in deep sleep.
קבעת The dregs. It is hap. leg. Some explain it to signify the dregs that are fixed (קבע to fix) to the bottom of the vessel.
התרעלה Trembling. Comp. הרעלו they have been shaken (Nachum 2:4). The cup of trembling, that is, the cup, at the sight of which man trembles.
מצית Thou hast wrung out. Comp. תמצו you may milk out (66:11), though of a different conjugation. The meaning of this figure is, thou hast received the full measure of evil.
There is none to guide her. Yisrael is like a woman, that has none to guide her; Yisrael has no king nor judge, to be saved by him.
ינוד Shall be sorry. Comp. לנוד to mourn (Iyov 2:11). שתים וגוי

Two things, etc. Desolation and the sword are the same, for desolation accompanies the sword; destruction and famine are likewise the same; comp. בשברי לכם מטה לחם. and when I have broken the staff of your bread (Vayikra 26:26). Others explain שתים In pairs. The evils come unto thee in pairs.
במי═מי By whom. By whom shall I comfort thee ? Man is usually comforted by being told that some other man has met with the same accident.
עולפו Have fainted. Comp. ויתעלף and he fainted (Yonah 4:8).
They lie. They are killed by famine and sword.
תוא A bird. It is hap. leg. כתוא מכמר As the bird of the net, that is, the bird caught in a net. מכמר Net. Comp. מכמוריו their own nets (Tehillim 141:10).
The rebuke of thy God. This is the explanation of the preceding, the fury of the Lord.
Hear now, the prophecy which follows in the next verses.
ושכורת And drunken with. Supply חמה anger, אף wrath, or רעות evils.
יריב עמו He will plead the cause of His people. Comp. אלמנה ריב the cause of the widow (1:23)
מוגיך That afflict thee. Comp. יגון trouble. It is Hiphil of יגה. Comp. הוגה He hath afflicted (Eichah 1:12).
Bow down, that is, make thyself low, that we may go over thee.
And as the street, etc. Repetition of the same idea.

All agree that this prophecy has reference to the time yet to come, notwithstanding the passage Depart ye, etc. (ver. 11), which is adduced by R.
